News.title: Security minister insists survival campaign not launched due to 'imminent threat' to UK
News.content:
Security minister insists survival campaign not launched due to 'imminent threat' to UK

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said the deaths of two men this weekend were 'an all-too-grim reminder of the devastating impact that storms can have'

View 2 Images Storm Boelo battered the UK over the weekend, with two men killed by falling trees (Image: Getty Images)

The Security Minister has insisted a campaign to prepare Brits for an emergency or disaster has not been launched due to a "specific or imminent threat" to the UK.

‌



‌



Dan Jarvis told MPs the public awareness drive was about having "an honest conversation" with the public about the risks Britain faces.

‌



The government’s "Be Ready" campaign , which launched last week, urges Brits to keep a three-day supply of goods at home, including non-perishable food and bottled water. It also tells people to sign up to the Priority Services Register, a service that helps gas, water, and electricity companies identify customers that may need extra support in an emergency.

‌



Setting the plans out in the Commons, Mr Jarvis said Brits were just 13% of people think their household is largely or totally prepared for a disaster - which he said is far below our European neighbours.

He continued: "This government is committed to having an honest conversation with the public about the risks that we face and helping them to prepare, household by household, step by step, to improve our national resilience

View 2 Images Dan Jarvis defended a public awareness campaign on how to prepare for an emergency

‌



Military planes to fight wildfires and survival campaign launched - see kit list READ MORE :

Brits start to stockpile essential goods as UK retailers see rise in sales after government's emergency advice READ MORE :

"To that effect, we've published updated preparedness guidance for households and launched a three-year campaign to raise awareness of the simple steps people can take to be ready for everyday emergencies. I want to be clear from the outset that we are not launching this campaign because of any specific or imminent threat.

"Instead, launching this campaign brings the UK into line with almost every single European country and countless others around the world who already run similar campaigns every year."

‌



Defending the campaign, Mr Jarvis said the deaths of two men this weekend were “an all-too-grim reminder of the devastating impact that storms can have”. He also pointed to the thousands of people left without power as proof the campaign is necessary.

He told MPs: “I saw this firsthand when I visited Cornwall in the wake of Storm Goretti earlier this year. Weather stations recorded wind speeds of 100 miles an hour. 50,000 homes, schools, and businesses were left without power.

‌



"Entire communities became trapped as fallen trees blocked country lanes. I heard families' fear as they talked about how quickly the basic necessities of everyday life were stripped away: power, water, internet. And I thanked the first responders for their tireless effort clearing roads and reconnecting homes.

“Now, to people who think the campaign is an overreaction, think of the people that I met in Cornwall, and people in countless other communities across the UK, including tens of thousands of people who were without power this very weekend, whose lived experience proves otherwise.”

‌



Storm Boelo battered the UK over the weekend, with two men killed by falling trees. A man in his 20s was pronounced dead in north London after his car was hit by a tree. Another man, 60, also died in Dumfies and Galloway. According to the Energy Networks Association, more than 90,000 homes were without power on Sunday evening.

Elsewhere, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting warned Britain must be braced to go to war within 1,000 days due to Russia’s growing military capacity.

Article continues below

On Sunday, he said the UK has three years to improve its defences alongside NATO allies because adversaries will be ready to attack by 2030. The threat of "state-sponsored terrorism" by hostile countries that could target our infrastructure is ever-increasing, he added.

News.title: First picture of 'loving family man', 29, killed when tree crushed his car in Storm Boelo
News.content:
First picture of 'loving family man', 29, killed when tree crushed his car in Storm Boelo

The 29-year-old tech sales executive was killed when a tree came down on his car in Mill Hill, north London, during high winds from Storm Boelo.

View 3 Images

A 29-year-old man who died after a tree crushed his car during Storm Boelo has been named and pictured for the first time.

‌



‌



James Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road in Mill Hill, north London, when the tree came down in high winds at around 12.30pm on Sunday.

‌



Police officers, paramedics, firefighters and an air ambulance were called, but Mr Abiwon was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



His next of kin were informed and police are now working with the local authority and coroner to establish the exact circumstances surrounding his death.

His cousin Tyrrell Okolo described him as a "master of everything". He told the Metro: "He loved his family he was a massive family man.

View 3 Images Storm Boelo brought strong winds and dangerous conditions across parts of the UK. (Image: Duncan Bryceland/Shutterstock)

‌



"He was 'Business Development Representative of the Year' at his company. He was a semi-pro footballer with Aldershot. He also had a music career with 40,000 viewers on YouTube. He was a mentor to many."

Mr Abiwon, a tech sales executive who gained a degree from the University of Essex, had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday.

‌



He had planned to mark the milestone with a padel tournament, which will now take place in his memory with proceeds going towards his family.

His long-time friend Kwame Affum, 29, said he was struggling to comprehend the loss after the pair played padel together just two days before Mr Abiwon died.

‌



He told Metro: "I'm trying hard to get my head around this. I played padel with him just on Friday.

"One of our friends messaged him just before the accident on Sunday because we owed him money for the court. He didn’t answer and the alarm bells started ringing."

‌



View 3 Images A fallen tree during Storm Boelo as strong winds battered parts of the UK. (Image: Duncan Bryceland/Shutterstock)

Tributes have also been left beneath posts on Mr Abiwon’s Instagram page following his death. One person wrote: “My brother. I miss you, taken away too soon, I hope God protects your soul and spirit will forever live on.”

‌



Another said: “Thank you for your kindess and memories James. I will miss you forever.” Others left messages including “RIP” and “Sleep tight.”

Chief Inspector Guy Ellwood, from the North West Command Unit, said: "This is a deeply tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the young man who lost his life."

Article continues below

The London Ambulance Service sent incident response officers, paramedics from its hazardous area response team and a trauma team from London’s Air Ambulance.

A spokesperson said: "Very sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a man was pronounced dead at the scene."

News.title: Parents who murdered their baby son have 'unduly lenient' sentences increased
News.content:
Parents who murdered their baby son have 'unduly lenient' sentences increased

Klevi Pirjani, 38, and Nivalda Pirjani, 35, have had their sentences increased after being jailed in April for murdering their 13-week-old son Miguel

View 4 Images Klevi Pirjani, 38 (L) and 35-year-old Nivalda Pirjani were jailed for murder in April

A couple jailed for murdering their three-month-old son after he died in hospital with severe head injuries have had their "unduly lenient" sentences increased.

‌



‌



Klevi Pirjani, 38, and Nivalda Pirjani, 35, were jailed in April for a minimum of 19 years and 15 years over the killing of their son Miguel, whose injuries were inflicted during what a judge called a "callous" fatal assault.

‌



The tot spent the first month of his life in hospital before returning home, where he was assaulted for the first time, suffering two fractured ribs.

‌



The abuse continued and escalated over the following weeks, with the infant suffering a series of blows to his head on November 24, 2024.

View 4 Images Tributes outside the home in Seacombe following Miguel's death (Image: Liverpool Echo)

'Lovely' mum of two swept to her death by wave during Storm Boelo as she walked her dog READ MORE :

Miguel was examined and found to have sustained a severe, irreversible brain injury and a number of fractures to his body, which were at various stages of healing.

‌



Paramedics had initially managed to restart his heart, but Miguel never regained consciousness and tragically died in Alder Hey children's hospital five days later.

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves, referred the defendants' murder sentences to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme.

‌



Their minimum terms were today increased by two and a half years each to 17 years and 9 months and 21 years and 6 months respectively.

Barristers for the government argued that the original sentences did not "meet the justice of this terrible case".

‌



Lord Justice Jeremy Baker, sitting with Mr Justice Goose and Mr Justice Hilliard, said baby Miguel was subjected to " routine" assaults which worsened over time and led to his " particularly callous" murder.

View 4 Images The couple were arrested after Miguel was found unresponsive at their home in Seacombe in November 2024 (Image: Merseyside Police)

‌



He said: "We take the view that the resulting sentences significantly underestimated the aggravating factors, to the extent that not only do we consider that the minimum terms were unduly lenient, but that we should set them aside."

Medical examinations found that Miguel had suffered 41 fractures in total, including injuries to his ribs, legs, arm, collarbone and spine, inflicted during repeated assaults over several weeks.

‌



The judge said it was not possible to determine which parent had inflicted the fatal injuries, but found that they had acted together and that whichever parent carried out the violence was encouraged by the other.

Sentencing them in March, Mr Justice Andrew Baker told the court the couple were "in this together, encouraging each other" to beat their "defenceless" son.

‌



View 4 Images Both sentences have been increased by two and a half years (Image: Merseyside Police)

He said that who "fatally battered" the baby "remains the guilty secret of a warped relationship, in which you came first for each other to an unnatural degree".

‌



The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP said: "Miguel Pirjani was a defenceless baby who had an entire life to live, yet he suffered appallingly cruel violence at the hands of the two people who should have protected him.

"This was a truly harrowing case, and my thoughts are with everyone who loved and cared for him.

Article continues below

"I welcome the Court of Appeal’s decision to increase both minimum terms following my referral and remain committed to ensuring those who carry out the most serious crimes face the full force of the law."

News.title: I’ve been through two divorces and sometimes you think “I can’t take any more of this”
News.content:
Dear Coleen

My husband and I are currently going through a divorce, and trying to keep it as friendly as possible, as we have a two-year-old daughter.

We’re all still living together for her benefit, but the plan is to sell up in the near future and go our separate ways. I was the one who wanted to end the relationship. He hasn’t been there for me since we had our daughter, who he adores, but I do all the parenting.

He likes to drink, party and stay out late. His social life with his mates will always be the priority, even though they’re starting to look like a sad bunch of losers who are too old to still be raving. I’m 36 and he’s 10 years older, but you’d never believe it from the way he behaves.

More couples getting divorced after over 20 years of marriage, new figures show READ MORE :

But I’m trying hard to keep it civil, which hasn’t been easy because he’s totally reinvented our life together to make himself look better, and I have to bite my tongue when he’s spouting this rubbish to our friends.

‌



The other day, we had two couples over with their kids and the amount of lies my husband was telling them about all the stuff he used to do for my daughter when she was a baby made my blood boil. If he’d done all those things, I wouldn’t be divorcing him.

We have the same close group of friends and it feels very unfair, as I’m sure they feel sorry for him and wonder why I’m divorcing this saint of a man.

View 2 Images Coleen says things will get better when they're not living under the same roof

Coleen says

I completely agree with keeping things civil for your child, in fact it benefits everyone, but if she’s not there you can absolutely talk to your husband about some of the things he’s been saying to your friends. I’ve been through two divorces and sometimes you do think: “Oh, God, I can’t take any more of this”, so it is important to have a frank conversation otherwise you’ll blow.

‌



Remind him that you haven’t outed him to your friends for being an absent husband and father, so you’d really appreciate it if he didn’t rewrite history to make himself look good and make you look bad for divorcing him.

Maybe he is trying to get the sympathy vote, but remember that you’re selling the house soon and there probably won’t be too many times in the future when you’re together like this with friends.

It’s tricky at the moment because you’re in limbo and still under the same roof, but it’ll be so much easier when you’re living apart and focusing just on arrangements for your daughter.

‌



Make the focus what’s best for her and, if you need to rant and rave to a friend when she’s not around, that’s perfectly fine, but keep any potentially heated discussions with your husband away from little ears. Good luck.

Get all the latest advice from Britain's straightest-talking agony aunt Coleen Nolan here

Coleen's words of wisdom

If you’re struggling with a decision, choose what feels right for now and trust yourself to figure things out along the way. Indecision and procrastination feel stressful, and there’s freedom in making a choice that’s good enough and helps you move on.

News.title: Hull adventurer Karl Bushby set to complete epic 36,000-mile walk around the world
News.content:
Hull adventurer Karl Bushby set to complete epic 36,000-mile walk around the world

Karl Bushby, who is a 57-year-old ex-paratrooper, will soon be reunited with his mum in Hull after walking 20 miles every day on Britain's back roads

View 4 Images Karl Bushby is heading home to Hull via the back roads of Britain (Image: Getty Images)

Global adventurer Karl Bushby is days away from arriving in his home city after finishing his epic 36,000-mile walk around the world.

‌



‌



The 57-year-old ex-paratrooper, who is about to complete the longest unbroken path in human history, first set off from Chile back in 1998, with the aim of walking home without using transport to advance.

‌



Since then he has been cast adrift on an ice floe, attacked by a polar bear and held in a hellhole Panama jail.

‌



But Karl is now on his final leg of his record-breaking journey, having finished a swim across the English Channel on October.

1 in 3 children forced out of grassroots sport as cost of living crisis risks losing next Harry Kane READ MORE :

Musicians travel the world in record time to play on each continent within 100 days READ MORE :

View 4 Images British Adventurer Karl Bushby arriving in Dover, Kent, after completing his English Channel swim. (Image: India Whiskey Photographic/Press Association)

Karl Bushby set for hero’s welcome in Hull

After days of walking through the gales, he has now reached North Lincolnshire area and on Sunday is due to walk across the Humber Bridge with his dad and brother.

‌



His final stop will be a visit with his mum Angela after receiving a hero’s welcome when he meets the Lord Mayor of Hull in his home city on Monday.

People are being invited to gather in Queen Victoria Square, where he will be welcomed by Lord Mayor Maria Coward, who said: "We have all felt inspired by his spirit, tenacity and dogged determination to carry on in challenges faced by the most fearless of explorers."

‌



Karl is expected to arrive in the city centre at about 11am on Monday. The former paratrooper will be invited to join the Lord Mayor on a stage in front of City Hall. A brief private reception will follow.

View 4 Images Karl Bushby arriving in London on his trip back up north (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Proud dad praises Karl’s ‘one heck of an achievement’

Coward added: "We all (take) pride in his incredible achievement. We also know what it's like to come home to Hull – that feeling as your car or train, or feet in Karl's case, crosses or goes under the Humber Bridge and over the city boundary.

"As the world's media and documentary crews gather in our city, we can show them how proud we are of Karl's achievement and how proud we are to be from Hull."

‌



His dad Keith, 79, an SAS veteran from Hereford, says his son is currently around North Lincolnshire, getting closer to home after walking around 20 miles a day.

“The roads are pretty full and he’s having to take the back roads. Angela Maxwell is walking with him and she’s a world walker as well. He first met her walking through America and walked with her back in Mongolia then she swam the Caspian Sea with him. Then they walked up to France.”

‌



Keith, says he is proud of his son, who “doesn’t even like walking or swimming” adding: “It’s one heck of an achievement”.

The dad was reunited with his son after he came out of the sea at Dover and is going to see him again this weekend.

‌



“It was great to see him, but it was a bit strange and weird to see him in the flesh when he walked out of the sea. I‘ve seen him a couple of times over the years and we speak on Facebook and Messenger.

“He’s going to have a good story to tell, I just wonder how long people have got,” Keith jokes.

‌



View 4 Images Karl crossed the Bering Straights into Russia (Image: AFP)

Karl’s lifelong wanderlust began in childhood

The dad said his son has always had the “wanderlust” and they had to keep a careful eye on him as a child, once having to track him down on a crowded beach in New Zealand after he went on a walkabout.

‌



“Karl has a wanderlust, a genuine one, when he was a kid and I was in the army I used to take them up to the Yorkshire Dales, we would walk the hills together.

“When he was younger, a couple of times I had to go and find him. It wasn’t so much the age, it was the opportunity. I remember we went to my sister’s in New Zealand and one day on the beach he wandered off along the beach. He was about ten. I had to go and find a little blond kid in trunks, it was like ‘Where’s Wally?’

Article continues below

“Certainly in Hull, there were a lot of fields around us and that’s where he lived.

“It’s a hell of an achievement, he’s broken a couple of records on the way round but there were long boring stretches too,” he adds “but he loved walking in the desert, he loved the horizons and he felt safe there, you only get trouble where there’s humans around!”

News.title: Goal King Kane crowned the best in the world and could now be set for a knighthood
News.content:
Goal King Kane crowned the best in the world and could now be set for a knighthood

The England captain beat superstars Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to collect the game's top individual award. The humble hero paid tribute to his parents, wife, kids and even his big brother as he fought back tears to collect the coveted trophy.

Harry Kane hoists the Ballon d’Or before heading to the Cirque Le Soir

The huge grin on goal king Harry Kane's face said it all as the England captain officially became the best player in the world - and is hotly tipped to become 'Sir Harry'.

‌



‌



The 33-year-old hero beat superstars Kylian Mbappe, of France and Lamine Yamal, of Spain, to collect the game's top individual award - the Ballon D'Or.

‌



Flanked by an army of supporters keen to grab the moment of triumph on their phones, Kane proudly held the trophy aloft as he celebrated his incredible achievement

‌



And the humble hero paid tribute to his devoted parents, his wife and kids and even his brother as he was awarded the coveted Ballon d'Or trophy at the London Palladium.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Harry Kane could soon become 'Sir Harry' after a glowing tribute from the Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Image: AP Photo/Kin Cheung)

‌



It was the first time an Englishman had won in 25 years after Michael Owen in 2001. Kane, 33, celebrated into the early hours of the morning with his parents Pat and Kim, his brother Charlie and his wife Kate.

Accepting his prize from Brazilian legend Ronaldo, he said: "My brother Charlie is here. I know you tell me that I got your ability as a footballer so I appreciate that. To have the love and support from an older brother means the world to me.

‌



"To my children at home watching, it is a bit later than we thought but to Ivy, Henry, Vivienne and Louis, I cannot wait to see you. Kate, my best friend, you are my biggest supporter, here we are now, we've done it."

He fought back tears as he added: "Mum and dad - all those years, the sacrifice, following me all around the world, even to this day, you are there for me."

‌



He told young boys and girls that 'anything was possible' with hard work, and admitted that he had to 'fight his way to be the very best'.

View 4 Images Stunned Harry Kane accepts his award (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



England team mates Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, and legends Steve Gerrard and Wayne Rooney were among the first to send congratulations.

Downing Street hinted at a knighthood. A spokeswoman for No 10 said: "To be the first Englishman to win it in 25 years is an extraordinary achievement, and what a moment to do it here at home.

‌



"Seventy years after Sir Stanley Matthews won the inaugural award, it caps a remarkable season and Harry continues to set a brilliant example to young players across the country, and the PM knows the whole nation will be incredibly proud of him. And, hopefully, there's another trophy to celebrate with England before too long."

View 4 Images Harry Kane on the billboards in London (Image: AP Photo/Alastair Grant)

‌



The spokeswoman was also asked whether the Prime Minister would like to see the player knighted, adding: "On your question about a knighthood, I think everyone would agree, Harry Kane has given an enormous amount to English football, and this is a very special moment for him and the country, but, as ever, I'm not going to pre-empt the honours process."

Kane was born in Leytonstone, London, before moving to Chigwell, Essex, where he played for the same junior team, Ridgeway Rovers, as his childhood hero David Beckham.

‌



David Bricknell, who coached Kane for Ridgeway under-7s, said: "He is the perfect role model for any kid coming into the game. He is an absolute credit to his parents. I saw him three weeks ago and he gave me a big hug and asked about my family. He kept the England coach waiting. He has never forgotten his roots."

Kane paid tribute to his former coach at Spurs, Chris Ramsey, in his acceptance speech. "It does not surprise me that he has won, he was hands down the best player," said Chris.

‌



"He has had an unbelievable season. He will look back with his grandchildren in the years to come to see the players he beat to this award. He never stopped believing, when lots of people did not believe in him. I am so proud. People can knock the way he speaks, but it is the content of what he says that counts."

View 4 Images Kane accepts his award (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



A stunning 2025-26 campaign saw Kane score 73 goals for club and country. He won two trophies with Bayern Munich and led England to third place at the World Cup.

He followed in the footsteps of Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, and Kevin Keegan to win the award and listed the "sacrifices, saunas, ice baths."

‌



He admitted: "Even now, I am thinking if I can win it again." England boss Thomas Tuchel said: "I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago."

Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton.

Article continues below

England legend Alan Shearer said Kane was humble despite his superstar status, adding: "You see footballers walking down the red carpet and some of them are in sunglasses when it's pitch black. Harry is just normal, as normal as they come."

News.title: Monty Python legend Eric Idle, 83, forced to cancel entire tour due to health concerns
News.content:
Monty Python legend Eric Idle, 83, forced to cancel entire tour due to health concerns

Legendary entertainer Eric Idle has made a tough decision after he was forced to pull the plug on his Evening of Idle Conversation tour in Australia and New Zealand.

View 3 Images Eric Idle was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2019, but was later given the all-clear (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Eric Idle has sparked concerns for his health after doctors ordered him to cancel his entire upcoming tour.

‌



‌



The 83-year-old Monty Python legend apologised to fans who had bought tickets for his An Evening of Idle Conversation tour, which was due to run throughout November and December.

‌



The news comes four years after the comedian was given the all-clear following a secret battle with pancreatic cancer.

‌



He said he had no choice but to call of the event in Australia and New Zealand but vowed to do all his can to get back on stage next year. The Spamalot star, who joked that people can buy his book instead, was showered with support from fans online after making his announcement.

View 3 Images The much-loved Monty Python star says he must listen to doctors (Image: Getty Images)

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



Eric said in a statement: “It is with great regret that, on the advice of my doctors, I must withdraw from my planned An Evening of Idle Conversation tour of Australia and New Zealand.

“This isn’t a decision I take lightly, but when the doctors talk, I must listen. My apologies to the venues and to all those who were coming to see me.

‌



“Thank you for your support, as ever, and I will do all I can to get back there soon, health permitting. Meanwhile, you can still read my book.” In 2022, he revealed he "survived" pancreatic cancer after receiving a rare early diagnosis in 2019.

View 3 Images Eric says he hopes to be back on stage soon (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Eric explained in an interview with the The Sunday Times that he thought the diagnosis was a “joke” because his doctor had suggested the same illness would be a suitable way to kill off a character in a stage show he was writing.`

“I laughed [when I was given the diagnosis] because I thought it was a joke. But I survived! Basically I shouldn’t f***ing be here. Every day is extra time for me. I just hope there aren’t any penalties at the end.”

‌



In a heartfelt 'Letter To My Younger Self' for the Big Issue, he's once again reflected on the ordeal. "I miss a lot of people. Great people like Mike Nichols [director of The Graduate]," he wrote.

"I will find myself thinking of a funny line and thinking, you must tell Mike that. Or Jonathan Miller [a British public thinker and former comedian]. So many of my heroes have gone, like Robin Williams. I still kind of occasionally speak to Billy Connolly, but I really miss him.

‌



"You’ve got to find other people, you know, because there are still other funny people you can have dinner with or play guitar with. I got lucky, because I had to, I survived pancreatic cancer. So I feel that since 2019 I’ve had a reprieve. So I don’t know or care what people say about me, I’m lucky every single day."

He was part of the Monty Python troupe which became one of the UK's best known comedy act which a hugely successful BBC TV series.

‌



He starred alongside Graham Chapman, John Cleese, Terry Gilliam, Terry Jones and Sir Michael Palin in TV series which began in 1969 as well as films and live shows.

Chapman died in 1989 of tonsil cancer aged 48 while Jones died in 2020 aged 77 from a rare form of dementia.

Article continues below

The series was a massive success, with 45 episodes produced from 1969 to 1974. It also gave rise to five films, including the 1975 classic 'The Holy Grail', which later inspired the hit musical 'Spamalot', penned by Eric himself.

News.title: Major UK law firm enters administration after 25 years
News.content:
Major UK law firm enters administration after 25 years

Rahman Ravelli Solicitors Ltd, a leading UK firm specialising in high-stakes financial defence, has entered administration after more than two decades, with clients now being contacted about transferring their active cases.

View 3 Images Powerhouse law firm crashes into administration after 25 years (Image: Getty)

Prominent UK law firm Rahman Ravelli has collapsed into administration, drawing the curtain on a 25-year reign as one of Britain's foremost specialists in high-profile financial defence cases. The London and Yorkshire -based firm appeared in a corporate insolvency notice in The Gazette, the official public record, today, October 27, 2026.

‌



‌



Rahman Ravelli Solicitors Ltd was established in 2001 by managing partner Aziz Rahman and went on to forge an impressive international reputation over the following decades. The firm became a go-to name for corporations, senior executives, and high-net-worth individuals embroiled in investigations involving serious fraud, bribery, corruption, money laundering, sanctions breaches, and asset recovery.

‌



Among its most high-profile victories, the firm secured the acquittal of former Nigerian Oil minister Olatimbo Ayinde in June this year, following a gruelling six-month trial at Southwark Crown Court.

‌



View 3 Images Rahman Ravelli Solicitors Ltd was established in 2001 by managing partner Aziz Rahman (Image: Getty)

Ensure our latest business news headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings

Although the formal administrative announcement published on the firm's website stopped short of disclosing any financial details, reports from Global Investigations Review and Lexology Pro suggest the firm's collapse is connected to the long-term ill-health of its founding partner, Aziz Rahman.

‌



According to the Official Administration Notice posted on the firm's website, Andrew Hosking and Jamie Taylor of BTG Advisory LLP were appointed as Joint Administrators on October 20, 2026. The company's accounts as of December 31, 2024, revealed that the firm had an average of 25 staff over the preceding 12 months, all of whom could now face redundancy.

View 3 Images The firm represented a defendant in a high-profile case earlier this year in London (Image: Getty)

‌



As part of the winding-down process, the firm has assured clients that ongoing operations are being handled safely. In a statement reported by The Law Society Gazette, the firm confirmed that all client funds held securely in regulated accounts remain completely unaffected by the administration.

To manage the orderly transfer of cases, the Joint Administrators have appointed Samantha Palmer of Child & Child Law Limited to act as Solicitor Manager.

Article continues below

Case handlers are currently reaching out to active clients to obtain urgent instructions on moving files to alternative legal representation.

Rahman Ravelli Solicitors Ltd has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase
News.content:
The rise in the minimum wage is expected to be announced in the Budget, but 18-to-20 year-olds are set to see lower increases than in previous years, the BBC understands.

Pay for younger workers will rise in line with the increase in minimum pay for employees aged 21 years and over.

However, the increase for younger workers is lower than that seen in the previous two years, when Labour raised the rate to meet a manifesto promise that it would remove "discriminatory age bands" with all adults entitled to the same minimum wage.

Chancellor John Healey is also announcing measures to give families what he is calling "breathing space" with the cost of living.

"The manifesto pledge on equalisation still applies but we were always clear it could happen over time," Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told the BBC:

"Of course, you want not just good wages but good work, " he added. "It is a balance of making sure the pressures on the labour market are taken into account."

The Times reported that the National Minimum Wage for 18-to-20 year-olds is likely to rise by 3.9% from Â£10.85 an hour to around Â£11.27.

That is a smaller rise than the 26% increase the Labour government has put in place for younger workers since returning to power in 2024.

Even after the reported rise, the rate remains below the National Living Wage for older workers, which is currently Â£12.71 an hour. It is set to rise by 3.9% to Â£13.20, the Times said.

Andrea Egan, general secretary of the union Unison, said it was "deeply unfair" to keep paying different rates for the same job.

"Twenty year-old care workers, teaching assistants and security guards do the same work as their older colleagues," she said. "They don't pay less in the supermarket or at the petrol pump. They must be paid equally."

News.title: Two in court over alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford
News.content:
Two British nationals have appeared in court in connection to an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford last month.

Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, from Westminster, London, has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police earlier said they believed to be Iran.

Nouman Essghir, also 24 and from Westminster, has been charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on 22 August - weeks before he was arrested near the airbase in Gloucestershire alongside four other men.

The pair appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near the US-operated airbase on 27 September.

Dozens of residents were evacuated and a large cordon was put up in the area around the base. No explosive materials were found in the vans by police but a quantity of petrol was seized.

The court heard vans bearing the logo "Fuel2You" were spotted close to the base.

In the early hours, the vans came across a Ministry of Defence Police cordon and re-routed to another location.

Police arrived and arrested five men. They later revealed that one had called 999 and reported what was going on.

During the hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court, Essghir stood in the dock wearing a grey sweatshirt and confirmed his name and address.

His charge relates to an alleged "reconnaissance mission" on 22 August, around a month before the Fairford incident.

Abdulkarim is charged with helping with the plot.

He appeared in court in a wheelchair wearing a checked shirt, jeans and a baseball cap. He confirmed his name and address.

Both men are charged under the 2023 National Security Act.

Essghir has been remanded in custody, while Abdulkarim has been granted bail with conditions including the surrender of his passport.

The case will be next heard at the Old Bailey on 20 November.

News.title: What does Israel's election mean for Gaza and the wider world?
News.content:
Israelis are voting in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is in a near neck-and-neck race with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to become prime minister.

But where do the two rivals stand when it comes to foreign policy and how might their actions differ with regards to Gaza and the occupied West Bank?

The BBC's diplomatic correspondent James Landale reports from Jerusalem.

More on Israel's pivotal election.

News.title: Men abused woman after her husband drugged and advertised her online, court told
News.content:
Four men sexually assaulted a woman after her then-husband drugged her and advertised her on Craigslist, Grindr and swinging websites, a court has been told.

Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, are on trial at Winchester Crown Court after pleading not guilty to sexual offences against Joanne Young.

They are charged jointly with her ex-husband Philip Young, 50, a former Conservative councillor, who has admitted to drugging and raping her over 13 years.

As the trial began, prosecutor Sarah Jones KC told the jury: "This case is about whether it is ever reasonable to have sex with an unknown woman without checking with her first."

Warning: This story contains distressing details

Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, told police that to her knowledge she had a "fairly normal" and "always monogamous" sex life with her husband.

But on one occasion in 2023, she said she had woken up with restraints and a blindfold on while a man was carrying out a sexual act on her.

Jones told the jury Joanne had believed her husband was performing the sexual act on her when in reality he was "stage managing another unknown person" who was "taking his place without her knowledge".

Jones told the jury Young had advertised Joanne online, seeking "strangers to come and sleep with his wife".

"He presented it as a kink for both of them, but there was no information from Joanne herself to support this and the photos he posted of her to advertise his offer showed her inanimate and tied to the bed blindfolded," Jones told the court.

"The nightcap they shared, it appeared, would be used to plunge her into a state where anything could be done to her by whoever answered and she would be unaware or unable to remember."

News.title: I'm a single mum and limit my weekly shop to £40 - here's what I want from the Budget
News.content:
Chloe Chin-Saad's husband passed away four years ago and her biggest worry is the cost of living.

She's very grateful that the rent she pays on her south London maisonette is set below the market rate as it is housing association accommodation, but says life was easier when she shared the bills. "Two incomes make a massive difference."

She lives with her 16-year-old son, and says her energy bill has risen sharply over the past year and she now pays about Â£200 a month on gas and electricity.

"We try to be more aware, we think more about how long we run the hot water when we do the dishes."

Chloe, 40, and her son have cut back on luxuries like going to M&S and the cinema, and she now tries to limit the weekly food shop to Â£40.

But she can't do anything to reduce her Â£200 council tax bill, the Â£250 a month she pays on car finance, or the amount she spends on medicines for her various health conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis.

Two mobile phone bills, and food and pet insurance for her dog also add to her costs. She says the amount she has left over at the end of each month varies, and sometimes she is left with as little as Â£50.

Chloe wants to see more help for single-parent families.

"I don't access benefits but I work full-time and it's hard. Can the government do anything else to help? Something on our tax bill perhaps."

News.title: Russell Brand told police he never had non-consensual sex
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had been "very promiscuous" in the past, but had never engaged in "non-consensual sexual activity", a court has heard.

Brand, 51, was interviewed four times between 2023 and 2025 by officers.

The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges.

Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each of the police interviews. In November 2023, he said: "I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. I have never engaged in non-consensual activity."

News.title: Worker at US embassy in London investigated over abuse images is senior Air Force member
News.content:
A US embassy staffer accused of possessing and distributing child sex abuse material, but left the UK before he was questioned by British police, is a high-ranking member of the US Air Force, the BBC has been told.

The BBC understands he is Lieutenant Colonel Michael Morris, who worked as an assistant military attachÃ© at the embassy in south-west London.

He was questioned by American authorities after investigators alleged his US-based brother Benjamin Morris had shared child abuse material with him.

Benjamin Morris, 33, is facing trial in the US state of Illinois for the possession and dissemination of child sexual abuse material, which he denies.

The Rock Island County State Attorney, Dora Villareal, told the BBC the allegations against Benjamin Morris relate to a period between March and April 2026.

His brother, Lt Col Michael Morris, was flown out of the UK in August on a civilian flight without first being questioned by British police.

While not a diplomat, it is understood he enjoyed the umbrella of diplomatic protection.

In September, the US embassy confirmed to the BBC that authorities are investigating the allegations and they reassigned the staff member to the US while inquiries continued.

A spokesperson for the US Air Force has since told the BBC: "Charges have been preferred against Lt Col Michael Morris, currently assigned to the Air Force District of Washington.

"The charges and evidence will be reviewed to determine whether the case should be tried by court-martial."

The US Air Force said "charges are merely allegations and the Department of the Air Force member is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty".

The spokesperson said a military hearing was due to take place in November at Joint Base Andrews near Washington DC, and Lt Col Morris will only enter a plea if the matter is referred to court-martial - a formal military criminal trial.

The US Embassy in London previously said it "expects all personnel to adhere to the highest standards of conduct, and we take these allegations seriously", adding it "quickly informed UK law enforcement and took swift action".

The Metropolitan Police said: "We have been liaising regularly with the US authorities since they made us aware on Tuesday, 25 August of their investigation into suspected offences relating to indecent images of children.

"We are aware that charges have been brought in the US in relation to this case and that legal proceedings are ongoing. We remain in contact with the US authorities".

A spokesperson for the UK government said: "We expect all foreign diplomats in the UK to abide by our laws, in the same way we expect all UK diplomats to do so when posted overseas.

"As a US investigation is ongoing, it would not be appropriate to comment further at this stage."

The BBC understands the government remains in close contact with the US Embassy, including at a ministerial level.

News.title: My husband's death was hard enough - then came the admin
News.content:
Louisa Nicoll knew her husband John was going to die about a year before it happened. The couple used the time to make memories with their children, James and Amy, and John meticulously organised their paperwork.

But despite him asking for accounts to be switched to Louisa's name, she still received post addressed to him after his death. In one letter from their energy provider, it said: "Sorry you're leaving us. Is there anything we can do to make you stay?"

"I felt utterly exhausted, overwhelmed, frustrated and angry because of those experiences," she told BBC's Morning Live.

Louisa now campaigns for changes in the way companies deal with admin after someone dies and offers advice on how talking about death before it happens can help families cope afterwards.

News.title: UK and EU officials to discuss freedom of movement
News.content:
Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Reynolds said current discussions ahead of the summit are around food and drink, electricity and emissions trading.

He said: "What the prime minister has also said, quite rightly, is we face a series of policy changes on the European side that will affect us.

"We need to get as little uncertainty as possible, we need to have a way to resolve what our long-term relationship will be and he is going to set that out after the summit.

"He is going to be frank with the British people about what the trade-offs are but no assumptions have been made on that."

Pressed on whether UK officials are talking to the EU about freedom of movement Reynolds said: "They will be talking to them about what the future options for our relationship might be.

"But here and now, the focus should be on the summit and the tangible difference improvements we're going to make."

A government spokesperson stressed there were no current discussions on freedom of movement.

"We are working with the EU on the areas set out and agreed ahead of the UK-EU Summit and within the manifesto red lines," the spokesperson added.

Burnham is far more willing to have a public conversation around Brexit than his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, whose government was nervous about reopening a debate that proved so contentious in the past.

Some people within the Labour Party had been urging Sir Keir to go further and there is a widely held view that Burnham's comments are likely to go down well with voters tempted by the Liberal Democrats and Greens.

But there is nervousness among Labour MPs with small majorities in Brexit-supporting, Reform-facing constituencies.

Labour MP Melanie Onn, whose constituency Great Grimsby and Cleethorpes backed leaving the EU, told the Today programme Burnham risked losing trust by talking about going beyond the 2024 manifesto at a future election.

"I don't think that the scars have healed for many people around the country so I do think this is an unnecessary conversation to be having at this time," she said.

Onn, who lost her seat in 2019 to the Conservatives but won it back in 2024, warned against re-opening the conversation, saying: "Trust is incredibly important, it's hard-earned and easily lost, and on this matter I think that we should tread incredibly carefully."

Speaking to BBC Wales, Labour MP Ruth Jones said: "We need to be very careful here. We must respect the Brexit referendum result."

Asked if a referendum on freedom of movement was something she would support, the MP for Newport West and Islwyn said: "We're a long way from that. Andy Burnham is floating the idea, and it's great to float ideas, but let's talk it through and see what does it mean, because another referendum at this particular time would be divisive."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told BBC Breakfast that "Andy Burnham has no mandate to be in Brussels, to be negotiating any of this" and called for the prime minister to put his ideas to the public in a general election.

On Monday, Burnham left the door open to a potential referendum on freedom of movement with the EU.

The prime minister caused some confusion when he told broadcasters that he would not reintroduce free movement without a referendum, but Downing Street later said no decisions had been made on whether a public vote would be needed.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC on Sunday that no options for the UK's future relationship could be taken off the table.

But Burnham did appear to draw some red lines of his own when he told the Sunday Times, external that he would not be in favour of the UK joining the euro or the border-free Schengen zone.

The fact the prime minister has not been willing to say the same thing about free movement is being seen in Westminster as evidence that he believes it is a genuine option.

News.title: Chancellor to promise £15m to tackle misogyny in Budget
News.content:
The "misogyny prevention fund" is expected to be confirmed in the Budget and is intended to support the work of a national taskforce established last month, external and chaired by Women and Equalities Minister Bridget Phillipson.

Healey said the money will support "practical action to tackle misogyny head-on" and he hopes it will attract additional funding from businesses and philanthropists to increase its reach.

Phillipson said daily incidents of misogyny, including sexist slurs and workplace discrimination, have "no place in modern Britain".

She said: "This funding is a critical step as we work to confine misogyny to the history books, where it belongs."

Phillipson added that "everyone, from big business to members of the public, can do their bit to stamp out misogyny and improve the lives of women and girls everywhere".

When launching the taskforce chaired by Phillipson, the government said last month that it would aim to ensure government policy is "shaped by those most affected by misogyny".

It added its first meeting would focus on young people and later look at "workplaces, digital spaces and social cohesion".

Statistics published by the Office for National Statistics this month showed an estimated 12.8% of females aged 16 and over in England and Wales - around 3.2m - experienced at least one of domestic abuse, sexual victimisation or stalking in the year to March 2026.

The figure was an estimated 8.9% for males - around 2.1m.

For the Conservatives, Morrissey cited the estimates for women and girls as she criticised the announcement.

She said: "Labour simply aren't serious about tackling the crisis of violence against women and girls.

"This week it seems they will get the hard-pressed British taxpayer to fork out Â£15m to fund projects to tackle the 'manosphere'."

News.title: More high winds hit parts of UK as Storm Boelo clean-up continues
News.content:
Strong winds are expected to continue across Scotland and parts of Northern Ireland on Tuesday, after Storm Boelo brought flooding and power cuts to thousands over the weekend.

While conditions are set to improve for much of the UK after a wet and windy morning, clean-up efforts could be hampered elsewhere - including in Scotland, where a third of a month's rain fell during the storm.

The Energy Networks Association (ENA) said almost 8,000 people were still without power after more than 800,000 experienced cuts.

Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s whose car was hit in north London and a 60-year-old man in Dumfries and Galloway identified as Richard Baines, the long-serving curator of Logan Botanic Garden.

A deep area of low pressure, while not severe enough to be a named storm, still brought strong winds with gusts of 65-80mph to parts of western England and Wales in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Through the rest of Tuesday, the strongest winds will be across Scotland and the northern coast of Northern Ireland, where a Met Office yellow warning is due to be in place until 21:00 GMT.

Gusts will continue to reach 50-60mph, possibly up to 70mph in the most exposed parts of northwest and northern Scotland.

That is is likely to bring further travel disruption and more power cuts in places.

Elsewhere across the UK, Tuesday will be a blustery day, but the wind is not likely to cause any major impacts.

Strong winds and heavy rain will ease off later on Tuesday, with the rest of the week looking much calmer across the UK.

Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen.

Leo Slade, CEO of the ENA said it had been "a tough weekend" and that efforts to reconnect some properties were being hampered by the weather, with sustained winds of 50-85mph across parts of Scotland and northern England.

"Until that weather system passes, we can't safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up, so today is going to be a hive of activity in getting engineers out into the field," he told the BBC.

He stressed that the UK's power network was very resilient and money was spent to prepare for these sorts of scenarios, but said a debate was needed over how much more investment was required to mitigate for further storms brought by climate change.

The Met Office has warned about the possibility of further power cuts and people should make sure they have essentials prepared, including torches and batteries.

News.title: Parents who killed their baby have sentences increased
News.content:
A couple who "fatally battered" their three-month-old son have had their "unduly lenient" sentences for murder increased.

Klevi Pirjani, 38, and 35-year-old Nivalda Pirjani, from Wirral, Merseyside, were sentenced in April to a minimum of 19 years and 15 years in April over the death of their son, 13-week-old Miguel.

The Court of Appeal has now increased Klevi Pirjani's sentence to 21 years and six months, while Nivalda Pirjani will have to serve 17 years and nine months.

Miguel was taken to Alder Hey children's hospital in November 2024. He had severe head injuries and died five days after being admitted.

Miguel was found to have suffered 41 separate bone fractures in at least four separate incidents.

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves, referred their sentences to the Court of Appeal, with barristers for the government arguing that the original sentences did not "meet the justice of this terrible case".

News.title: Boy who stabbed girl at school was radicalised online, says father
News.content:
Warning: The following report contains details that some may find distressing

The father of a teenager who tried to kill a fellow pupil in a school knife attack has described his devastation and belief that his son was "radicalised" by extreme material online.

The boy, now 16, was found guilty of attempted murder last week after a trial heard how he harboured a hatred of women, had a fascination with serial killers and had planned to target others in the attack at Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich.

Speaking exclusively to the BBC and calling for tighter controls, the boy's father said he did not want to "absolve" his son but suggested online material and "a culture of violence and horror" had influenced him.

The government said it was committed to ensuring all children were safe from radicalisation and threats online, pointing to its Prevent anti-terrorism scheme and the Online Safety Act, which compels social media platforms to remove and prevent the spread of illegal content.

The boy cannot be identified due to his age, and nor can witnesses and the victim in the case.

His father, who we are calling John, apologised to the 15-year-old girl injured in the attack on 11 March, saying: "We're so very sorry for what happened."

John spoke of his fears that young men were being radicalised towards violence and hatred.

"You can think... it can never happen to my family or my son couldn't be involved, but that's what we thought and that wasn't the case," he said.

News.title: Landline switchover could cut people off in emergency, minister warned
News.content:
Plans to switch off the UK's traditional landline phone network could leave people in remote areas unable to contact help in an emergency, MPs have warned.

Landline operators aim to complete the switch to an internet-based network instead of copper-wire cables by the end of January next year.

The government and operators say the move to digital landlines will offer a more reliable service.

But MPs representing remote areas of the UK urged security minister Dan Jarvis to ensure that scrapping the copper-wire network did not make their communities more vulnerable in a storm or other emergency.

Unlike digital services, the traditional landline network does not rely on mains electricity and continues to work in a power cut.

Labour MP Torcuil Crichton, who represents the Western Isles constituency of Na h-Eileanan an Iar, said: "Resilience is inbuilt in the islands but we have major problems with connectivity because of this move from analogue to digital phone lines."

He said that "when the power goes out people don't have the phone, they don't have the internet and often they don't have a mobile signal either".

BT OpenReach has been giving back-up battery packs to vulnerable customers, which can keep landline phones operating for an hour or more.

But Crichton said this was "simply not adequate" and that mobile phone providers "simply don't have the means to maintain or keep their signal going during storms".

He urged the minister to get telecoms firms to "up their digital game" to protect places "on the edge where people are vulnerable, isolated from their neighbours, where the ambulance is an hour away and the storm is 70 miles an hour".

Similar concerns were raised by MPs from the West Country and the Lake District.

Markus Campbell-Savours, Labour MP for Penrith and Solway, said: "I ask the minister to imagine an elderly constituent living alone in an isolated Lake District valley where copper phone lines have been replaced by fibre.

"A storm takes out the power to their router in the night and by the time they wake, the modest battery back up has failed, as has the mobile mast, does the minister share my concerns that they would have no way to raise an alarm in an emergency and agree that we need a new technological solution to protect the elderly?"

News.title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears
News.content:
A celebrity has asked the High Court to prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations that he abused his status for many years to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".

The unnamed celebrity is seeking an injunction, and his legal team told the first day of a trial on Tuesday that any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself.

They told the court that his drastic reaction was not because of any wrongdoing, but because of the fear of "trial by media".

The man denies abusing "his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them", the court heard.

The legal team for ITN and Guardian News and Media (GNM) told the court that the celebrity's "suicide risk" could be mitigated and there was no proper basis "to restrain the publication of public interest journalism".

A medical report carried out for the court said inpatient treatment could provide "significant, but not complete mitigation of the risk", but that treatment, perhaps for months, had "a realistic potential to reduce the risk".

The judge, Mr Justice Nicklin, said there was "significant public interest" in the proceedings and that "this is a difficult and important case".

He added: "The court must determine it fairly, on the evidence and legal submissions."

News.title: Police failings in friends' death on mountain ridge could risk lives, coroner warns
News.content:
More people could die on remote mountains unless police do a better job in responding to dropped 999 calls, a coroner has warned.

The bodies of friends Eddie Hill, 20, and Jayden Long, 19, both from Dereham, Norfolk, were found on a mountain ridge in Eryri, also known as Snowdonia, on 19 February, a day after a call from Long to North Wales Police was disconnected.

Officers did try unsuccessfully to call him back, but then made "limited" efforts to find out who owned the phone and took more than three hours to alert mountain rescue, assistant coroner Sarah Riley said.

North Wales Police said it had taken steps to strengthen its policies and procedures.

Hill and Long died in extreme winter conditions on Crib y Ddysgl, a ridge that peaks at 1,065m (3,494ft), less than a mile north of Yr Wyddfa's summit and linking it to the notoriously narrow ridge of Crib Goch.

A Prevention of Future Deaths, external report said police received a discontinued call from Long's mobile phone at 16:27 GMT on 18 February.

A playback captured him saying "hello" and "can you hear me?" before the call was lost.

News.title: Fleetwood v Arsenal LIVE: Max Dowman starts in Carabao Cup as two handed debuts
News.content:

Max Dowman scored twice in the 4-2 win at Ipswich in the third round ( Getty )

Arsenal could offer another opportunity to Max Dowman as they face Fleetwood Town in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

The 16-year-old scored twice and was named player of the week as Arsenal beat Ipswich 4-2 in the previous round of the competition, with Arteta looking to rotate his team ahead of Sunday’s trip to Liverpool in the Premier League.

The champions will be expected to progress against League Two strugglers Fleetwood, who lie 18th in the fourth tier and some 84 places below the Gunners in the English football pyramid.

Arsenal have won 11 of their 13 games in all competitions this season and defeated Everton in the Premier League on Saturday thanks to goals from centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes.

Arteta, whose side were runners-up in the Carabao Cup last season, warned his players that they will need to be ready when they travel to Fleetwood. "We need to go there and win the game," he said. "Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play.”

Follow updates from Fleetwood v Arsenal in the Carabao Cup, below

News.title: Trump accused of raping former Miss Switzerland in Democrats’ Epstein report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump is accused of raping a former Miss Switzerland in a report probing the president’s relationship with Jeffrey Epstein released by House of Representatives Democrats this week.

Beatrice Keul, a retired model and beauty pageant contestant, told the House Judiciary Committee about an incident alleged to have taken place at New York’s Plaza Hotel in 1993. The report, released a week ahead of the midterm elections, also summarizes previously reported allegations from four other women against Trump.

The White House has strongly denied all of the reports’ claims, accusing “crazed” Democrats of “a desperate attempt to distract Americans” and insisting that the president has been “fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.”

Keul previously claimed in October 2024 that Trump had sexually assaulted her at a beauty pageant staged at the Plaza Hotel, which Trump then owned.

Keul told Judiciary Committee staff who interviewed her for the new report that she was 24 when she flew in from Zurich to attend the American Dream Pageant in Manhattan and met Trump at a lunch associated with the contest.

open image in gallery Beatrice Keul and Donald Trump in 1993, in a picture included in the House Committee on the Judiciary report ( Courtesy of Beatrice Keul )

Over the course of a 15-minute conversation, the then-real estate tycoon promised to arrange a visa for her and to help her get into New York University, Keul told the committee.

When Trump stepped away, she said she was then approached by Epstein, who said: “I’m Jeffrey, Don’s best friend.”

She claims Epstein invited her to a party at Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s residence in Palm Beach, Florida, and assured her: “You know I can take care of you. We organize many parties with Don… Flights, accommodations, you don’t have to worry about anything.”

The report states that Keul was then approached by a Trump representative later that day and invited up to the future president’s suite, explaining that she saw the chance of a further meeting with the influential businessman as “a lucky break for the purpose of furthering her career and education.”

“Upon entering, Trump reportedly grabbed Keul from behind and forcibly raped her; in the process, tearing her dress and causing bleeding and bruising on multiple parts of her body,” the report recounts of her allegations.

Keul described the alleged rape as “brutal,” according to House Democrats, who said she remembered Trump sitting on the bed afterwards, repeating his promise to help with her visa and enrollment in higher education and reminding her: “The show must go on.”

open image in gallery The White House stressed Trump had been “fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein” ( Getty )

Keul concluded her testimony by saying she had completed her part in the pageant and then returned home to Switzerland, declining to take part in another Trump-sponsored event in Hawaii scheduled for several weeks later.

She did take a call from Trump several months after that, she said, in which he again offered to help with her U.S. visa. She turned down the gesture.

Keul previously made allegations about the Plaza Hotel incident in The Daily Mail two years ago, a week before the 2024 presidential election.

“He kissed me on the lips and on the neck,” she told the newspaper at the time. “He tried to lift my dress. He was grabbing and touching my body everywhere he could.

“I tried everything I could. Finally, I said ‘let’s talk first’ or something like that, then he slowed down.”

Her account was denied at the time by Trump’s then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who called it a “false” story.

“Fake allegations like this are a disservice to women who are truly victims of assault,” she said.

Of the other accusers highlighted in the Democrats' report, Stacey Williams, a former Sports Illustrated swimsuit model, has accused Trump of groping her at an event at Trump Tower in 1993 as part of a “twisted game” with Epstein, who had introduced them.

open image in gallery Trump’s accuser also claims to have met Jeffrey Epstein at the event in question ( New York State Sex Offender Registry )

Jill Harth accuses Trump of sexually assaulting her at a party at Mar-a-Lago, his Florida home, in the mid-1990s at which he and Epstein appeared to be the only men present.

A woman using the pseudonym “Katie Johnson” claimed Trump and Epstein raped her when she was a teenager and aspiring model, an incident she once gave a detailed account of to the FBI.

And another woman using the pseudonym “Jane Doe” likewise claims to have told the FBI about Trump allegedly sexually assaulting her when she was a minor.

“None of these allegations are true,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told The Independent, in response to the Judiciary Committee report.

“This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements.

“The President kicked Jeffrey Epstein out of his club at Mar-a-Lago because he was a creep, and he has been fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein.”

News.title: Budget 2026 latest: Chancellor Healey ‘to freeze NHS prescription charges’ for another year
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in
