Sports.title: Donnarumma gets Maresca’s backing; Iraola feels bond growing at Anfield
Sports.content:
1. Maresca: ‘He’s a strong character’

Enzo Maresca has given his backing to Gianluigi Donnarumma after the goalkeeper’s costly errors in Manchester City’s recent defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa.

Donnarumma was at fault for Nicolas Jackson’s game-winning strike at Villa Park on Saturday, the forward’s long-range shot squeezing under the Italian’s body and leading to City’s first league defeat of the season. Against PSG in the Champions League this month, Donnarumma was at fault for Désiré Doué’s and Maghnes Akliouche’s goals as City lost 4-2 against the holders.

“As a football player or manager, when you don’t get results or make some mistakes, it’s normal. It’s a consequence,” Maresca said. “Gigio since we started is doing well. Like any manager or player making some mistakes, it’s part of the season.

“They [footballers] play so many games and minutes that sometimes it’s impossible not to make mistakes. He’s a strong character. He knows that when he makes a mistake, he doesn’t need us to tell him – sometimes it’s so clear so they recognise this.”

Marc Guéhi has been in uneven form, too. The defender was culpable for Jackon’s opener on Saturday. He also conceded a late penalty in the previous weekend’s 3-2 win against Ipswich, and made an early mistake that led directly to Lamine Yamal scoring for Spain against England in the Nations League last month.

“I am completely happy with Marc,” Maresca said. “The way he reacts is fantastic, he is a top guy. He is one of the captains, he is a leader and I love Marc. Same as Gigio, when they make some mistakes it is recognised.”

Donnarumma will be rested for Brighton’s visit in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. Maresca said: “After the Villa game we gave five players three days off to recover the energy: Erling [Haaland], Rúben [Dias], Elliot [Anderson], Gigio and Josko [Gvardiol]. They are all on holiday. Three days off, energy, go, come back with full energy then we go again.”

Geronimo Rulli will again deputise for Donnarumma against Brighton. JJ

Sports.title: Pierre Sage given more time by Crystal Palace but remains under pressure
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage has been given more time to turn around Crystal Palace’s fortunes but he remains under huge pressure and could be dismissed if they lose against Tottenham on Saturday.

The Frenchman’s position was in serious doubt after another poor performance in the 2-0 defeat against Newcastle at the weekend. That followed a 5-0 thrashing against Brighton when Sage was warned that he could be dismissed if results did not improve quickly.

However the club’s chair, Steve Parish, has decided not to act given the tight turnaround in Palace’s schedule: the side face Fulham at Craven Cottage in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, before their trip to Tottenham in the Premier League. But Sage, who attended the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Monday evening, is understood to have been left in no doubt that the meeting with Spurs on Saturday is crucial to his future.

Palace are 17th and have conceded 19 goals in eight Premier League matchesthis season – the highest in the division. But, it is understood, Sage retains the support of his squad, with two leading players having sent him messages saying that they still have faith he can turn things around.

Palace’s hierarchy are said to be split over whether to fire the former Lens manager after only 12 games in charge, with some in favour of bringing in Thomas Frank or Sean Dyche to steady the ship. The former Wolves manager Rob Edwards has also been mentioned as a potential contender.

There is sympathy for Sage at boardroom level given that Axel Disasi – who was signed on loan from Chelsea to replace the key defender Maxence Lacroix – has only just returned from a three-match suspension. There were also signs of improvement in the 2-2 Europa League draw at Besiktas in midweek, with Sage believed to have been delighted with Jean-Philippe Mateta’s response since returning from injury. The France striker is in the final year of his contract but failed in an attempt to have it ruled invalid by an independent Premier League tribunal and Fifa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There are concerns about Ismaïla Sarr, however, who missed the defeat against Newcastle after a recurrence of the groin injury that ruled him out earlier in the season. The Senegal forward has made no secret of his disappointment after Palace rejected a bid from Liverpool in the summer and Sage needs the club’s player of the year last season back on the pitch if they are to recover from a poor start to life after Oliver Glasner.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga.

The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao.

“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” Mbappé said in a statement in French, Chinese and English.

Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 – and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths – remain taboo.

The beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappé consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheese maker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappé, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappé” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views.

One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks … crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappé’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappé’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”.

View image in fullscreen Two Chinese brands have ended deals with Kylian Mbappé after he allegedly referred to Mao Zedong as a ‘Chinese dictator’. Photograph: Karwai Tang/WireImage

In an interview with the French sports newspaper L’Equipe last month, the 27-year-old Mbappé addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny … but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said.

China’s foreign ministry said it was aware of the reports regarding Mbappé, who on Monday finished runner-up to Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or award for the world’s best player. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesperson Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and removed all s involving Mbappé. On the CCTV website, La Liga matches this weekend were still on its online viewing schedule.

Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there. The former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s then vice-president and current president, Lai Ching-te, sparking fury on Chinese social media. Beijing claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

The Houston Rockets general manager, Daryl Morey, posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.

Fans in China made their feelings clear. “I used to really enjoy watching Mbappé play on the pitch,” Zhang Jingqi, 30, who works at a mall in Beijing, said. “But ever since this news broke yesterday I have lost that admiration, sorry to say.”

Sports.title: Police called to Florida soccer game after parents say three-year-old benched for being too good
Sports.content:
Police were called after a dispute involving the parents of a three-year-old player at a soccer game in Florida over the weekend.

The boy’s parents can be heard on police body cameras saying their son, Nevada, had been kicked out because he was too good at soccer and was embarrassing the other children. However, an organizer at the game said Nevada had pushed other children and his parents had become argumentative when their son was taken out of the game.

In police body camera footage the organizer of the event, who works for i9 Sports, a youth sports group, can be heard saying Nevada’s parents had caused a disturbance.

“The kid is good. He’s great. Really good,” the organizer says in the footage. “He’s very advanced compared to the other ones, so he’s scoring a lot of goals. But he’s pushing the kids ... So, I try to tell him, don’t push; we want to play without pushing, right?”

Nevada’s parents posted a clip of their son at the event in which he can be seen dribbling around older children with ease. The video has since gone viral. Nevada cannot be seen pushing any other children in the footage posted by his parents.

Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'. Allow and continue

“They’re mad at my son because he actually plays soccer. They’re literally kicking him out of this place because he’s good at soccer,” his mother says in the body camera footage. “First, they said he’s not passing, but nobody’s catching the ball when he’s passing.”

The i9 Sports worker told police they were willing to give Nevada’s parents a refund if they left.

“I just want him out. Immediately,” the organizer told police. “Just give me their names so I can give them their refund.”

The Winter Park Police Department said the family agreed to leave the event and no one was arrested.

“The family stated the game was over and they were leaving. The family was cooperative with the officers,” the department wrote in a statement on its website. “No one was arrested, trespassed, or forced to leave the park.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

i9 Sports said it was reviewing the incident and had contacted Nevada’s family.

“We are aware of concerns being shared regarding an incident at a local i9 Sports program, and we take them very seriously,” i9 Sports said in a statement. “The respectful treatment and well-being of every child and family matter deeply to us. We have reached out to the family and have begun a review that includes speaking with those involved. While we work to understand the circumstances, we will not speculate or share unverified information. We appreciate everyone who has brought their concerns to our attention.”

One officer appeared to want to see more of Nevada though. “I kind of want to see him play. I bet he’s good,” he can be heard saying to another officer on body camera.

Sports.title: Kai Rooney scores four goals for Man United U18s as fans all make same demand
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney scores four goals for Man United U18s as fans all make same demand

Kai Rooney left fans purring after netting four goals for Manchester United Under-18s on Tuesday.

The 16-year-old, son of United legend Wayne Rooney, provided some much-needed seasonal cheer at the club with a superb display in the 6-0 win over Burnley.



4 Kai Rooney was in sensational form for Man United U18s against Burnley Credit: Getty

Kai has been in superb form this season as he targets a future breakthrough into the senior squad.

For some United fans, a call-up can't come soon enough for the talented forward following Tuesday’s heroics.

He took just 22 minutes to break the deadlock at Burnley’s training ground.



Kai was quickest to react when Jaume Camacho’s powerful header came crashing off the post to put United in front.

His subsequent knee-slide celebration was just the beginning on what was a celebratory day for the star.



Just four minutes into the second half, Kai kept his cool to convert from the penalty spot after being impeded in the box.

And he didn’t have to wait long to claim his hat-trick when his 63rd-minute looping header found the back of the net.



His fourth arrived just three minutes later when the starlet produced a smart low finish into the bottom right corner.

That was the end of Kai’s torment of the Burnley defence but there was more torture to come for the Clarets as Camacho got on the scoresheet before Noah Ajayi completed the rout.

It was undoubtedly Kai’s standout performance of the season having registered five goals and an assist from just three matches.

4 Kai is up to five goals in his last three games for United's academy sides Credit: Getty



It hasn’t taken long for fans to recognise his potential with some already pitching the idea of throwing him into the first team as early as… this Saturday!

Taking to social media, Fans had a clear message for under pressure United boss Michael Carrick ahead of Saturday lunchtime’s trip to Chelsea – live on talkSPORT.

One fan wrote: “This boy is better than all our forwards.”

Another added: “Play him next match against Chelsea.”

A third demanded: “ Start him on Saturday.”

Another Red Devils fan wrote: “Put him in the first team and get some Rooney passion in the team.”

4 Kai is hoping to follow in the footsteps of dad Wayne at Old Trafford Credit: Getty



Meanwhile one other added: “Carrick you know what to do.”

Carrick uncertainty

talkSPORT reported on Tuesday that Carrick will be given time to turn things around at Old Trafford despite a torrid run of eight games with a victory in all competitions.

The 45-year-old is expected to take charge of the team for the trip to Stamford Bridge despite many claiming his time was up following Sunday’s 3-0 drubbing at home to Bournemouth.

United sit 16th in the Premier League table, just one point from safety with patience wearing thin in the boardroom.

Victory at Stamford Bridge feels obligatory for Carrick even at an early stage of the season.



4 Carrick is on thin ice at United but will take charge of Saturday's match at Chelsea Credit: Getty

However, Carrick faces an uphill battle against Xabi Alonso’s side with his big hitters all misfiring this season.

But United fans are safe in the knowledge that whatever the coming weeks and months bring, the future appears bright with prospects including Kai, Shea Lacey and Harry Amass all impressing in the club’s academy.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz is better without injured Liverpool teammate – and the stats back it up
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz is better without injured Liverpool teammate – and the stats back it up

Andoni Iraola may have finally cracked how to get the best out of Florian Wirtz - and in a way, Jamie Carragher was right all along.

Wirtz was a whisker away from scoring his first Premier League goal of the season on Sunday when his strike in Liverpool's 2-0 win over Brighton deflected off Pascal Gross.



5 Wirtz appeared to have smashed in the opener for Liverpool, but his shot went off Gross for an own goal Credit: Getty

The 17th-minute effort was credited as an own-goal, but it did mark the fourth straight game in which the German was contributing in some way to the scoresheet.

Wirtz came into the match on Sunday off the back of recording three goal contributions in his last three games for Liverpool, matching his tally from his previous 14 matches for the club.

The Brighton win marked his 50th start for Liverpool in all competitions - only Rayan Cherki (16) has more assists from open play for a Premier League club since the start of last season than the 23-year-old (11).



However, the reality is that Wirtz has been questioned for his output since he made his £116million switch to Anfield in 2025.

Liverpool's No.7 was one of only two players, alongside Mohamed Salah, to both score and assist 10 or more goals in each category in Europe’s big five leagues across the last two seasons that preceded his move to Merseyside.



Yet it took until after Christmas for Wirtz to open his account in Red, en route to managing just eight Premier League goal contributions during his debut campaign.

There was an expectation that Salah's exit would see him kick on in his second year, but teething issues under Iraola quickly emerged.



Wirtz particularly found himself under the microscope following the Reds' 3-0 loss to Manchester City before the international break.

The Germany international lost the ball 16 times in the first half and headed away with his country with just one assist in seven games.

Liverpool legend Carragher claimed that Wirtz's role at No. 10 forced Dominik Szoboszlai into a position that does not suit him, and for that reason, Iraola's midfield is not one that can function.

5 Wirtz is currently enjoying his best form in a Liverpool shirt Credit: Getty



As a result, it was suggested that Wirtz would be the fall guy to drop out of the team as opposed to his Hungarian teammate.

Szoboszlai was voted Liverpool's Player of the Season in 2025/26 and committed his future to the club with a new contract this summer.

But injury has restricted him to just 32 minutes across the Reds' last five matches - which has coincided with Wirtz's upturn in form.

Wirtz stats with and without Szoboszlai

The warning signs may have been there when Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal in a 2-1 win over Wolves last December - in a game in which Szoboszlai was serving a one-match suspension.



The latter's only other absence from a top-flight game last season came two months later when he was banned against Sunderland.

5 Wirtz has found himself less on the periphery of Premier League games without Szoboszlai in midfield

Florian Wirtz Premier League (Starts) With Dominik Szoboszlai playing in midfield With Dominik Szoboszlai playing in defence Without Dominik Szoboszlai Games 24 6 4 Minutes 1959 497 310 Goals 3 1 1 Assists 4 1 0 Total Shots 44 8 10 Chances Created 52 12 9 Passes 1219 220 208 Passing Accuracy 84.1% 82.7% 83.7%

Liverpool went on to inflict a first Premier League home defeat of the season on Regis Le Bris’ side in a 1-0 victory.

The Reds had 23 shots on goal – one of which saw Wirtz hit the post - while the playmaker also earned supporters' player of the match.



The upward trend of Wirtz's performances in Premier League games without his fellow midfielder has since continued this term.

He assisted Victor Munoz's strike in the comeback win at Brentford, after Szoboszlai was subbed, having reaggravated his hamstring.

5 Iraola has claimed the media are 'too focused on numbers' in regard to Wirtz - but right now the numbers aren't lying Credit: Getty

Stats from Opta show that Wirtz has had 10 shots, created nine chances and made over 200 passes in the four Premier League matches without Szoboszlai.



On average, that means he takes 0.67 more shots per game without Szoboszlai starting alongside him in midfield (an increase of +36.4%).

His goal rate doubles from 0.13 (1 every 8 games) to 0.25 (1 every 4 games) and he also creates more chances per match as well.

Curiously, Wirtz's Premier League influence was at its worst on average in fixtures where Szoboszlai started from right-back.

Florian Wirtz in Premier League games without Dominik Szoboszlai Liverpool 2-1 Wolves (27/12/25) - Wirtz scores his first Premier League goal Sunderland 0-1 Liverpool (11/02/26) - Wirtz voted Liverpool's Carlsberg Player of the Match Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City (11/10/26) - Wirtz hooked after 66 minutes as Ryan Gravenberch is sent off Liverpool 2-0 Brighton (25/10/26) - Wirtz's effort deflects off Pascal Gross to give the Reds the lead

5 Carragher rightly pointed out that a midfield of Wirtz and Szoboszlai can't function - but recent showings may prove him wrong about which personnel should drop out Credit: AFP



Ian Rush told talkSPORT that people need to be patient with Wirtz, once referred to by Jurgen Klopp as 'a once-in-a-century talent'.

"In a way, he's seeing things maybe too quickly, and people are maybe not making that run, and he's holding onto the ball too much.

"So I think if I was him, I'd sort of say put the ball in the space and let the striker in - you [the striker] should be in that space.

"But I think he's still got a lot to help with Liverpool."

The question for new Reds head coach Iraola is what that help looks like once Szoboszlai returns from injury...

Sports.title: Eddie Howe frontrunner for Man United job but Julian Nagelsmann interested and has key advantage
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe frontrunner for Man United job but Julian Nagelsmann interested and has key advantage

Manchester United have been urged to consider one key factor if when choosing their next manager.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are both in the running to succeed Michael Carrick, if he is sacked by the Red Devils.

3 Nagelsmann is interested in replacing Carrick as United boss Credit: Getty

United's current boss will remain in charge for Saturday's trip to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, live on talkSPORT.

However, pressure is mounting on Carrick amid an eight-match winless run in all competitions.

Nagelsmann 'interested' in United job

talkSPORT understands Howe is currently the frontrunner to replace him in the Old Trafford dugout.

Nagelsmann is also interested and German football journalist Constantin Eckner also claims the former Bayern Munich manager also holds a key advantage over Howe when it comes to the appointment, he has revealed.

Eckner told talkSPORT on Tuesday: "Nagelsmann was already interested in the Manchester United job in the past, but the timing was never really there to join Manchester United, despite them hiring a new manager every 12 months or so.

"The (Christopher) Vivell connection is there, these two know each other and Vivell might be pushing for Nagelsmann."

talkSPORT understands United head of scouting Christopher Vivell is pushing for the club to appoint Nagelsmann.

The pair previously worked together during his time as RB Leipzig boss, with Vivell serving as technical director.

Nagelsmann to 'cost nothing'

As well as his relationship with Vivell, Nagelsmann's contractual status also provides a potential advantage to his hopes of securing the job.

Eckner continued: "As far as I understand it, Nagelsmann would be interested, but he’s not the frontrunner. Eddie Howe is the frontrunner, but Nagelsmann is ready.

3 Nagelsmann would cost nothing to appoint right now, says Eckner Credit: Getty

"The DFB, the German Football Association, bought him out of his contract. So there is no hurdle to take.

"He can join whoever he wants, whilst Manchester United have to pay Newcastle United to get Eddie Howe as their manager right now."

Nagelsmann left his role as Germany head coach in July following their shock World Cup exit.

The four-time winners were beaten on penalties by Paraguay in the round of 32.

His resignation saw the DFB buy Nagelsmann out of his contract, which had been due to run until the end of Euro 2028.

As for Howe, he departed St. James' Park at the end of the same month after almost five years in charge of Newcastle United.

3 United must pay £3million in compensation to appoint Howe Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands United would have to pay the Magpies £3million in compensation if Howe becomes manager.

Whilst it is more than the cost of bringing in Nagelsmann, it represents a lower fee than those for the likes of Fabian Hurzeler and Unai Emery, who have also been linked with the post.

Sports.title: EFL striker wants Bundesliga move after Valencia deal fell through
Sports.content:
EFL striker wants Bundesliga move after Valencia deal fell through

Birmingham City striker Marvin Ducksch is unhappy with his playing time in the Championship and wants to leave St Andrew's.

That is according to German football transfer journalist Florian Plettenberg, who reports the forward is seeking to head back to Germany.



2 Ducksch left Germany in the summer of 2025 Credit: Getty

The 32-year-old has made just seven league appearances this season and not a single one has been a start.

In total, he's played 95 minutes in the Championship this year.

Ducksch has two caps for Germany but is firmly out of favour under Chris Davies.

He came close to joining Valencia in the summer, although the move ended up collapsing.



The 32-year-old does have options in a few countries, but there are no offers on the table as of yet.

Dream move off

With the summer transfer window approaching its conclusion, Valencia made an effort to sign Ducksch.



The deal would have been a loan for the German striker, but it was the Blues who pulled the plug.

Birmingham informed the LaLiga giants there wasn't enough time to complete the transfer.



Valencia picked out Ducksch as an option to cover for Umar Sadiq.

At the point of the deal being negotiated, the striker had appeared for just six minutes in three Championship matches.

2 Ducksch was an important player for Birmingham last season, but he has seen his game time drastically reduced Credit: Getty

The deal fell through due to Valencia delaying their response to the initial offer.

This was due to Ducksch's drink driving conviction, and that delay cost the striker his chance to play in Spain.



Birmingham felt they wouldn't have enough time to sign a replacement.

Ducksch's conviction

In May, Ducksch was ordered to pay £1,000 compensation to two female drivers involved in a serious car crash with the striker.

The 32-year-old pleaded guilty to driving his Mercedes while over the drink drive limit.

The crash happened on Easter Monday following Birmingham's 2-1 defeat to Ipswich, a match Ducksch appeared in.

The forward told Leamington Spa Magistrates’ Court that he was trying to avoid a fallen branch in the road and crashed.



Magistrates handed Ducksch a 14-month driving ban alongside a fine of £16,155, a total of £2,000 in compensation, a £2,000 surcharge and a bill for costs of £85.

The court agreed to allow Ducksch to pay off the total amount of £20,240 at a rate of £2,000 per month.

He was also informed that he was lucky to be alive.

Chairman of the bench John Kiely said: “Thank you very much for your patience while we have been talking about this offence.

“We heard that there was an incident in which two vehicles were clipped.



“We have looked at the photographs (of the damaged cars).

“You can consider yourself lucky first of all that you weren’t killed and secondly that the other drivers weren’t killed.

“That’s how serious this matter is.”

Sports.title: Real Madrid told they made transfer mistake not signing Harry Kane to replace legend
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have been told they missed a trick by failing to sign Harry Kane after Karim Benzema's departure in 2023.

England captain Kane celebrated an historic Ballon d'Or win on Monday evening as he pipped Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to football's most prestigious individual prize.

4 Kane has become just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or Credit: AFP

The Bayern Munich superstar became the first Englishman to lift the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001, capping off an incredible year.

Kane was crowned the world's best player after scoring a stunning 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England combined during the 2025/26 season.

He won the Bundesliga title at club level, breaking endless records as well as lifting the German Cup and German Super Cup, while also captaining the Three Lions to the World Cup semi-finals.

Ballon d'Or glory marked a career-high for Kane, who has soared to new heights since moving to Germany in 2023.

The 33-year-old left boyhood club Tottenham as their all-time record goalscorer three years ago after almost 20 years on their books, and has since scored a staggering 156 goals in 159 outings for Bayern.

But things could have turned out differently, with Kane also eyed up by Real Madrid in the summer of 2023 as a potential replacement for legendary striker Benzema - who left for Saudi Arabia - before opting for the Bundesliga.

Real Madrid's loss?

With Kane the name on everyone's lips, Spanish football correspondent Phil Kitromiledes joined talkSPORT to discuss his Ballon d'Or triumph, and if there was any chance of him conquering LaLiga in the coming years.

The Englishman has been linked with a move to Barcelona as recently as this summer, but Kitromiledes insisted this is unlikely going forward and instead claimed Real Madrid missed the boat in 2023.

Asked about a potential Barca switch on talkSPORT's White and Jordan, he replied: “Possibly not.

“He might have to take a little bit of a pay cut to come to Barcelona. I'm not sure they've got the money to shell out for him at the moment. But yeah, he's a player."

4 Kane has shattered goalscoring records in his three years at Bayern Credit: Getty

4 Benzema won the 2022 Ballon d'Or with Real Madrid and is their second all-time leading goalscorer Credit: Getty

While few would argue with Kane's decision to move to Bayern now, Kitromiledes claimed one option could have suited him even better.

He insisted Kane's similarity to Benzema would have made him the perfect man to succeed the Frenchman at Real in 2023 - with both players hailed for their playmaking abilities as well as goalscoring prowess.

The Spanish football expert continued: “He should have gone to Real Madrid. Real Madrid should have signed him when Karim Benzema left.

“He would have been the ideal player to come in and fulfil that role because he is a brilliant number nine, but he's also a brilliant number ten. As Benzema once said, 'I'm a nine with the soul of a ten, a nine and a half.' And Harry Kane could have done that.

"Obviously, I think that that boat has passed now. But at the time I was saying it and it felt pretty obvious if you want to replace someone like Benzema, go and get Harry Kane.

"It didn't happen, but it's worked out all right for Harry.”

4 Kane's goals fired Bayern to a league and cup double as he scored 61 times for the club last season Credit: Getty

Kane is unlikely to have any regrets over joining Bayern after his Ballon d'Or triumph - his latest milestone in a stellar three years.

Last season, he scored 61 goals in 51 matches across all competitions and won the European Golden Boot with 36 league strikes.

His time in Germany has also seen him end his infamous trophy drought, with Bundesliga glory in the 2024/25 campaign Kane's first career silverware, scooped at the age of 31.

Ironically, the ex-Spurs man pipped a current Real Madrid star in Mbappe to clinch football's top individual prize.

Mbappe finished second in the final rankings despite scoring 58 goals in 60 games in the 2025/26 season, while Lamine Yamal came third.

The Frenchman also won the Golden Boot at the World Cup this summer as France reached the semi-finals, becoming the tournament's all-time top scorer, but failed to winy any trophies.

Sports.title: Jermaine Pennant feared he’d lose his leg in horror dog attack that left him needing 50 stitches
Sports.content:
Jermaine Pennant has admitted that he was fearing his leg would have to be removed after being viciously attacked by a dog last week.

Pennant revealed on Friday that he required more than 50 stitches after a German Shepherd attacked him while on a walk.



3 Pennant has revealed that he feared for his leg after a German Shepherd attacked him and his dog King while on a walk Credit: The Sun

The former Liverpool and Arsenal winger was walking his own dog, King, when the German Shepherd targeted him.

He revealed that he stepped in to help protect King, but the other dog then ended up mauling his leg in reaction.

Pennant had to go to hospital for treatment on his injuries that left him grounded during the horror attack.



And he has now opened up on what was going through his mind during and after the scary incident...

'It all happened so quickly'

"I was holding King back and the next minute my leg..." Pennant explained on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs.



"I just felt this crazy pressure on my leg which then ultimately made me drop to the floor.

"It felt like an eternity, I was shouting: 'My leg! My leg!'

"But by that time, King didn't know what was going on, and then he realised and jumped to my defence.



"That's when the German Shepherd let me go as King was intervening and trying to get him off me.

"But without King it would have just been there thinking it was a toy or something... it all happened so quickly."

3 Pennant was bitten on the leg and it forced him to fall to the ground during the attack Credit: Supplied

Pennant feared for his leg after attack

Pennant went on to explain the aftermath to the attack, revealing that he had to get himself to hospital in a taxi.



"It was a 12-hour wait for an ambulance, so I had to get an Uber to take me to A&E," the 43-year-old explained.

"I called my partner when I was on the floor... I was disorientated, not even explaining where I was but she managed to find where I was and called an Uber on the way and got me in the Uber.

"It was in the middle of nowhere in between a graveyard and a golf course, so I had to find to find my way down the path to the road and jump in the Uber straight to A&E."

He then admitted: "I was fearing for my leg. I knew it was bad, but I couldn't see it because my trousers were stuck to it.



"I just thought: 'This isn't good'. My first thought was 'is King okay' my next thought was I need to get to A&E as soon as possible.

3 Pennant had to get an Uber to the hospital before being treated with 50 stitches, while he may also need a skin graft

"I then got to A&E and they gave me a Tetanus jab straight away and all the necessary antibiotics.

"Tomorrow I have an appointment with a plastic surgeon as one of the wounds, there's a lot of skin gone and it's like a crater, and you can't stitch that as there's no skin to pull it together.



"So they're going to see if it can heal, if not, they're going to have to do a skin graft."

Pennant has been out on a couple of dog walks since the attack and is hoping that the impact of it doesn't affect his life.

He said: "Hopefully there's no lasting damaging. I'll have a scar wound and if it is a skin graft then that will be there for the rest of my life... and my tattoo is ruined!

"I can walk, that's the good news, and there's no pain."

Sports.title: Why there is no early game this Sunday with unique Premier League schedule explained
Sports.content:
Why there is no early game this Sunday with unique Premier League schedule explained

This weekend will see just one Premier League fixture take place on Sunday.

Fans have become accustomed to top-flight matches taking place across two time slots every Sunday as part of the weekly schedule.



3 Arsenal's trip to Liverpool is the only Premier League match this Sunday Credit: Getty

Due to Premier League rules, though, Arsenal's trip to Liverpool at 4.30pm is the only fixture being played on November 1.

It comes after the fixture schedule had to be adjusted in September, two weeks on from the TV selections being made.

Why is there no early kick-off this Sunday?

When the broadcast picks were confirmed through to this weekend in August, Aston Villa vs Fulham was moved to the 2pm slot on Sunday.



The match at Villa Park was selected for live TV coverage by Sky Sports.

However, the clash was later brought forward to an 8pm kick-off on Saturday, October 31.



The move was caused by Villa's involvement in the Champions League, with Unai Emery's side in European action on Tuesday, November 3.

This change was announced on September 1 after the league phase schedule was finalised.



Villa are set to play Barcelona at the Nou Camp on Tuesday, with kick-off at 8pm, live on talkSPORT.

As a result, they could no longer be in league action on Sunday.

Their fixture against the Cottagers was subsequently moved to the rarely seen 8pm slot on Saturday night and will be live on talkSPORT.

3 Villa's home clash with Fulham was originally scheduled for 2pm on Sunday Credit: Getty

This weekend's Premier League fixtures 3pm unless stated Saturday, October 31 Chelsea vs Manchester United, 12.30pm - live on talkSPORT

Bournemouth vs Leeds United

Brentford vs Nottingham Forest

Coventry City vs Sunderland

Hull City vs Ipswich Town

Manchester City vs Brighton

Tottenham Hotspur vs Crystal Palace, 5.30pm

Aston Villa vs Fulham, 8pm - live on talkSPORT Sunday, November 1 Liverpool vs Arsenal, 4.30pm Monday, November 2 Newcastle United vs Everton, 8pm - live on talkSPORT

How often can Premier League clubs play?

The change was in part caused by the Premier League's rules on fixture scheduling.



As well as broadcast selections, European commitments also impact the fixture list after dates and kick-off times are confirmed.

Clubs are given at least two clear days between matches by the Premier League.

The rule prevents sides playing in the Champions League on a Tuesday from playing on the previous Sunday.

3 Villa's fixture schedule was changed due to their Champions League commitments Credit: Getty



This is the case with Villa's home meeting with Fulham following the scheduling of their trip to Barcelona.

The criteria also prevents clubs playing on Thursdays from featuring in the Premier League on the following Saturday.

Teams playing in the Europa League and Conference League are most regularly affected by this.

Matches in both competitions are traditionally played on a Thursday night throughout the season.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk is past his best but still crucial to possible Liverpool title challenge
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk is past his best but still crucial to possible Liverpool title challenge

Virgil van Dijk is essential to Liverpool and their hopes of challenging for the Premier League title - despite his gradual decline.

That's the shared belief of Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist now that the Reds appear to be in contention for the 2026/27 crown amid a strong run of form.



2 Van Dijk is a Liverpool legend, having made 385 appearances and won every major trophy, but is deemed to not be as good as he once was Credit: Getty

Liverpool were 2-0 winners on Sunday afternoon against a Brighton side who, ahead of kick-off, had the joint-best defence in the league with Arsenal on just five goals conceded.

The Reds are fourth in the table on 15 points with eight matches played, and have won six of their last seven matches in all competitions.

Manchester City lead reigning champions Arsenal on goal difference at the top, although a heavy points deduction remains a possibility if their appeal against a guilty verdict on financial rules breaches fails.



Starting in the Liverpool defence for all of their league fixtures so far has been Van Dijk, the club captain who is regarded to be one of the best centre-backs in Premier League history with two titles won.

Now aged 35 and in his tenth season at Anfield, the Dutchman looks to be heading into the final years of his playing career, while the Dutchman is in the final year of his contract, but Stelling and McCoist believe he still has what it takes to excel for Liverpool.



Is Van Dijk past it, or still world-class?

On talkSPORT Breakfast, Laura Kirk-Francis asked if Van Dijk is past his best or can still be part of a team capable of winning titles.

"Is the answer potentially yes to both of those questions?" Stelling questioned. "Because he probably is fractionally past his best, but if I'm looking for a central defender, Virgil van Dijk is still right up there amongst the very best.



"I think he's a leader, an organiser as well, I would love to have him in any of my teams.

"How long he'll go on for is another issue but if Liverpool are to launch another title challenge, it will be with Virgil van Dijk as the rock at the heart of their defence."

In response, McCoist said: "I think you've answered it spot on, Jeff, I really do. I think the answer is yes to both questions.

2 Although Van DIjk is said to be past his best, Stelling and McCoist still believe he is crucial to any title challenge at Liverpool Credit: Getty



"I don't think he's at the peak of his powers and he probably won't get back to that peak again, because you've got to remember where he was.

"Probably one of the best centre-backs the country has ever seen, without doubt. You can talk about the rest of them - John Terry, Rio (Ferdinand) and all those guys.

"Van Dijk, at his peak, was absolutely unbelievable and comparable with those guys, in my opinion.

"So, I don't think he will reach that again, but if Liverpool are going to maintain a challenge in the next few seasons, I would certainly see him in that centre-half position."



Liverpool will be just three points off Arsenal with a win at home to the holders on Sunday, whilst leaders City face Brighton a day before.

However, Andoni Iraola's side are first looking to book a spot in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals as they host Chelsea on Wednesday night, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso is back at Anfield - this is how close he really came to taking the Liverpool job (twice), and why he chose Chelsea instead
Sports.content:
There is a significant chance that this season’s top three Premier League managers will all be products of the same grassroots club in a San Sebastian suburb.

Given what we know about Manchester City's potential points deduction and with apologies to Brighton, the wise money on the top three may well be Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea. That is Mikel Arteta, Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, all 44 years old and all close friends after growing up together in the Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea youth team.

This week, Liverpool boss Iraola will meet both of his former team-mates as Chelsea and Arsenal come to Merseyside. It is the biggest week of his fledgling Anfield career and will shape just how serious the Reds’ ambitions are this season.

But things could easily have played out very differently. There is an alternate reality not too distant from our own where Alonso is Liverpool boss.

When Jurgen Klopp announced his departure in 2024, many expected Alonso to be the next man in at Anfield. He was the instant bookies’ favourite and the popular choice with the fanbase, having spent five years and 210 matches in Liverpool's midfield and been one of the heroes of Istanbul, scoring the equaliser as Rafa Benitez's side came from 3-0 down to beat AC Milan on penalties in the Champions League final in 2005.

Fast forward to early 2026, when Arne Slot was failing to back up his title triumph and his second season was continuing to disappoint, and the noise from supporters was again to hire Alonso. He had been sacked by Real Madrid and was out of work. So how close did he actually get to becoming Liverpool manager?

There's a reality not too distant from our own where Xabi Alonso is the Liverpool manager

Alonso was a club hero at Anfield, playing 210 games in five seasons and scoring the equaliser in the Miracle of Istanbul in 2005

Alonso was certainly admired by Liverpool in the months immediately after Klopp’s resignation, but both parties insist nothing was ever as advanced as it might have seemed from the outside.

Klopp's bombshell announcement came in the middle of Alonso's stellar season at Bayer Leverkusen, in which he won the Bundesliga and German Cup unbeaten. He was keen to stay for another year in Germany, while Liverpool had pivoted to other candidates including Slot, Ernesto Valverde (another Basque) and then-Sporting Lisbon boss Ruben Amorim.

Perhaps there is something about the Basque identity that prompts its favourite sons to do things differently. Alonso took himself out of contention for jobs at Liverpool and Bayern Munich that summer, and Iraola quit Bournemouth this year without having another job lined up because he felt he had completed all his objectives on the south coast.

When Slot was failing this year, the conversations internally at Liverpool weren't about Alonso. For months, the word from the Anfield hierarchy was one of support for the Dutchman. Sources close to Slot insisted he was planning to continue in his post up until around two days before the official announcement of his exit.

In stalling their decision to sack Slot, Liverpool missed out on Alonso, who decided to join Chelsea in early May. Living in London appealed to him, as did having a young squad and no European football this year, allowing him more time on the training pitch.

‘It was about the timing,’ Alonso told his former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher in an interview last week. ‘For me it was the right time after Leverkusen, after Madrid. I had my time off and I wanted to choose to have a good connection, a good feeling about where to go.

‘And I knew Chelsea. I had no link but what I heard, what they had, the potential was here, few things could change. And I thought that we could start the journey together. I had a feeling that the base of the squad was very good.’

Regardless of being the Chelsea manager, Alonso will receive a rousing reception on Wednesday – just as he did in late 2024 when his Real Madrid side came to Anfield and were outplayed by Slot's Liverpool in a 2-0 win for the Reds.

When Jurgen Klopp (left) announced his Liverpool exit in 2024, many expected Alonso to be the next manager at Anfield, while the Reds took too long to decide when Arne Slot (right) departed

Living in London appealed to Alonso, as did having a young Chelsea squad and no European football this year to give him more time on the training pitch

Iraola can also pick Alonso’s brain on how to get the best out of Florian Wirtz and Jeremie Frimpong, both of whom joined Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen last year. Wirtz scored 34 goals and assisted 35 across Alonso’s two full seasons in charge.

And don’t forget to watch out for the reception Jordan Henderson gets if he plays. Liverpool's former captain received a standing ovation when he returned to Anfield for the first time with Brentford last term.

This fourth-round tie is not all pomp, catch-ups and happy-clapping, though – it is a significant game for both Alonso and Iraola.

With no European football for Chelsea this year and Liverpool seen as a work in progress (a view that will change should they beat Arsenal on Sunday), getting one over their old pal represents both managers' easiest route to silverware.

Sports.title: Morgan Gibbs-White becomes latest Premier League player to have his house BURGLED: England star's fiancée 'incredibly unsettled' by raid on Nottinghamshire home
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White's partner has said that she feels 'incredibly unsettled' after the couple's house was burgled a few days ago.

It is the latest incident in a string of Premier League footballers' burglaries, with Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes having suffered a similar incident while he was in Italy for his club's Champions League game against Como last week.

Britney De Villiers, who lives with the England and Nottingham Forest midfielder and their two children in Nottinghamshire, issued the statement on Instagram in an attempt to warn others to remain alert.

She wrote: 'I wasn’t going to publicly share this but our home was burgled a few days ago and after hearing about another one since, I feel it’s important to just warn others.

'It’s incredibly unsettling knowing that homes are being targeted.

'Please be extra vigilant, make sure your security systems are on whether you’re in the house or not and report anything suspicious.

'Thankfully, nobody was home when it happened and material things can be replaced but it’s a horrible feeling knowing someone has violated your home, especially when you have young children.

'Please stay safe and look out for one another.'

Daily Mail Sport have contacted Nottinghamshire Police for comment.

Morgan Gibbs-White and his fiancee Britney De Villiers' house was robbed while the couple were away a few days ago (Source: britneydevilliers/Instagram)

Gibbs-White's fiancee Britney De Villiers issued the statement on Instagram in an attempt to warn others to remain alert (Source: britneydevilliers/Instagram)

The Nottingham Forest and England star shares two young sons, Greyson and Hayes, with fiancee De Villiers (Source: britneydevilliers/Instagram)

Gibbs-White and De Villiers reportedly met in 2019, before getting engaged in June 2025. They have two young sons, Greyson and Hayes.

Last week, United midfielder Fernandes' house was raided by burglars while he and his wife, Ana Pinho, and their two young children were away from their luxury £4million property in Nether Alderley.

Three thieves struck at around 8.30pm before making off with designer jewellery and other expensive items.

The 32-year-old flew back with the United squad straight after a 4-1 defeat in Como and arrived home in the early hours of the morning.

The intruders were said to have been in the house for around five minutes before police arrived after being alerted by a neighbour who spotted them acting suspiciously in the back garden.

It’s understood that the house backs on to woods and the burglars jumped over the fence before breaking in, despite the Fernandes having installed CCTV and a high-tech alarm system.

A spokesman for Cheshire Police said: ‘At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

‘The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property. Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects.

Last week, United midfielder Fernandes' house was raided by burglars while he and his wife, Ana Pinho, and their two young children were away (Source: anaapinho/Instagram)

‘However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.’

Detective Inspector David Jarvis, of Macclesfield Proactive CID, told The Sun: ‘This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we’re committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

‘As part of our enquiries, we’re keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.’

Criminal gangs have been known to prey on the Cheshire homes of football stars when they are playing away with their clubs.

They include a number of United and Manchester City players including Paul Pogba, Victor Lindelof, Jesse Lingard, Ruben Dias and Joao Cancelo.

Sports.title: Man United fans see their owners for what they are. They see their greed and their acquisitiveness. Man City fans are still in denial about theirs: OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Man United fans see their owners for what they are. They see their greed and their acquisitiveness. Man City fans are still in denial about theirs: OLIVER HOLT

Oliver Holt Chief Sports Writer

It is usual, in days of disillusion and crisis at a football club, when results are bad and the league position is heading south fast, for the manager to be the lightning conductor for dissent and anger. It is he who takes the brickbats and suffers the abuse and listens to the chants demanding that he give up the fight.

‘We hope you die soon,’ the front cover of a Southampton fanzine shouted at the club’s then manager, Ian Branfoot, in 1993. And if that is extreme, the sight of planes flying above grounds with a banner proclaiming ‘WengerOut’, or similar, has long become part of the supporters’ armoury of resistance.

Not on Sunday. Not at Old Trafford. After Manchester United lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth and sank to 16th in the Premier League table, the home fans did not turn on Michael Carrick. They turned on the players but most of all, they turned on the club’s hated owners, the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

They turned on them because they know that the owners, much more than Carrick, are responsible for the depths to which a once great club has sunk, both on and off the pitch. They turned on them because the debt they saddled the club with when they bought it in 2005 has now grown to over £1.15billion.

They turned on them because that debt has cost United £852million in interest payments. In the last financial year, the interest payment was £37m, an increase from £34m the previous year. They turned on them because the club has declared war on its own season-ticket holders in its bid to increase the number of tourists and day-trippers spending money at Old Trafford.

At various points during the match, fans were given updates about the plans for a new stadium but those were met with derision, too. Many loyal United fans think the new stadium, and the prices they will be asked to pay to sit in it, are just another way of driving them out of the club so they can be replaced by shinier, happier people with bigger wallets.

On Sunday, the Manchester United fans turned on the players but most of all, they turned on the club’s hated owners, the Glazers, including Avram (left), and Sir Jim Ratcliffe

The fans detest the owners because they know that they are responsible for the depths to which a once great club has sunk, both on and off the pitch

United fans see their owners for what they are. They see their greed and their acquisitiveness. They see through the homilies about how much the fans mean to the club.

We know what you are, they have been saying to them for many years. They have said it with protests and with banners. They said it on Sunday with chants and anger.

These are dark days for Manchesterism in football. If United fans have seen through their owners, City fans, who are trying to come to terms with the fact that their owners have been found guilty of cheating on an industrial scale between 2009 and 2018, are not quite there yet. Maybe one day, when the legal process has played out fully, they will feel it, too.

Many are still in denial about what the emirate of Abu Dhabi has done to their club. That is understandable. Abu Dhabi has pumped money into City, not taken it out.

Abu Dhabi has overseen an incredible period of success in east Manchester, winning the league title an unprecedented four times in succession, compared to United’s failures.

But the reality for both sets of supporters is stark. United have been hijacked by corporate leeches whose model is said by financial experts to be the ‘aggressive utilisation of debt financing secured against high-value, cash-generative assets to fund acquisition and expansion’. United are the Glazers’ cash-cow.

City have become a plaything for a petro-state. They have become one of the world’s most high-profile sportswashing projects and one of the most effective, as Abu Dhabi has sought to sluice away the reputation of its repressive regime with the beautiful football of Pep Guardiola and the series of golden triumphs he delivered.

For now, Abu Dhabi brief about ‘irrefutable evidence’ they possess in their pursuit for justice from the Premier League. They are said to be ‘bullish’ about their chances of success in their appeal.

United fans have seen through their owners, but City supporters are not quite there yet

City have become a plaything for a petro-state. They have become one of the world’s most high-profile sportswashing projects

The UAE wields immense wealth, power and influence. No one can be sure of what the appeal findings will be. But let’s get something straight here: don’t let City’s owners and the aggressive public relations campaign they have mounted fool you into thinking they are the good guys in any of this.

The idea, propagated brilliantly by some Abu Dhabi acolytes, that the modern City are somehow a champion of the oppressed in the Premier League, fighting against the tyranny of some imagined ‘red cartel’, might be a clever ruse but it is also laughably ridiculous.

Abu Dhabi’s defenders want to couch this battle as Harry Potter versus the Dark Lord but even a fool can see it’s not like that. City want dominance. They are not here for altruism.

They are not here to spread the love. And they have achieved dominance. Their four successive titles earlier in this decade was a level of rule that no club has ever achieved in the long history of the English game.

What do you think would happen if the Premier League got rid of the Squad Cost Ratio controls that some present as the yoke of the dictator, designed to keep smaller clubs in their place? Do you really think Aston Villa would have a chance of winning the league in seasons to come? Or Everton? Or Spurs? No chance of that. None at all.

The imagined ‘red cartel’ would be replaced by a very real nation state cartel. Abu Dhabi (Manchester City) or Saudi Arabia (Newcastle United) would win the Premier League every season. No one else could get remotely close to the level of spending facilitated by their public investment funds. The Premier League would be finished as a spectacle.

City wanted to join the European Super League, don’t forget. City, under Abu Dhabi, are not anti-establishment. They are the establishment. They have stripped ambitious, proud mid-table clubs like Everton and Villa of their best players time and again over the last 20 years. Red cartel? Please. Do me a favour.

City's owners have cost the club its reputation for a very, very long time to come. Other fans do not forget. The stain of ‘cheats’ is not an easy thing to wash away

Manchester United has been twisted out of shape until it is unrecognisable

And City have been found guilty of doing all that by cheating. By being, according to some metrics, the biggest cheats in the history of English football. Abu Dhabi are only custodians of Manchester City and they have cost the club its most valuable asset.

They have cost it its reputation for a very, very long time to come. Other fans do not forget. The stain of ‘cheats’ is not an easy thing to wash away.

This is English football now. This is what we are. This is what the modern game has done to football’s idea of Manchesterism.

It has taken Manchester United and Manchester City and it has given it owners that have twisted those clubs and tortured them out of shape until their fans stare at them long and hard and do not recognise what their clubs have become.

Sports.title: England legend Jimmy Anderson takes on new cricket challenge in ITALY just days after retirement announcement amid fury from Lancashire members
Sports.content:
Jimmy Anderson is throwing himself into T10 franchise cricket – as co-owner of Napoli Knights in an unlikely new Italian tournament starting next month.

Less than 24 hours after a tense meeting at Old Trafford, where members expressed their anger at Lancashire’s recent decision not to renew his contract for 2027, it emerged that Anderson and former county team-mate Luke Sutton were joining forces for the Italia T10 competition.

Italy took part in this year’s T20 World Cup in South Asia, briefly giving England a scare at Kolkata’s Eden Gardens before losing their group game by 24 runs.

And Anderson insisted: ‘There’s a huge opportunity to help raise the profile of cricket in Italy. Of course, we want Napoli Knights to be competitive and challenge for the title, but we also want to contribute to something that continues to grow well beyond the tournament itself. I can’t wait to get involved.’

Teams from Bologna, Florence, Milan, Naples, Rome and Venice will play all their games in Rome over 12 days from November 18. The competition founder, former Surrey batsman Nadeem Shahid, said: ‘I played against Jimmy and Luke enough times to know how competitive they are, so having them as owners of the Napoli Knights is a massive statement for Italia T10.’

The news comes after Lancashire members challenged the club’s incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace – who joined the meeting via video link from his holiday in the USA – over the decision to let Anderson go, despite taking 50 championship wickets at just 17 each this summer.

Jimmy Anderson is throwing himself into T10 franchise cricket as co-owner of Napoli Knights

Farbrace made it clear he took full responsibility for releasing Anderson, and won some sceptical members over by saying he was motivated by building a team capable of winning the county championship in the next four years.

The club will look into arranging a possible farewell event for Anderson after one member pointed out that fans had been denied the chance to say goodbye. Whether he will be in the mood to play ball is unclear.

Meanwhile, South Africa were dismissed for 329 by Australia on a topsy-turvy opening day of the third and deciding Test at Cape Town. Having been asked to bat, openers Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman put on 158, before the hosts collapsed from 203 for one to 232 for six.

Then, after Ryan Rickelton and Marco Jansen added 95, Mitchell Starc took the last four wickets in six balls to finish with six for 72.

Sports.title: Man United chiefs have been struck by paralysis and indecision again. By not putting Michael Carrick out of his misery, they are letting another season go to the dogs, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
Were the reputation of one of our great football clubs not being traduced and one of its great servants not being so diminished, then you might say there was something laughable about the dithering and indecision of the geniuses currently running Manchester United. Michael Carrick spent three hours at the club's training ground on Monday, watching the Under 21s play, while somewhere across the complex, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox were putting their heads together about whether to sack him or not. No word was forthcoming as darkness fell – not the remotest sense that Carrick was wanted, or appreciated, or that the wagons were being circled around their man. Just pictures of these vastly overpaid executives driving home in their high-powered vehicles. United fans had nothing but guesswork to go on until Carrick arrived back at Carrington just before 8am on Tuesday morning, wearing a Manchester United tracksuit. So, after 48 hours of uncertainty, we are told that Carrick is to continue. People are talking about his chance to ‘turn the season around’ though no one has actually stated the fact and we now know all too well that United bosses – people somehow deemed competent to dictate the direction of this proud football club – are not so sure he can. Wilcox is an Eddie Howe man, apparently. Christopher Vivell, United's head of recruitment, has a leaning for Nagelsmann, architect of Germany's disastrous World Cup, as they worked together at RB Leipzig. Michael Carrick is not the man to lead United out of the wilderness. That much is written all over his face

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

United supporters aren’t buying either one of those candidates and, more through sympathy for one of their legends than conviction in his management, applauded Carrick from the field after the indignity of a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday. That support apparently didn’t go unnoticed by the United front office staff and it seems to have precipitated the latest drift. The same paralysis and indecision which led Sir Jim Ratcliffe to allow Erik ten Hag to blindly blunder on, two years ago, is being visited on supporters all over again. Carrick is not the man to lead the club out of the wilderness. That much is written all over his face, in the pained and melancholic air he’s been giving off as the side he leads have tanked. But Berrada and Wilcox are incapable of intuiting the fact. Just as they are incapable of seeing that a dressing room smells a manager’s weakness, knows when he is mortally damaged, is alive to the way the ego merchants are successfully spinning against him in the public realm. Carrick carries so much United history into that training ground – five Premier League titles and a Champions League trophy – yet Bruno Fernandes, the weasel, will have been able to look him right in the eye on Tuesday morning, knowing that he has mortally damaged him and emerged intact. It would have been gratifying to have heard, in a statement bearing the name ‘Manchester United Football Club’, that Fernandes is to be fined several weeks’ wages for his vicious little digs at Carrick, including the Instagram post – laughably, about ‘loyalty’ – which he ‘liked’ as Carrick’s future lay on the line, on Monday. It would have been gratifying to have heard, in another message put into the public sphere, that Berrada and Wilcox believe in their man and have his back. Instead, we will have Carrick the lame duck in the Stamford Bridge dugout on Saturday lunchtime. A placeholder, we must assume, until United secure Howe or Nagelsmann or Antonio Conte or any other of the dismally pedestrian names who will condemn United to more of these infernal, ever-decreasing circles. Of course, the solution to all of this resides way beyond the imagination of cheapskate Ratcliffe and his executive stooges. United, as we argued on Monday, require a manager with the kind of clout, class, gravitas which Carlo Ancelotti, the Godfather of management, would bring. It would have been gratifying to have heard, in a message put into the public sphere, that Jason Wilcox (left) and Omar Berrada believe in Carrick and have his back. But no There was no sense on Tuesday that Carlo Ancelotti had been approached by Berrada or Wilcox and entreated to give up a Brazil international posting The reaction to that Daily Mail Sport piece underlined the depth of United fans' wish for Ancelotti. ‘Could it happen?’ many asked us. There was no sense on Tuesday that Ancelotti had been approached by Berrada or Wilcox and entreated to give up a Brazil international posting which is heading nowhere to succeed where so many others have failed at one of the great European clubs. Ancelotti is a proud man and flattery might have worked. We may never know. Carrick will probably survive the games against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa which precede the next international break but few will be betting on him still being there at the other side of that interval, when the trip to Liverpool arrives. It feels like another season is being sacrificed – games just given away and, needless to say, the dithering authors of all this, Berrada and Wilcox, will sail on through it all, untouchable and immune to the latest catastrophe.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's rivals spark conspiracy theories over 'orchestrated' Ballon d'Or win: Lamine Yamal's uncle says it's 'not right' as Real Madrid legend Guti questions legitimacy of beating Kylian Mbappe
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's rivals have sparked wild conspiracy theories in the wake of the England captain's historic Ballon d'Or win - with supporters of fellow favourites Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe hinting that there had been behind-the-scenes machinations to rig the voting. The Bayern Munich striker - who returned to his club this morning - became the first Englishman to win football's ultimate individual honour in 25 years, since Michael Owen claimed the prize in 2001. All the more special was that the 33-year-old - who bagged a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season - was able to do so in front of a home crowd, with the France Football event relocating from Paris to London for the first time since its founding 70 years ago. But despite Kane's mammoth contributions to football making him a worthy winner, those who might have backed his closest rivals Yamal and Mbappe were quick to seek alternative explanations as to why their favourites had lost out. Real Madrid legend Guti suggested that the change of venue had played a large part in the timing of Kane's honour. 'It just so happens that, for the 70th anniversary, they move the ceremony to London and someone from London wins it,' the former Los Blancos claimed on Spanish panel show El Chiringuito. 'It's an incredible coincidence that they move it to London and someone from London wins it, isn't it? ‼️ Ballon d’Or Winner @HKane is back in Munich 👋 pic.twitter.com/yNSHjY29Bu — FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) October 27, 2026 Wild conspiracy theories have been swirling in the wake of Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win (pictured after touching down in Munich) Those who believe that Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe should have received the top prize have suggested foul play behind the scenes Lamine Yamal came away the winner of the Young Talent of the Year but might have preferred a more significant honour 'I mean, it's as if everything is…' he deliberately trailed off, before another member of the panel suggested the word 'orchestrated'. 'Completely. Absolutely. That's what I think, and it's what I've thought about this award for a long time,' Guti added, before bafflingly citing Kane's surprise at having been named the best footballer in the world as further evidence in favour of his theory. 'I'm telling you, when I saw the look on his face when they announced Harry Kane, he never in his life thought he was going to win it,' he continued. 'Never. I think he expected both Lamine Yamal and Mbappe to finish ahead of him. 'You only have to look at his face.' The decision to move the legendary French event to London as a one-off was made to pay tribute to the award's first ever winner, Sir Stanley Matthews. The Stoke City icon's family were present at the event and featured on the red carpet. Yamal's uncle Abdul entered the fray to defend his nephew, claiming that the teenager should have won the honour and making a dig at Kane in the process. Speaking to Cadena SER in the immediate aftermath of the announcement, he stressed that 'my nephew was fantastic, he was the best player in the world.' Real Madrid legend Guti (left) was one to draw a spurious connection between Kane's heritage and the London venue of the event While Yamal's uncle Abdul fiercely defended his nephew on Cadena SER after he missed out 'Everyone knows it. If you love football, you go to see Lamine, not Harry Kane,' he added. 'Lamine is very young, he's 19, he'll win more, but Harry only has three days of competition left and they give him the Ballon d'Or. 'Lamine has won a World Cup, La Liga, and the Super Cup. He plays very well. He's had an incredible season. He scores goals that no one else scores. Passes, assists, he has it all. He'll win five Ballon d'Or awards.' Instead, Yamal won the Young Talent of the Year award for a staggering third consecutive year. When asked cheekily by co-host Thierry Henry if this was the award that he really wanted, Yamal was politely bashful, noting that he believed that the honour belonged to his Barcelona and Spain team-mate Pau Cubarsi. While Kane's triumph was won on merit rather than skulduggery, France Football editor in chief Vincent Garcia confirmed that the voting had been incredibly tight between the English star and his closest competitor Mbappe. 'This year, there were several serious contenders,' Garcia said. 'The two closest were the top two, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe, and the race between them was decided by very little. 'The points gap between Kane and Mbappe was smaller than the gap between Rodri and Vinicius in 2024, which was 41 points - and that was already a very narrow margin at the time.' Amid speculation Kane focused on celebrating in London with his partner Katie Goodland Early in the evening Ousmane Dembele and Mbappe were accused of not showing Kane significant respect The 33-year-old went on to dance the night away at upscale club Cirque Le Soir on Monday But by Tuesday lunchtime, he was back in training as Bayern Munich prepared for their midweek DFB-Pokal fixture Kane was pictured picking up congratulations from coaching staff and fellow players alike

Your browser does not support iframes.

'I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote. Kylian led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points.' So hard-fought was the battle between the players that there appeared to be a touch of sour grapes in the immediate aftermath. Footage from inside the London Palladium showed French superstars Mbappe and last year's winner Ousmane Dembele failing to stand to shake Kane's hand after he had accepted the top prize. But Kane brushed off any suggestions of tension between rivals as he went on to celebrate his win at nearby nightclub Cirque Le Soir. Former team-mates and colleagues including Eric Dier, Tim Sherwood, and James Maddison joined the jubilant party at the upscale hangout, where Kane and his wife Katie Goodland were treated to a parade of Champagne bottles and sparklers. With training on Tuesday in Munich however, Kane went easy on the alcohol in preparation for a return to the pitch with Bayern against Magdeburg on Wednesday evening.
