Sports.title: More radio problems vex Verstappen: “‘Maybe we should use sign language’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed he had yet more problems with his radio during the United States Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver suffered serious disruption to his pit-to-car communications when he won the previous round in Singapore. He said the radio fault in Austin was “not the second time” it has happened this year.

“It’s already, I don’t know how many times this year,” he said. “Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It’s probably cheaper as well.”

“It’s a disaster. It’s really frustrating, to be honest.”

Verstappen qualified second in Austin but fell to third place in the race as he struggled with his car’s balance. During one radio exchange Verstappen admitted he did not know how to change his front wing angle at his next pit stop.

Afterwards he said Red Bull had not been especially strong or weak anywhere at the Austin track.

“We are balanced as a car,” he said. “We are not the fastest in high-speed, we’re not the fastest in low-speed, and I think maybe here you either need to be very fast in high-speed or you need to be the quickest in low-speed.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“When you’re none of it, you’re just a little bit average, and I think we were just a little bit average in the race.”

However he does believe there was potential for Red Bull to perform better last weekend.

“Of course, if we chose different tyres, probably we could have maybe been second, but that’s always easy to say afterwards. Plus, when you have too many issues with the consistency of your power unit, then that already costs you free lap time.

“So it’s normal that you can’t execute everything to the limit or at least be at your best. There are still a lot of things that we need to look at and do better.”

Sports.title: Antonelli was “concerned” by threat from Verstappen’s early pit stop in Austin | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was concerned to see rival Max Verstappen make an early pit stop in the United States Grand Prix.

Verstappen committed to a two-stop strategy early in the race, pitting on lap 14 for a second set of soft tyres which meant he would have to come in again. Mercedes delayed Antonelli’s first pit stop but the tactics paid off as he was able to reach the end of the race with a single tyre change.

However Antonelli admitted he was “a bit concerned in the beginning” when he stayed out after Verstappen’s pit stop. “But we were able to extend and actually the pace came back with the medium, and we were able to extend without losing too much time.

“So then, as you know, after doing the first stint on the medium, we were like, ‘Oh, right, we’re going to go for one-stop.’ And the hard, to be fair, felt very robust, so I felt pretty confident to go all the way to the end.

“I just didn’t know how much management was required, but it was good, and the car felt very good today.”

Verstappen saved two sets of soft tyres from qualifying which appeared to give him a strategic advantage before the race began.

“We didn’t have much choice, to be fair,” said Antonelli. “We didn’t have any new softs, so the new medium was the only choice we really had, or the hard.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But the medium was not amazing. I think today the best tyre was the hard, just because it was the most resilient tyre. It was quite surprising because in recent races the soft has always been probably the best tyre. So it was a good surprise, and luckily it worked for us.”

Antonelli scored Mercedes’ first win since it introduced a major upgrade for its W17 in Malaysia. He said there is still room for improvement with the car.

“In some places, I would say it’s still not [delivering] as much as we expected, but in other places it is delivering very well,” he said. “I think in the high- and medium-speed [corners] the car is very strong. The balance is good.

“We’re still struggling a little bit in low-speed with front locking. But overall, I feel like the package is finally starting to deliver, and we’re starting to see the results and the improvements from the package.”

Sports.title: Adam Azim Risks IBF Title Shot Against Gabriel Valenzuela
Sports.content:
Adam Azim’s reported fight against Gabriel “Gollaz” Valenzuela is a dangerous test for a contender whose knockout streak has moved faster than his résumé. Azim can punch, but he remains largely untested against fighters with Valenzuela’s experience at the top end of the 140-pound division.

Azim and Valenzuela are set to meet on December 4 at London’s Copper Box Arena in a 12-round IBF junior welterweight eliminator, The Ring reports. The bout is expected to headline a Boxxer-promoted card, with the winner hoping to fight for the vacant IBF title in the first half of 2027.

Valenzuela’s losses to Subriel Matias and Lindolfo Delgado in 2025 could lead some to dismiss him as an opponent who falls short when the stakes rise. That overlooks what he brings against Azim. The Mexican contender has shared the ring with two established fighters at 140 and carries enough power to punish mistakes.

Azim (15-0, 12 KOs) has stopped his last six opponents, most recently Steve Claggett in the third round on May 30. His streak also includes wins over Sergey Lipinets, Ohara Davies, Kurt Scoby, Enock Poulsen and Franck Petitjean.

Those victories have built Azim’s profile, but they haven’t established how he’ll respond if a dangerous opponent takes his shots and makes him fight under pressure. Lipinets and Davies were recognizable names, but neither represented the kind of peak contender Azim could face if he wins a world title.

Valenzuela (32-5-1, 18 KOs) returned from his defeats to Matias and Delgado by stopping Rogelio Laguna in May. His knockout record doesn’t suggest he’s the most devastating puncher in the division, but Azim can’t afford to assume his own power will end the fight before Valenzuela has a chance to land.

The question is what happens if Azim’s early speed and combinations don’t settle matters. Against a more experienced opponent, he may have to manage distance for 12 rounds, defend after throwing, and take shots without losing his composure. His previous wins haven’t given fans a clear answer about how he’ll handle that kind of fight.

The IBF title picture remains uncertain after Delgado failed to travel to Riyadh for his scheduled vacant-title fight against Arthur Biyarslanov. It’s unclear whether that bout will be rescheduled. The Ring reports that the Azim-Valenzuela winner will hope to fight for the belt, rather than guaranteeing that the winner will get the opportunity.

A convincing win would be a significant step for Azim and could bring him closer to a future domestic fight with WBC champion Dalton Smith. But that’s a conversation for later. First, Azim has to get past an opponent who has fought at a level he has yet to reach.

If there is a spot on Azim’s resume where the wheels could come off, this is it. Azim looks like a world-beater when guys freeze in front of him or let him dictate the tempo with his hand speed. Steve Claggett usually brings relentless pressure, but he walked straight into Azim’s kitchen and got dismantled early.

Sergey Lipinets and Ohara Davies had recognizable names, but neither guy had the legs or the work rate left to make Azim uncomfortable. Azim has essentially been having target practice against stationary or faded opposition.

Valenzuela is a completely different proposition. He is durable, he knows how to survive rough patches, and he carries genuine power. More importantly, he has shared the ring with Subriel Matias and Lindolfo Delgado. When you have stood in the pocket with punchers like that, nothing Azim throws is going to shock you.

The real question mark around Azim has always been his defense and composure when things stop going his way. He tends to admire his work after firing combinations, he pulls straight back with his chin in the air, and he has not had to prove he has a world-class chin of his own. If Valenzuela eats his early shots, marches through the fireworks, and lands a heavy counter in rounds four or five, we are going to find out immediately what Azim is made of.

If Azim gets dragged into the trenches and has to fight off the back foot with a bruised face and an empty gas tank, he could easily get unraveled. It is the first time he faces someone who will not care about the hype and will still be throwing bombs in the second half of the fight.

Sports.title: David Haye Spots Moses Itauma’s Costly Mistake
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma’s loss against Filip Hrgovic revealed a clear development problem. He showed the speed to control the early action, yet he had never learned to pace himself under elite heavyweight pressure. David Haye points directly to that pacing problem as the young contender plans his comeback.

Haye wants Itauma to analyze his own energy output before pointing fingers. The former two-weight world champion sees a situation similar to his 2004 defeat to Carl Thompson, where early aggression led to late exhaustion.

“The first five rounds he was amazing,” Haye noted on talkBOXING. “Even in those first five rounds, did he need to throw as many shots as he did to win the rounds comfortably? When I lost to Carl Thompson, I didn’t think I need a new coach. That was the last thing. It was like, ‘coach said this, I did that. I got my a kicked.’”

Haye rebounded from that early loss to collect cruiserweight belts before winning a heavyweight title, proving that an early defeat can sharpen an elite talent. The parallel highlights an uncomfortable reality for Itauma. Early knockouts generated a lot of hype, yet those quick finishes never forced him to survive against tough situations.

However, Haye’s situation after his loss to Thompson was entirely different than Itauma’s. Haye made that low-output style work because the terrain allowed it. At cruiserweight, Jean-Marc Mormeck was tailored for him, and Enzo Maccarinelli folded early. When Haye moved to heavyweight, Nikolai Valuev was a slow, static target who threw almost nothing back.

Haye spent twelve rounds running laps, threw about twenty punches a round, landed one late hook that rocked the giant, and walked away with a belt. The moment he ran into Wladimir Klitschko, a disciplined fighter with a real jab who refused to walk into traps, Haye spent twelve rounds on the back foot landing single-digit punches and complaining about a broken toe.

That blueprint does not translate to the current heavyweight division. Today’s landscape is loaded with massive, six-foot-six punchers who impose physical pressure. Itauma cannot jog around the ring against guys like Zhilei Zhang, Agit Kabayel, Hrgovic, or Joseph Parker, throw twelve punches a round, and expect to survive or get the decision.

A heavy, explosive heavyweight cannot rely on smoke and mirrors. When heavy muscularity clashes with a high-tempo pressure fighter, the tax gets paid quickly.

Haye correctly holds the fighter responsible, yet Ben Davison’s corner also deserves a look. If his fighter expended excessive energy while controlling the action, the corner needed to pull back the throttle. Both trainer and pupil need a shared view of those tactical lapses, whether their partnership continues or not.

Recent sightings at Floyd Mayweather’s gym alongside Shakur Stevenson and Zaquin Moses have sparked speculation. Neither camp has confirmed a split from Davison, meaning the Las Vegas trip might just be a temporary training stint.

Frank Warren floated a four-fight slate for 2027. Stacking up appearances only helps if matchmaking forces Itauma out of his comfort zone.

Blowing away overmatched foes could rebuild bruised confidence, but soft touches will leave basic developmental flaws unresolved.

Sports.title: Abel Sanchez Urges Vasiliy Lomachenko to Stay Retired
Sports.content:
Abel Sanchez believes Vasiliy Lomachenko should stay retired, even with the lure of a final undisputed championship run hanging out there. The veteran trainer points directly to age and inactivity as major red flags, making clear he would urge the Ukrainian maestro to reconsider any planned return.

Lomachenko, now 38, aims to campaign at super featherweight, viewing unified champion O’Shaquie Foster as his route toward all the belts. Charly Suarez remains in the mix as a potential test run, though nothing is official.

“I would try to dissuade him,” Sanchez said to Fight Hub TV when asked how he would advise someone in Lomachenko’s shoes. “I would obviously support any kind of decision like that, but I would do my best to point out all the pitfalls and the negatives of it. Obviously, there’s a lot of positives to it, too. But you’re not talking about him fighting for the undisputed at 38. You’re talking about at 40.”

Sanchez doubts the promotional gears can turn fast enough for Lomachenko’s timeline. Foster holds three major titles at 130 pounds, which leaves another belt holder to negotiate with down the line before a full coronation can happen.

Beyond scheduling headaches, Sanchez worries a late loss could tarnish Lomachenko’s legacy. He cited Sugar Ray Leonard’s painful defeat to Terry Norris in 1991 as a cautionary tale of what happens when legends stay too long.

That comparison stretches things a bit. Dropping a decision to Foster at 38 after sitting out wouldn’t undo what Lomachenko built. Most observers understand the physical tax of Father Time. Besides, there is real honor in targeting elite champions rather than milking tune-ups against soft touches.

The real question centers on what Lomachenko has left in the engine. His trademark side steps, pinpoint timing, and sudden angle changes rely on elite reflexes. Reflexes slip quickly when age catches up, and prolonged breaks outside the ropes only muddy the waters further.

Suarez offers a genuine gauge if that bout gets made. The Filipino contender shares the same birth year at 38, yet his gritty display against Emanuel Navarrete proved his engine is intact. A victory there gives Lomachenko far more honest feedback than beating up a designated fall guy.

Sanchez argues Lomachenko needs exactly that type of litmus test before hunting world titles. It has little to do with appeasing ringside spectators. The fighter himself needs an honest self-assessment before walking into deep waters.

“If he wants to do it and his heart is in it, go ahead,” Sanchez said. “But I would love to see a tune-up fight, not for us to gauge him. Forget us, for him to gauge himself.”

Sports.title: Can Canelo Alvarez Still Beat Elite Pressure Fighters?
Sports.content:
No one knows whether Canelo Alvarez can still beat an elite pressure fighter. At 36, he hasn’t faced an opponent who combines high-level ability with the sustained attacking style Christian Mbilli is expected to bring.

Their October 31 fight will test whether Alvarez can still use his counterpunching and power to slow down an opponent who keeps coming. Mbilli, the WBC super middleweight champion, will try to make Canelo fight at a pace he hasn’t faced in years.

Some believe Mbilli is made for Canelo because he can plant his feet and counter the WBC champion. But that view is based on what a younger Canelo did against fighters who weren’t at the elite level. Trying to do that now at 36 against one of the best pressure fighters he has faced in over a decade it going to be difficult.

11 years ago, James Kirkland tried to take the fight to Canelo in 2015 and was knocked out in the third round. Kirkland was not elite or anywhere close to that. Journeyman Alfredo Angulo also came forward in 2014, but he was too slow to avoid punishment and was stopped in the tenth. Those were impressive wins for Alvarez, yet neither tells us how he will handle Mbilli more than a decade later.

Those fights showed that Canelo can beat lower-level pressure fighters, but it doesn’t say anything about what he can do against an elite-level fighter. He’s also a lot older now, and nowhere near the youth he had when he fought those guys.

Gennadiy Golovkin was a much higher-level opponent, but his approach was different from Mbilli’s. In their first fight in 2017, the 35-year-old Golovkin worked behind his jab and picked his moments to throw hard punches. Many fans thought he deserved the victory, although the judges scored the fight a draw. In the rematch, Golovkin was 36 and spent much of the contest boxing rather than applying nonstop pressure.

Miguel Cotto chose to box Canelo, working behind his jab rather than trying to overwhelm him. Dmitry Bivol chose to move in and out and land combinations to beat Canelo.

Berlanga finally put it on Canelo late in their 2024 fight and had some success. The trouble was that he’d spent too much of the fight waiting and had already fallen behind.

Mbilli won’t likely give Canelo that kind of time. When Alvarez gets tired, his output drops, his face turns red, and he starts taking more punches. He’ll have chances to counter Mbilli, but what happens if the champion walks through those shots and keeps throwing? That’s something the 36-year-old Canelo hasn’t had to deal with in a long time.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Haney Chase Ends With Raymond Muratalla Order
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson’s long wait for a major payday has left him facing a fight he may not find commercially appealing. The WBO has ordered its 140-pound champion to negotiate a mandatory defense against Raymond Muratalla, a dangerous opponent who offers far less name value than Devin Haney.

That is the cost of spending months chasing a fight that never came together. Stevenson has not boxed since taking the WBO title from Teofimo Lopez on January 31, and his split with Zuffa Boxing has left him searching for a promotional arrangement as a free agent.

The WBO’s order gives Stevenson and Muratalla 20 days to reach terms. President Gustavo Olivieri said the championship committee unanimously ordered negotiations to fulfill the outstanding mandatory obligation. He said the formal notice would be issued shortly.

“Please be advised that the WBO World Championships Committee has unanimously resolved to order the commencement of negotiations between WBO Jr. Welterweight World Champion Shakur Stevenson and WBO #1 World-Rated Contender Raymond Muratalla, in fulfillment of the outstanding mandatory championship obligation,” Olivieri said. “The parties shall have 20 days to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations.”

Top Rank had petitioned the WBO to install Muratalla as the mandatory challenger. Now Stevenson must decide whether a defense against him fits his plans and whether the two camps can agree on financial terms.

Stevenson spent much of the year pursuing Haney, a bigger name who would have offered a far larger event. But those talks failed, and Haney has moved on to a planned fight with Liam Paro. The WBO order leaves Shakur with a less glamorous opportunity, but one that could get him back in the ring.

Muratalla is the kind of challenger a champion might prefer to face after building momentum, not after nearly nine months of inactivity. The former IBF lightweight champion gave up his belt at 135 to pursue a chance at 140. He can apply pressure and throw enough punches to make Stevenson work, even if Shakur’s speed and accuracy make him the favorite.

The financial side could be difficult. Stevenson has talked about wanting major purses, but Muratalla doesn’t have Haney’s drawing power. A promoter would have to decide how much the matchup is worth, while both fighters seek terms they consider acceptable.

If they cannot agree, a purse bid could follow, though the WBO’s formal notice should spell out the procedure. Stevenson could also choose another direction rather than defend, but he has not said he intends to vacate.

That distinction matters. The order is a test of whether a deal can be made, not proof that Stevenson wants to avoid Muratalla. Still, giving up the belt without defending it would leave him with a long layoff and one less title to offer a future opponent.

Stevenson’s win over Lopez gave him a valuable position at 140. A defense against Muratalla would give him a chance to use it, end the inactivity, and add another quality victory while the bigger fights remain uncertain.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Oleksandr Usyk vs. Vitali Klitschko | FANTASY FIGHT
Sports.content:
What happens when the two most dominant Ukrainian big men in modern prizefighting history collide across 15 grueling championship rounds?

In the fifth installment – and the very first heavyweight edition – of our Fantasy Fight series here at Rummy’s Corner, we examine an ultimate dream matchup: two-division undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk squaring off against former long-reigning WBC heavyweight titlist “Dr. Ironfist” Vitali Klitschko.

Under our standardized neutral ground rules, both fighters enter the squared circle at their absolute physical and tactical peak, competing under unified rules with modern 10-ounce gloves, day-before weigh-ins, and tested across the classic 15-round championship distance. On paper, it pits Usyk’s sublime lateral movement, rapid angles, and relentless southpaw volume against Vitali’s towering 6-foot-7 frame, awkward leans, and suffocating punch output.

Yet, when put to the test across our boxing communities, this dream heavyweight collision ignited one of the most passionate and polarized debates in the history of the series.

To Usyk’s supporters, his peerless conditioning, agile footwork, and surgical combination punching present an impossible stylistic puzzle. Having already proven his ability to disarm and systematically outbox modern super-heavyweight giants, proponents believe Usyk’s continuous feints, angles, and relentless second-half pace would drag the bigger man into deep, uncomfortable waters.

However, writing off Vitali Klitschko in mythical head-to-head territory is dangerous ground. Boasting an iron chin, an 87% knockout ratio, and a resume where he was never knocked down and rarely lost a round, “Dr. Ironfist” was an immovable force of nature. If Vitali establishes his long range-finder jab, dictates the distance, and imposes his crushing 245-pound frame, he could turn the contest into a claustrophobic nightmare for any moving target.

Can Usyk tame the giant with fleet-footed wizardry, or does Vitali break him down over the championship haul?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner breaks down the tactical mechanics, community debate, and official scorecards. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Tests What Canelo Alvarez Has Left
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli in Riyadh with sharp questions hanging over what remains in the Mexican superstar’s tank. Veteran boxing insider Dan Rafael views Alvarez’s mileage, ring age, and recent outings as unmistakable signs that the veteran is drifting further from his peak.

Rafael argues that a prime Canelo would have systematically broken Mbilli down. Heading into Saturday, however, Mbilli brings youth, stamina, and relentless pressure, making the outcome far harder to forecast.

“A lot younger. He’s fresher. I mean, it’s a crapshoot at this stage of Canelo’s career,” Rafael said on About Boxing. “This is the type of guy that in his best days he would completely pick apart and probably just do damage to for 12 rounds or maybe stop him. But the reality is Canelo hasn’t had a stoppage in a long time.”

Rafael pointed to Canelo’s defeat against Terence Crawford alongside his decisions over Jaime Munguia and Edgar Berlanga as clear proof of decline. Alvarez turned pro at 15, and more than two decades in the ring have built up heavy wear and tear.

Canelo hasn’t stopped an opponent since halting Caleb Plant in 2021. While he has managed to keep winning most nights, the emphatic dominance that fueled his run to the top of the sport has largely vanished.

When a fighter has one flat performance, people call it an off night. When it stretches across four straight outings as we’ve seen with Canelo in his last four fights, it is an unmistakable pattern. The public senses it, which explains why the energy around this Riyadh card feels muted.

Mbilli’s relentless work rate presents a serious operational hurdle. Canelo can still punish mistakes off the back foot, and Mbilli’s aggression will present openings. Yet it remains uncertain whether Alvarez can match that output and maintain his gas tank across 36 minutes against a hungry titleholder.

Surviving Mbilli is step one. An emphatic showing keeps Canelo primed for another lucrative main event. Turki Alalshikh could look toward Hamzah Sheeraz next, a fight Alvarez could handle comfortably. It seems doubtful anyone will push him into the ring with a destructive puncher like Osleys Iglesias anytime soon.

A disputed decision on the cards might protect Canelo’s status contractually, but it would hammer his standing with fans. If observers feel Mbilli got robbed, friendly judges will not quiet Rafael’s warnings about the veteran’s fading reflexes.

Mbilli also carries pressure into the ring, looking to rebound after battling Lester Martinez to a draw on the Canelo Crawford undercard. Both enter this meeting off identical layoffs.

Rafael declined to pick the outright upset. Still, he expects Saturday to deliver a clear verdict: Canelo either proves he still belongs at elite championship caliber, or the final bell on his career draws noticeably closer.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury’s 10-Fight Plan Could Lead to More Losses
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury already has his eyes on the future, tossing out the idea of signing another 10-fight contract once his current deal wraps up. That talk might hit a brick wall fast if Anthony Joshua takes care of business on December 11 in Cardiff.

A rough beating at Principality Stadium would leave the 38-year-old stuck in no-man’s-land, stuck weighing genuine ring threats against matchups nobody wants to pay to see.

Walking away does not seem to be anywhere on Fury’s radar. He has walked away and come back enough times that even a lopsided loss might not force his exit.

“I’m going to continue,” Fury told WSVN Miami, brushing off exit talk. He mentioned having two bouts left on his current deal before adding, “I’ll finish the contract off and then probably sign another 10-fight deal. Who knows?”

The Gypsy King tossed in a reality check, noting the cash must make sense and the schedule needs to move fast given his age.

That is a wild roadmap for someone who has logged 39 pro outings, survived a brutal three-bout war with Deontay Wilder, and dropped consecutive decisions to Oleksandr Usyk. He grabbed comeback wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach earlier this year, but Joshua delivers power on a whole different level.

A bad knockout loss would trigger alarms that go way past whether he can hang with top-tier champions. Depending on the damage taken, even a hungry fringe contender who brings steady heat, works the body, and presses the action could become an unnecessary hazard.

Fury spent his prime dominating with slick movement, massive reach, and smothering upper-body weight. Those attributes fade in a hurry when reaction times dip against fresh heavyweights. Joshua owns the raw dynamite to reveal exactly how much punch resistance Fury has left when shots start landing clean inside.

The Fury brand will always sell tickets at home. British fans backed him through long layoffs, fake retirement posts, and the Usyk defeats. A tune-up bout against an easy touch would pull numbers in the short term.

Selling a full ten-rounds against soft touches is an entirely different hustle. The Wach bout worked as a quick warm-up. Stacking up multiple dates against fading veterans or clear underdogs will simply drain fan interest.

Promoters will cut checks as long as Fury wants to put gloves on. The real headache will be finding guys he can handle without boring the crowd to tears.

Ghana News.title: Full statement: Wontumi’s reflections from prison
Ghana News.content:
RE: CHAIRMAN WONTUMI'S REFLECTIONS FROM PRISON - CALLS FOR DEDICATED PRISON HOSPITAL, CONJUGAL VISITATION, AND TOTAL REFORM

Following my consistent visits to Chairman Bernard Antwi Boasiako (Chairman Wontumi) since his remand on July 20th, 2026, I wish to share his full reflections on the state of Ghana's prisons and his humble appeal for urgent reforms.

Chairman Wontumi notes that his incarceration has been a period of deep reflection. He has had first-hand interaction with prison officers, inmates, and the conditions under which the Ghana Prison Service operates - a system he says has seen little structural improvement since 1962.

He emphasizes that "Not all prisoners are prisoners" and that our correctional system must move from punishment to true reform, welfare and productivity.

His detailed observations and appeals:

Prison Officers' Welfare and Pay

Calls on government to urgently review pay, accommodation and conditions of service for prison officers. Dedicated Prison Hospital

No dedicated, well-equipped prison hospital, no ambulance, no standby generator in many prisons. Seriously sick inmates with terminal illnesses including tuberculosis are managed under difficult conditions. He calls for construction of a dedicated, ultra-modern Prison Hospital for all facilities, and in the interim, emergency linkage with 37 Military Hospital and Police Hospital. Classification of Inmates

Minor offenders sleep with armed robbery convicts. Persons on trial for treason and terrorism are mixed with ordinary inmates - a security risk. Youth, Defilement and Behavioural Concern

Majority are young men 18-35 years for defilement cases. He observes that due to prolonged incarceration and lack of counselling, these cases often end up engaging in same-sex activities and becoming gays and lesbians within prison. Calls for proper classification and counselling. Family and Conjugal Visitation

Calls for a dedicated private area for spouses and children to visit. It is the prisoner who is in prison, not the children or spouse. Regulated visitation for love and intimacy will reduce tension, preserve marriages and aid reformation. Overcrowding and Infectious Diseases

Inmates with tuberculosis sleep with healthy inmates. LGBTQI+ Management

Calls for clear policy direction on LGBTQI+ classification. Prison Agriculture

Service has vast lands and skilled labour but only one tractor for food and garbage. Pleads with Ministry of Food and Agriculture to support prison farms. Justice Sector Collaboration

Regional Prison Commanders should be included in jury and justice deliberations because "the real job begins after judgement." Infrastructure

Since 1962 little investment apart from pure water production. Calls on government and private sector to build ultra-modern facilities and factories. Parliamentary Involvement - Key to Reform:

Chairman Wontumi makes a special appeal to Parliament of Ghana for these changes to happen. He calls on:

1. The Speaker of Parliament to lead the conversation on prison reform as a matter of human rights and national development.



2. The Majority Caucus and Minority Caucus to work together in a bipartisan manner to pass a new Prison Reform Act, approve budgetary allocation for a dedicated Prison Hospital, ambulance service, generators, and agricultural equipment.



3. The Parliamentary Select Committees on Defence and Interior, Health, and Food and Agriculture to pay working visits to prisons across the country to see conditions firsthand.

He believes that without Parliament - Majority and Minority working together with the Speaker - the needed legal and budgetary reforms cannot happen.

Continental Lesson

African prisons must change - even the name must change. Ghana can lead Africa.

“At this experience since July 20th till date, prison doesn't reform as it should be. I pray that the entire Africa will learn from Ghana."

Appeal:

Chairman Wontumi respectfully appeals to the Speaker, Majority Leader, Minority Leader, Attorney General, Chief Justice and Government to prioritize prison welfare.

He remains in high spirits.

Signed:

Dr. Palgrave Boakye-Danquah

Spokesperson to Chairman Wontumi

Ghana News.title: Ghana developing first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security – Osman Ayariga
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is developing its first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security to strengthen young people’s participation in conflict prevention, peacebuilding and national security, Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, has announced.

Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment at the ECOWAS Ministerial Consultation on Youth, Peace and Security in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Ayariga said the initiative reflects Ghana’s commitment to giving young people a meaningful role in shaping peace and security policies.

He said young people must be recognised not only as beneficiaries of peace and security interventions but also as partners in developing and implementing solutions to challenges confronting their communities and the sub-region.

Mr Ayariga said the proposed action plan would provide a framework for strengthening youth participation in peacebuilding and conflict prevention, while supporting efforts to promote stability and security across West Africa.

Ghana News.title: No extension for manufacturers: EPA on January 1, 2027 styrofoam and single-use plastics ban
Ghana News.content:
The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has rejected calls by local manufacturers and importers for an extension of the January 1, 2027 deadline for the nationwide ban on polystyrene foam (styrofoam) products and selected single-use plastics.

Speaking at a stakeholder engagement session in Wa, the EPA’s Chief Executive Officer, Professor Nana Ama Browne Klutse, said the policy would be enforced as scheduled despite concerns from businesses about investments made in machinery, equipment and raw materials.

“We have engaged producers, manufacturers, and importers of styrofoam products. Their concern is that they want some extension of time so that they can recoup some of the investment they have made in their machines, equipment, or raw materials,” Prof. Klutse said.

“However, we have informed them that we cannot. They are making their profits at the expense of the environment, our health, and our properties,” she added.

The ban follows an announcement by President John Dramani Mahama during the 2025 World Environment Day observance. It targets products including takeaway food packs, foam mattresses, ceiling panels and roofing insulation.

Prof. Klutse urged Ghanaians to adopt sustainable alternatives, including carrying personal food containers, using reusable plates and wrapping traditional meals such as waakye and tuo zaafi (TZ) in plantain or banana leaves.

Providing further details on the scope of the ban, the EPA’s Director of Sustainable and Circular Economy, Larry Kotoe, said polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic bottles would be excluded from the immediate ban because of their distinct polymer structure and recycling potential.

He said the Authority would, however, target single-use thin polythene bags commonly known as “coco rubbers” as part of its efforts to eliminate single-use plastics.

“Once you serve food in a coco rubber, you can't use it again; the next thing is it gets thrown away,” Mr Kotoe said.

He added that the bags would be banned from next year as part of the single-use plastics elimination strategy.

Mr Kotoe also warned food vendors against wrapping hot food items such as kenkey in thin plastic film before boiling or wrapping them in leaves. He said environmental officers would confiscate materials that do not comply with the policy.

To support implementation, EPA management is working on a reward system to encourage compliance at the district level. The Authority is also developing a structured take-back collection system to channel recyclable PET plastics to specialised processing plants.

The EPA said the nationwide campaign was being funded through its internally generated funds (IGF).

The Authority’s Director of Risk and Strategic Management, Sydney Kwaku Danso, said the prohibition of imported styrofoam materials was already being enforced at key entry points in collaboration with the Ghana Revenue Authority’s Customs Division.

Speaking on behalf of DSP Abdul-Rahman, Sergeant Gabriel Akornor said security personnel were prepared to enforce compliance when the deadline takes effect.

“We will be at the borders with Immigration. If you say you haven't heard and you try to bring it out, police officers will meet you in the middle of town,” Sgt. Akornor cautioned.

“We are there to protect lives and property, and if you refuse to protect your own life, we will force you to protect it. We urge our rich importers: stop importing these items and start bringing in healthy alternatives,” he added.

The Deputy Director of the Upper West Regional Coordinating Council (RCC), Tonsuglo Alhassan, who delivered a speech on behalf of the Regional Minister, Charles Lwanga Puozuing, pledged the region’s support for the policy.

“Protecting our environment is a shared responsibility and an essential condition for sustainable development. The convenience of styrofoam comes with environmental costs that require urgent action,” Mr Alhassan said.

He added that the RCC, together with municipal and district assemblies, would support the implementation of the ban and public education efforts.

Mr Alhassan also described the phase-out as an economic opportunity for young Ghanaian entrepreneurs to develop alternatives such as paper-based packaging, bamboo products, glass bowls and sugarcane-bagasse tableware.

The Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) also expressed support for the ban, with Juliana K. Toboyee, an officer of the Ministry’s Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRSD), highlighting the harmful effects of plastic pollution on agriculture.

Ms Toboyee said MoFA would use its agricultural extension networks to educate farmers on the ban and the proper disposal of agrochemical containers to promote a safer agricultural environment.

As the January 1, 2027 deadline approaches, the EPA is expected to continue its nationwide public education campaign, urging citizens, traders and institutions to adopt environmentally friendly packaging alternatives.

Ghana News.title: SAWA Program: Newage begins training of first cohort of ‘urban bluers’
Ghana News.content:
Newage Agric Solutions Ltd. has held the first hands-on field training for participants in its Urban Blue initiative, under the Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program at the Saletso Industrial Hub at Okwenya in the Eastern Region of Ghana, marking a new stage in their preparation to establish home-based catfish production businesses.

The training combines practical catfish production exercises, business guidance, and safeguarding education to prepare young women for home-based aquaculture enterprises.

Held on October 15, 2026, the training brought together the first cohort of female participants known as Bluers, who had completed the initiative’s online learning course. The sessions moved beyond theory, giving participants practical exposure to catfish production, tank assembly, water management and stocking density, alongside business guidance and a session on Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion.

Led by Mr. Ken Nelson, the practical aquaculture sessions covered feeding practices, water management, identifying signs of fish illness and determining appropriate stocking density based on tank capacity. Participants also worked in teams to assemble and fix their tarpaulin fish tanks, determine appropriate water levels and stocking density.

The exercise gave the Bluers an opportunity to practice tasks they will need to undertake when they receive their starter packages and establish their own production units at home. It also encouraged teamwork, shared problem-solving and peer learning. Beyond the practical demonstrations, Newage’s General Manager, Mr. Martin Tettey Nartey, facilitated a business-focused session that introduced participants to considerations involved in turning their aquaculture skills into a livelihood.

The program also included a tour of Adwenepa Hub, another initiative under the SAWA Program, and Saletso’s cereal processing unit, where Evivi Foods products are produced, including a Tom-Brown processing site.

The visit exposed participants to food processing and the wider possibilities of value addition within agribusiness. A Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion session led by Ms. Berlinda Sarfoa Owiredu addressed respectful conduct, safe and inclusive environments, and how participants can raise concerns and seek support if they experience or witness unsafe behavior.

For Gariba, one of the Bluers, the practical experience was particularly significant. She shared that she had joined the initiative despite initially disliking catfish because she wanted to challenge herself to try something new. Although she had doubts at the beginning, she said the hands-on training had helped ease her fears and strengthened her willingness to commit to the business as her own.

About SAWA Program

The Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program is a four-year national initiative of the Mastercard Foundation in partnership with Agri-Impact Ltd spanning 2026 to 2030, designed to address systemic constraints while unlocking inclusive economic opportunities within the aquaculture sector. The Program is a women-centred initiative that seeks to unlock 60,000 dignified and fulfilling jobs for young women aged 18–35 years, including 3,000 young women with disabilities, across the aquaculture value chain i.e. tilapia and catfish.

The SAWA Program is being implemented in collaboration with a consortium of strategic partners, including Newage Agric Solutions Ltd.

About Urban Blue Initiative

Through its Urban Blue initiative, Newage seeks to support women aged 18–35 who are interested in establishing homebased catfish production businesses. Selected participants receive training, technical support and a starter package comprising a tarpaulin fish tank, juvenile catfish and fish feed. Before attending the physical training, they complete an online course covering catfish production and foundational business concepts. According to Newage, the initiative received over 1,000 applications. Applicants were assessed against the program’s selection requirements, and successful candidates were organised into cohorts for training. The first cohort’s field training marks an important step in Urban Blue’s rollout, with further cohorts expected to follow.

Ghana News.title: AHSAG calls for stronger accountability in Free Primary Healthcare implementation
Ghana News.content:
The Association of Health Service Administrators, Ghana (AHSAG), has called for stronger administrative coordination, accountability and resource management to ensure the successful implementation of the government’s Free Primary Healthcare programme.

The Association says the initiative’s success will depend not only on policy and funding but also on effective planning, logistics, maintenance and supervision at health facilities. It has also raised concerns about staff discipline, financial management systems and the sustainable funding of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund.

The concerns were outlined during AHSAG’s 49th Annual General Conference and Continuing Professional Education programme, in Tamale, Northern Region.

The Association of Health Service Administrators, Ghana (AHSAG), Rev. Ezekiel Amadu Daribi, said health service administrators must be actively involved in planning and implementing healthcare policies to improve service delivery.

“Involve Health Service Administrators in programme planning, implementation, resource allocation and relevant decision-making structures. Implementing facilities should receive the administrative capacity and operational resources needed to deliver the programme. AHSAG stands ready to contribute its expertise in administration, transport, estates, supply chain and technical support services,” he said.

AHSAG seeks role in Free Primary Healthcare implementation

AHSAG commended the government for introducing the Free Primary Healthcare (FPHC) programme, describing it as an important step towards improving access to essential healthcare and advancing Universal Health Coverage.

However, the Association cautioned that the programme’s effectiveness would depend on the capacity of health facilities to manage resources, coordinate services and maintain the infrastructure required for quality healthcare delivery.

It called on the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service, development partners and other stakeholders to involve health service administrators in programme planning, implementation, resource allocation and relevant decision-making processes.

The Association said its members had the expertise to support the programme in areas including administration, transport, estates management, supply chain operations and technical services.

Calls for stronger staff discipline

The Association also expressed concern about misconduct among some healthcare workers, warning that negligence, absenteeism, lateness, abandonment of duty and breaches of patient confidentiality could undermine public confidence in health institutions.

It urged health service administrators, hospital administrators, facility heads and other managers to strengthen supervision, attendance monitoring, duty-roster compliance and staff performance management.

AHSAG further called for regular staff education on professional ethics, confidentiality, patient rights and customer care.

It stressed that alleged breaches should be addressed consistently and fairly, in accordance with applicable rules and due process.

Rev. Amadu said maintaining discipline and professionalism was essential to protecting patients and improving the quality of healthcare services.

Concerns over GIFMIS role assignments

The Association also called on the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service and the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to review role assignments under the Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS).

According to the association, some health service administrators and pharmacists have reportedly not been assigned system roles that correspond with their approved responsibilities.

AHSAG warned that incomplete or unclear role configurations could disrupt established workflows and weaken coordination within health institutions.

“AHSAG calls on the MoH, GHS and the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department to review the relevant

GIFMIS role configurations against approved responsibilities and financial controls. The review should identify the specific functions affected and ensure that authorised officers have the access needed to perform their duties, subject to segregation of duties, approval limits and applicable financial management requirements” he said.

Ghana News.title: Uganda Airlines begins scheduled flights to Accra
Ghana News.content:
Uganda Airlines has commenced scheduled commercial flights to Accra, introducing a new travel option between West and East Africa and raising prospects for improved regional connectivity, trade, investment and tourism.

The Ugandan national carrier began operations at the Accra International Airport on October 27, 2026, with four-times-weekly services linking Entebbe, Lagos and Accra.

The new route is expected to provide travellers with an additional option in a market served by established airlines, while potentially intensifying competition on airfares between the two African regions.

Speaking at the inaugural flight ceremony, Managing Director of the Ghana Airports Company Limited, Yvonne Nana Afriyie Opare, said the airline's entry into Ghana's aviation market demonstrates the country's growing appeal as a destination for aviation investments.

“The arrival of Ugandan airlines in Ghana represents a significant milestone in the growing relationship between the two countries. Beyond expanding travel options for passengers, this new service is expected to enhance connectivity, stimulate tourism and culture, facilitate trade and strengthen economic cooperation between Ghana and Uganda”, she said.

She noted that the development reinforces Ghana's position as a strategic gateway for regional and international air travel.

Chief Executive of Uganda Airlines, Girma Wake, said the airline's operations in Ghana would strengthen air connectivity between West and East Africa, making travel between the regions more accessible.

The service is also expected to facilitate business travel and create opportunities for stronger commercial relationships between Ghana, Uganda and other markets along the route.

Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe reaffirmed government's commitment to investing in aviation infrastructure to strengthen Ghana's position as a preferred destination for international travel.

He said continued infrastructure development would be important in supporting growth in the aviation sector and improving the country's competitiveness as an aviation hub.

Uganda Airlines' entry into Ghana comes amid broader efforts by African aviation stakeholders to improve intra-continental connectivity and reduce reliance on indirect journeys through European and Middle Eastern hubs.

Limited direct air links between African countries have long been identified as a constraint on regional trade, tourism and business integration.

The new service adds to the available connections between West and East Africa, with the potential to improve travel convenience and expand opportunities for businesses and travelers.

The launch marks another development in Ghana's efforts to attract aviation investment and strengthen its role in connecting African markets to one another and the rest of the world.

Ghana News.title: GRASAG president joins World Bank-backed Africa development conference in Italy
Ghana News.content:
The World Bank Group has invited the President of the Graduate Students Association of Ghana (GRASAG), Richard Class-Peters, to participate in an international conference in Italy focused on skills development, job creation and Africa's economic growth.

Mr Class-Peters is expected to join the second edition of the Africa Growth and Opportunity – Research in Action (AGORA) conference, scheduled for October 26 to 27, 2026, in Palermo, Italy.

The invitation was extended by Nancy Lozano Gracia, Head of the World Bank Group's Rome Center.

The conference, held under the theme “Building Skills for Africa's Home-Grown Development,” will bring together policymakers, researchers, think tanks, private-sector leaders and development partners to explore how research can inform policies that expand employment and economic opportunities across the continent.

Discussions will focus on the mismatch between the skills acquired through education and training and those required by employers, an issue that continues to affect graduate employment and workforce development across Africa.

According to the World Bank, many businesses struggle to find workers with the technical, digital and management skills they need, while graduates face difficulties securing jobs that match their qualifications and competencies.

Mr Class-Peters' participation could provide an opportunity for graduate students' perspectives to feature in discussions on how African countries can better align tertiary education with labour-market demands.

The conference will also examine ways to expand employment opportunities in sectors such as energy and agribusiness while preparing young people for changes in the workplace driven by artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Focus on skills and job creation

The World Bank says Africa's working-age population is projected to increase by more than 450 million by 2040, placing greater urgency on efforts to create jobs and equip young people with relevant skills.

Against this backdrop, AGORA seeks to bridge the gap between research, policymaking and implementation by bringing together stakeholders to identify practical approaches to Africa's development challenges.

The discussions are expected to explore how governments and businesses can translate investments in education, skills training and economic development into productive employment.

For Ghana, the conference could offer an opportunity to highlight challenges facing postgraduate students and young graduates, including the transition from university to employment and the need for stronger links between academic training and industry.

It could also provide opportunities for exchanges with policymakers, researchers and development partners on approaches to entrepreneurship, workforce development and job creation adopted in other African countries.

The two-day conference will take place at the historic Palazzo dei Normanni in Palermo, bringing together participants from across Africa and beyond.

Mr Class-Peters' participation would place graduate representation within broader discussions about the future of work and the policies needed to ensure that Africa's growing workforce can contribute to and benefit from the continent's economic transformation.

Ghana News.title: Spain gives NACOC €300,000 to complete first forensic laboratory
Ghana News.content:
The Government of Spain has provided €300,000 in financial support to the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to facilitate the completion of its first forensic laboratory.

The funding is intended to strengthen the Commission’s investigative and prosecutorial capabilities, particularly in the fight against illicit drug trafficking and transnational organised crime.

The Spanish Ambassador to Ghana, Ángel Lossada, announced the support during a brief ceremony to present the package to NACOC management, reaffirming Spain’s commitment to strengthening security cooperation between the two countries.

He said Spain was prepared to deepen its collaboration with Ghana through capacity building, specialised training and technical assistance to support efforts against drug trafficking and organised crime.

The Ambassador disclosed that the Spanish Government was stepping up cooperation with Ghana, either through the European Union Security and Defence Partnership or through the negotiation of bilateral agreements with the Ministry of the Interior.

He also pledged support for the training of forensic officers to ensure the effective operation of the laboratory once it is completed.

Receiving the support, NACOC Director-General, Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, expressed appreciation to the Spanish Government for its continued partnership and commitment to strengthening Ghana’s fight against drug trafficking.

He described the funding as timely, noting that the establishment of a modern forensic laboratory had been one of his key priorities since assuming office.

According to him, the absence of a dedicated forensic laboratory has posed a major operational challenge for the Commission, particularly in investigating and prosecuting drug-related offences.

He explained that NACOC currently depends on other state institutions to conduct forensic examinations, a situation that often delays the receipt of laboratory results and the prosecution of cases.

Major General Mantey said completing the laboratory would enable the Commission to conduct forensic examinations more promptly, strengthen investigations and improve the prosecution of drug-related offences.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
