World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro's passports cancelled after he fails to surrender them
World.content:
Police in Brazil say they have cancelled the passports of the defeated right-wing presidential candidate, FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, after he failed to comply with an order to surrender the documents.

On Monday, the Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to hand his passports over to police within 24 hours as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering, which he denies.

At the time, Bolsonaro said he had no plans to leave the country, and insisted that he would stay in Brazil to lead the opposition to his left-wing rival, President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva.

However, the deadline has passed without the senator surrendering the passports, prompting speculation he may have left the country.

Federal officers are checking border crossings to establish if Bolsonaro may have travelled to neighbouring Argentina, according to a police source consulted by BBC News Brasil.

However, Argentine authorities have told the BBC there is no record of Bolsonaro entering their country through any border crossing.

Bolsonaro was already under investigation for alleged corruption over the financing of a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of plotting a coup and is under house arrest.

In addition to that investigation, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered police on Tuesday to probe FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro's electoral campaign over alleged foreign funding.

The 45-year-old senator suffered a stinging defeat on Sunday when he was beaten by Lula in a presidential run-off, which Bolsonaro had been widely expected to win.

World.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
World.content:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.

The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".

After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.

The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.

Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", StÃ¸re said.

Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.

The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".

StÃ¸re added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."

The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.

He - like Stubb and StÃ¸re - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.

World.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
World.content:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday.

Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.

Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

There are concerns that the truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity."

Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, Kyiv believes, with only 1,700 still living in the city itself.

Before the war it was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape is highly dangerous because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.

No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water for three years.

World.title: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist jailed in Algeria
World.content:
Gleizes, who contributes to French magazines So Foot and Society, travelled to Algeria in May 2024 to report on Jeunesse Sportive de Kabylie (JSK), one of the country's best-known football clubs.

It is based in Tizi Ouzou, about 100km (62 miles) east of the capital Algiers, in the mountainous Kabylie region, which is mainly home to the ethnic Amazigh people (historically known as Berbers).

It is also the base of the Movement for the Self-Determination of Kabylie (MAK), which Algeria designated a terrorist organisation in 2021.

Gleizes was accused of possessing publications deemed harmful to national security.

The case centred on his contacts with a JSK official who was also associated with the MAK.

Reporters Without Borders (RSF), which has campaigned for his release, says the exchanges took place in a journalistic context and that some contacts predated the outlawing of the group.

During his appeal hearing last December, Gleizes acknowledged mistakes in his reporting and said he should have applied for a journalist visa rather than entering Algeria on a tourist visa.

"I beg your mercy so that I can be reunited with my family," he told the court.

Prosecutors argued that he had not travelled to Algeria to carry out journalistic work, but to commit a hostile act.

The Algerian authorities have yet to commented on the decision by the Ballon d'Or, which is organised by France Football magazine in partnership with European football governing body Uefa, to dedicate the ceremony to Gleizes.

RSF has announced a solidarity football match for 11 November, marking Gleizes's 500th day in detention, as part of its campaign calling for his release.

Former France internationals Robert PirÃ¨s and Vikash Dhorasoo, along with Paris Mayor Emmanuel GrÃ©goire, are among the first participants announced.

Gleizes's case comes amid wider concerns over the prosecution and imprisonment of writers and other public figures in Algeria.

Franco-Algerian writer Boualem Sansal was sentenced to five years in prison for undermining national security before receiving a pardon from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune following mediation by Germany's president in 2025.

Gleizes's arrest also came during a period of heightened diplomatic tensions between France and Algeria, marked by the withdrawal of ambassadors and reciprocal expulsions of diplomats.

Relations deteriorated further after France recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara in July 2024. Algeria supports the pro-independence Polisario Front, which seeks independence for the disputed territory.

As relations began to improve in May, France's Justice Minister GÃ©rald Darmanin visited Algiers and urged the Algerian authorities to allow Gleizes to reunite "not with France, but with his mother".

He said that he believed President Tebboune would be receptive to the request.

World.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
World.content:
Kylian MbappÃ© has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

MbappÃ© had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," MbappÃ© said in a statement.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."

Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian MbappÃ©'s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.

Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like MbappÃ©.

The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's AurÃ©lien TchouamÃ©ni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, MbappÃ© does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.

But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to "a Chinese dictator".

Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".

Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.

World.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
World.content:
If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of FlÃ¡vio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.

When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt".

Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back â and it paid off.

He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading "Brazil belongs to Brazilians".

His approval ratings jumped.

He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic â a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain.

Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point.

The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again.

Relations then improved.

The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks "very good" and Lula said he left "very satisfied".

Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strong leader.

World.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
World.content:
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.

Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.

It comes after nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.

World.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah detained after court orders news site's closure
World.content:
The CPJ said Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, was a vital source of critical reporting in Egypt and that it had long faced pressure from authorities over its journalism.

The site had repeatedly sought an operating licence from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) since a new media law was passed in 2018, but that its applications were either rejected or left unanswered, the media watchdog added.

Amnesty International said Lina Attalah had also faced "years of harassment and intimidation", including six criminal investigations over Mada Masr's reporting.

Last week, prosecutors summoned her for questioning over allegations of publishing "false news" and operating a website without a licence.

Mada Masr's lawyer said the investigation included a recent report that the website had published about a wave of protests in prisons across the country, as well as a letter from the SMRC regarding its legal status.

Attalah was released on bail and later referred to trial before the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court on the charge of operating a website without a licence.

During Tuesday's hearing, Judge Mohammed Mubarak ordered the courtroom to be cleared of everyone except Attalah, her eight-person defence team, and Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), an independent human rights group.

Bahgat told AFP news agency that security personnel then filed in before the judge announced that the court was denying several procedural requests made by the defence and appointing its own lawyer for Attalah.

"In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," he said. "Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes.

"In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer - who had not uttered a single word - and entered them into the official record," he added.

The judge then announced the fine for Attalah and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before she was detained, according to Bahgat.

Amnesty International warned that the court's verdict marked "a dark day for independent journalism" in Egypt and demanded that it be overturned.

"This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country's last remaining independent media voices," said the group's senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed.

"Lina Attalah should never have been prosecuted for exercising her right to freedom of expression and doing her journalistic job."

CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah said: "If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting."

World.title: Makinde’s campaign group asks EFCC to probe alleged sale of ministerial appointments
World.content:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate a claim that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments and later sought to recover the money while in office.

The organisation, which is championing Oyo State Governor Oluseyi Makinde’s campaign for the presidency on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), made the demand in a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa.

Its demand follows remarks by Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, who alleged during an interview on Arise Television on 23 October that some ministers paid billions of naira to secure their appointments.

“A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money,” Mr Hassan said.

Although Mr Hassan did not identify any minister allegedly involved in the practice or name anyone who received the payments, he noted that such practice had been going on for years in the country.

However, in its statement, the MDPCO said the EFCC should independently investigate the allegation and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable under the law.

It also criticised President Bola Tinubu for not publicly addressing the controversy, describing the Presidency’s silence five days after the remarks as a cause for concern.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It argued that the allegation raised questions about the integrity of ministerial appointments and the possibility that public office could be treated as a financial investment to be recouped through access to public resources.

“Mr President’s silence validates public apprehension that either he is not in control or he sits in approval of a corrupt and fraudulent system where public offices are reduced to commodities sold to highest bidders with devastating consequences on governance, the welfare of Nigerians and image of our nation,” the statement read.

It urged Nigerians to demand greater transparency and accountability ahead of the 2027 presidential election, while promoting its proposed “Reset Nigeria” agenda under the APM platform.

World.title: Six killed in another Plateau attack as governor vows to track down killers
World.content:
At least six people have been killed in an attack on Gero community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, with Governor Caleb Mutfwang saying investigators have recovered evidence that could help track down the perpetrators.

The attack, which occurred on Monday night, has renewed concerns over the security of communities around Jos metropolis, with residents appealing to the government and security agencies to prevent further killings.

Mr Mutfwang gave the assurance on Tuesday during the swearing-in of special advisers at the New Government House, Little Rayfield, Jos, describing the attack as disturbing because of its proximity to the state capital.

The governor said investigators were pursuing leads from evidence recovered at the scene, expressing confidence that those responsible would be brought to justice.

“This particular attack left some bits of evidence that we are trailing and, by the grace of God, we will continue to pursue these perpetrators of this dastardly act,” he said.

Mr Mutfwang also urged communities across the state to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies, acknowledging that delays in providing information could undermine efforts to prevent attacks.

“The security forces cannot be everywhere; they can only cover some places. If they get information, they will react, but sometimes the reaction comes late because by the time the information gets to them, it is impossible to have saved the situation,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Plateau State Police Command confirmed that six people were killed in the attack, revising an earlier figure of seven reported by community representatives.

In a statement, the police spokesperson, Alfred Alabo, said unidentified gunmen invaded Gero in the early hours of Tuesday, 27 October, and opened fire indiscriminately on residents.

He said the Commissioner of Police, Ayodeji Faniyan, immediately deployed mobile policemen and tactical operatives, led by the deputy commissioner of police in charge of operations, to the community.

The team, working with military personnel and operatives of Operation Rainbow, dislodged the attackers, who fled into a nearby hillside forest, according to the police.

The bodies of the victims were evacuated to a morgue, while an injured person was taken to hospital for treatment.

Mr Alabo said joint security personnel subsequently began bush-combing, cordon-and-search, and clearance operations to locate the fleeing attackers.

The operations led to the recovery of motorcycles and other items allegedly abandoned by the assailants, he added.

Mr Faniyan visited the community on Tuesday to assess the situation and meet community leaders, youth and women representatives, and other residents.

During the visit, residents expressed concern over the attack and called for measures to prevent further violence.

The police commissioner urged stronger cooperation between security agencies and community members to improve intelligence gathering.

The police also appealed to residents to remain calm and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

Earlier, the National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, said seven people were killed when the attackers stormed Gero at about 9:30 p.m. on Monday.

Mr Tengwong said the gunmen opened fire on unsuspecting residents at relaxation spots and nearby shops.

He called on the state government and security agencies to strengthen surveillance and intensify operations to protect communities.

Beyond the Gero attack, Mr Mutfwang disclosed that the alleged leader of the deadly attack on Kombun District in Mangu Local Government Area had been arrested.

He said his administration would continue to pursue the prosecution of suspects linked to violent attacks across the state.

The governor’s pledge comes amid persistent concerns over attacks on communities in Plateau, where residents have repeatedly called for sustained security operations and the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killings.

World.title: Police arrest man in viral video preaching religious intolerance, violence
World.content:
The Zamfara State Police Command on Tuesday arrested the man caught in a viral video preaching religious intolerance and violence against Christians in Enugu and Plateau states.

The suspect, reportedly a member of Jama’atu Izalatil Bidi’a Wa’ikamatus Sunnah (JIBWIS), was arrested by the group and handed over to the police for investigation after the video circulated on social media.

The Commissioner of Police, A.M. Bello, disclosed this during a press briefing in Gusau, saying the command had launched an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The arrest followed a call by the leadership of JIBWIS) which has distanced itself from the man leading a jogging exercise in its First Aid Group uniform, chanting threats to Christians.

The National Chairman of JIBWIS, Abdullahi Bala-Lau, condemned the footage and urged the State Security Services (SSS), the police and other security agencies to launch an immediate investigation, unmask those behind the recording, and prosecute anyone found culpable.

Mr Bala-Lau stated that the inciting remarks and calls for violence are entirely foreign to the core values, teachings, and objectives of JIBWIS.

He cautioned that merely wearing the organisation’s First Aid Group uniform or standing among members does not confer official representation or authority to speak on behalf of the body.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Expressing concern about the video’s timing and nature, the cleric noted that external actors might have calculatedly staged the incident to smear the organisation’s image and undermine national peace.

He pointed to JIBWIS’s peacebuilding track record, citing its recent international conference in Abuja, which convened Christian leaders, scholars from Islamic denominations, and international delegates to foster interfaith harmony and religious tolerance.

World.title: Unlocking the Future: Zenith Bank’s Tech Fair 6.0 puts AI in focus
World.content:
Zenith Bank Plc is set to host the sixth edition of its flagship technology event, Zenith Bank Tech Fair 2026: Future Forward 6.0, on Thursday, 5 November 2026, under the theme, “AI: Embrace or Extinct.”

Renowned for its scale and showcase of technological innovation, the annual Tech Fair has evolved into a platform for connecting ideas, talent and opportunities. Over the years, the event has brought together technology leaders, entrepreneurs, and young innovators to explore emerging technologies, showcase solutions and examine the future of the digital economy.

Conceived by the Bank’s Founder, Jim Ovia, the initiative reflects his vision of empowering young Nigerians through technology and nurturing inventors capable of developing solutions with global relevance. It also reinforces Zenith Bank’s commitment to digital advancement and the growth of Nigeria’s technology ecosystem.

The impact of the Tech Fair is evident in the solutions emerging from its competitions. Previous winners include JumpnPass, which developed a self-checkout solution for retail, and CreditChek, which uses artificial intelligence and open banking to streamline credit verification. At the 2025 edition, TrustLoopwon the hackathon for its digital identity verification solution, while Cubbes Technologies won the startup pitch competition with its AI-powered EdTech learning platform. Through millions in prize funding and mentorship, the Tech Fair continues to support promising innovators in developing practical solutions to real-world challenges.

For the first time, the Tech Fair will be held virtually, opening participation to a wider borderless audience across Nigeria and beyond. This year’s theme explores the growing influence of AI and challenges individuals and organisations to consider howbest to harness its potential in an increasingly technology-driven world. The event will offer participants an opportunity to discover emerging innovations, gain fresh insights and engage with ideas shaping the future of work and business.

The Tech Fair will be accessible via Zoom, Instagram, X, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube.

Be part of the future of technology. Register now at www.zenithbank.com/techfair and experience the possibilities of AI at Zenith Bank Tech Fair 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

About Zenith Bank Plc

Zenith Bank Plc is one of Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, recognised for its commitment to innovation, service excellence and strong corporate governance. Through strategic investments in technology and human capital, the Bank continues to deliver innovative financial solutions and contribute to the development of Nigeria’s digital economy.

World.title: Family announces burial arrangements for Nigerian actor Steve Echendu
World.content:
The family of late actor Steve Echendu has announced his burial arrangements.

His death was announced hours after veteran actor Francis Duru’s passing sent shockwaves through the entertainment industry.

In a statement posted on actress Clarion Chukwura’s Instagram page on Tuesday and signed by his son, Kamsiyochukwu Echendu, the family announced a three-day funeral programme for the 52-year-old actor.

The family said a wake-keep ceremony will take place on 27 November, ahead of his burial on 28 November in his hometown of Umuokwara Umuohiri, Isiala Mbano, Imo State.

A thanksgiving and outing service will follow on 29 November, bringing the funeral activities to an end.

“Your life was a blessing, your memory a treasure; you will always be loved and deeply missed”, said the family.

According to the family, the actor leaves behind his wife, children and brothers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Echendu

Mourning his death, Chukwura recalled his contributions to Nollywood during its formative years, when the industry was still finding its feet.

She described his death as a painful loss, saying his exit was hard to bear.

“This is hard. Indeed, a painful exit. A major pillar in the early days of Nollywood, the most professional, hardworking and respectful production manager I ever worked with in the foundational years of Nollywood. Rest in Peace, Steve”, she noted.

Echendu wore several hats in the industry, working as an actor, producer and director. His film credits include “Knockout Blessing”, “Fury”, “Infant at Heart”, among others.

As of press time, his family had not disclosed the cause of his death.

Meanwhile, colleagues paid tributes to his contributions to Nollywood during the industry’s formative years, as the home-video sector expanded.

World.title: ANALYSIS: Nigeria’s first methane disclosure raises questions over repeated figures, missing data
World.content:
Nigeria has taken an important step towards improving transparency in its oil and gas sector by publishing company-level greenhouse gas emissions data for the first time.

The disclosure, released by the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) in its 2023 oil and gas audit report, is expected to help citizens, regulators and investors understand how much pollution companies emit and whether the country is making progress towards its climate commitments.

However, an independent review of the data has identified several issues that may undermine confidence in the disclosures if left unresolved.

Using the Emissions Monitoring and Accountability Tool (EMAT), an interactive platform that organises and compares emissions data published by NEITI, this analysis found repeated emissions figures across different companies, missing methane information, and inconsistencies in the number of companies reported as having submitted emissions data.

The findings do not suggest wrongdoing by any company. Rather, they highlight areas where Nigeria’s emissions reporting framework could be strengthened to improve transparency, data quality and public confidence.

Repeated emissions figures

One of the most striking observations is that Chevron Nigeria Limited and the Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) reported exactly the same methane emissions figures for 2022.

Both companies reported 173,578,759.2 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) and 6,943,150.368 kilograms of methane.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The values are identical across virtually all reported fields except for halons.

The figures appear in Appendix 12 of NEITI’s 2022 and 2023 Oil and Gas Industry Reports, which contain Nigeria’s first publicly available company-level greenhouse gas disclosures.

This became immediately visible because EMAT allows users to compare company data side by side, identical figures that may be difficult to notice in static tables.

The Chevron-SPDC entries are not isolated cases.

Another example is Aradel Holdings Plc, which reported exactly the same methane values in both 2022 and 2023: 133,522,033 kilograms CO₂e and 5,340,877 kilograms of methane.

Similarly, Network E&P reported 112 kilograms CO2e and 3.64 kilograms methane in both reporting years.

Repeated figures do not automatically mean the data are inaccurate. Companies with similar operations, shared production facilities, or common reporting boundaries could legitimately report similar emissions. However, exactly identical values reported to several decimal places warrant further verification against the original submissions.

Another case concerns Pillar Oil, where the same numerical value appears repeatedly across different greenhouse gases.

For example, in 2022, the value 1,610,170.7872 appears across several gases, including carbon monoxide, nitrous oxide, nitric oxide and sulphur dioxide. The same pattern appears in 2023 with 2,389,859.8050.

The published report does not explain why these different gases share identical values.

Missing methane information

The analysis also found that methane reporting is far from complete.

Of the 30 company-year records reviewed in Appendix 12, only 12 contain information across all three methane reporting fields.

The remaining 18 records contain missing information, and some of the omissions are difficult to interpret.

For instance, NAE reported 963,970 kilograms of methane in 2022 but recorded zero for the corresponding carbon dioxide equivalent.

In 2023, the company again reported methane emissions but left the carbon dioxide equivalent field blank.

Similarly, Chevron and Heirs Energies reported methane only as carbon dioxide equivalent in 2023 without providing the underlying methane mass.

Heirs Energies reported 217.4 million kilograms CO₂e, one of the highest methane-related figures in the dataset, yet the absence of the methane mass makes it impossible to independently verify the conversion.

In another case, Platform Petroleum appears on the reporting sheet, yet all of its methane fields are blank for both years.

The report provides no explanation of whether blank cells indicate that no emissions occurred, that no data were submitted, or that emissions were not calculated.

This distinction matters because a blank field is not the same as reporting zero emissions.

Inconsistencies in company reporting

The analysis also raises questions about how many companies actually submitted emissions data.

NEITI states that 15 out of 62 audited companies submitted greenhouse gas information, while 47 companies did not.

However, the appendix presents 15 companies on the reporting sheets, and 58 entries on the non-reporting sheet.

Taken together, the lists contain 73 entries, rather than the 62 companies referenced by NEITI.

Further review shows that Platform Petroleum appears on both the reporting and non-reporting lists.

In addition, some entries refer to joint venture interests or individual oil fields rather than clearly identifiable legal entities, making it difficult to determine exactly which companies reported emissions.

For example, the non-reporting list includes the NEPL (55 per cent) and Shoreline (45 per cent) interests in OML 30, while the reporting sheets separately list Esso’s Erha and Usan fields.

A reconciled list that clearly distinguishes legal entities, operators, and production assets would significantly improve transparency.

Why this matters

Nigeria has committed to ending routine gas flaring by 2030 and reducing fugitive methane emissions from the oil and gas sector by 60 per cent by 2031.

Measuring progress towards these goals depends on reliable baseline data.

Because Appendix 12 represents Nigeria’s first public company-level greenhouse gas disclosure, it effectively serves as the benchmark against which future emissions reductions will be measured. If the baseline contains gaps or inconsistencies, assessing future progress becomes more difficult.

Several practical improvements could strengthen future disclosures, including publishing the original reporting templates submitted by companies, clearly distinguishing between reported zeros and missing information, identifying the legal entity responsible for each reported asset, providing explanatory notes for unusual entries and maintaining a public log of corrections where errors are identified.

NEITI’s response

NEITI was asked, through a Freedom of Information request, to respond to the issues identified in the analysis, including questions concerning the methodology used by companies, duplicate figures, missing or zero values, emissions intensity, the number of reporting companies, verification procedures, and the accessibility of the published data.

NEITI explained that under EITI Requirement 3.4, greenhouse gas reporting is encouraged rather than mandatory.

According to the agency, its reporting template requested companies to provide greenhouse gas emissions data and information on the methodology used, including emission factors, direct ground based sensors, satellite estimates, and other recognised approaches.

However, the template did not require companies to provide the Global Warming Potential values used, the specific IPCC or other scientific assessment from which those values were derived, or the time horizon used to convert emissions into CO₂ equivalents.

The agency said it did not convert, normalise, recalculate or adjust the data submitted by companies. The published figures, therefore, reflect the information provided by the companies.

NEITI also said there is currently no established national verification framework for these disclosures and that its role is focused on transparency, collection, and publication rather than on independent technical validation or methodological harmonisation.

Regarding repeated entries and identical figures identified in the analysis, NEITI acknowledged the observations and said it would conduct an internal review.

The agency said necessary adjustments had been reflected in the published data. It added that the original company templates and internal validation records were not intended for public disclosure.

NEITI said that any corrections or clarifications resulting from its internal review would be reflected in the published dataset. It acknowledged the observations and said it would take the feedback into account as it updates the published information.

What happens next?

NEITI’s first company-level greenhouse gas disclosure represents an important starting point for public scrutiny of emissions in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector.

The data provide journalists, researchers, civil society organisations and policymakers with information that was previously difficult to access at the company level.

At the same time, the analysis shows that the value of the disclosure will depend on improvements in the way emissions information is collected, standardised, verified and published.

The immediate priority should be to establish a clearer and more consistent reporting framework that enables users to distinguish between zero emissions, missing information and non-applicable data; understand the methodology behind reported figures; identify the companies and assets covered; and reproduce emissions-intensity calculations.

As Nigeria works towards its methane-reduction commitments, the quality of the underlying data will be as important as the targets themselves.

The first disclosure has opened the window of transparency. The next challenge is ensuring that the information available through that window is complete, consistent and reliable to support meaningful public accountability.

This report was supported by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development(CJID) as part of the Deepening Methane Emissions Transparency Initiative-Stream II

World.title: Lawmakers move to make formal identification compulsory for renting apartments in Abuja
World.content:
The Senate on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, to present valid means of identification before renting apartments as part of efforts to curb criminal activities.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, directed the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, to draft the bill for consideration by the National Assembly.

Mr Akpabio gave the directive during the plenary while lawmakers were debating a report by the Senate committees on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations; Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters; Foreign Affairs; and Special Duties on the need to protect Nigerians from being trafficked to Libya for slavery.

The report was presented by Aniekan Bassey, chair of the Senate Committee on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations.

Mr Akpabio expressed concern that many property owners rent out their properties to strangers without obtaining adequate information about their identities, occupations and other relevant details.

He argued that the lack of proper documentation makes it difficult for security agencies to trace suspects when crimes are committed, allowing perpetrators to escape without leaving a clear trail.

“A lot of people just give their properties to strangers. They don’t even have any papers to know where they come from. In some instances, the phone number that is used in renting the property does not even belong to the occupant of the house. So when something happens, the person will escape and then leave no trace,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Senate President urged Mr Bamidele to consider legislation that would strengthen tenancy regulations and make landlords more accountable for verifying prospective tenants’ identities.

“People enter people’s properties with very nefarious intentions and, at the end of the day, they will just commit some crimes, traffic people’s children and make money while living in the house itself. It is something that we must tighten the laws on tenancy,” he said.

Mr Akpabio proposed adopting an approach similar to the banking sector’s Know Your Customer (KYC) policy, which requires financial institutions to verify customers’ identities.

“As you know in the bank, they say, know your customer; this one we can say, know your tenants. Let’s make the necessary law for the FCT, for instance. We can enact an Act for the FCT that says know your tenants so that nobody will come and live in the house and perpetrate crime,” he said.

He said the proposed legislation could also cover the rental of shops and other commercial spaces, arguing that inadequate identity verification could expose occupants and business owners to criminal attacks.

Mr Akpabio said people renting shops should provide verifiable identification, including a driver’s licence or international passport, to help security agencies trace them if they are implicated in criminal activities.

He said the lack of reliable tenant information could leave property owners unable to identify or help locate people who used their premises to commit crimes.

“And then even those that are going to do shoplets, we can use that opportunity to regulate shoplets because people go into secluded environments and then do shoplets, and then they move in and they rob them in the night and escape.

“So people who want to do shoplifting should have clear identities; you should be able to show either a driver’s licence or an international passport and other means of identification so that if you stay in somebody’s property and then you go and commit a crime, when they trace and come there and find out that this was where you live, the owner of the property may not even have an idea of who you were.”

Akpabio’s experience as governor

To support his argument, Mr Akpabio recalled measures his administration introduced to tackle kidnapping when he was governor of Akwa Ibom State.

He said his government prescribed the death penalty for kidnapping and introduced measures involving the destruction of property used as hideouts by criminals.

The Senate President noted that the measures encouraged landlords to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious behaviour for fear of losing them.

He said similar measures could help deter criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as bases for criminal activities.

How the proposed law could affect Abuja’s rental market

If enacted as envisaged by the Senate President, the proposed legislation would require landlords in the FCT to verify prospective tenants’ identities before letting out their property.

The proposal is intended to help security agencies trace people suspected of committing crimes from their residential addresses and discourage criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as hideouts.

However, its effectiveness would depend on the legislation’s details, including how identities would be verified, what records landlords would be required to keep, and how compliance would be monitored.

READ ALSO: Tinubu transmits bill to Senate to allow transfer of convicted Nigerians abroad back home

If enacted, the law could make it easier for investigators to establish the identities of tenants linked to rented property. It could also impose additional responsibilities on landlords and property agents, potentially requiring them to retain identification records and provide relevant information to authorised authorities when legally required.

The proposal could, however, raise concerns about privacy, the security of tenants’ personal information and the possibility of landlords using the requirement to discriminate against prospective tenants or deny accommodation to people who cannot readily provide the prescribed documents.

The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 provides a framework for lawful, secure handling of personal information. Any system requiring landlords to collect and retain tenants’ identification details would need to comply with applicable data protection obligations.

The proposal remains in the drafting stage, based on the proceedings described by the Senate President. It would need to go through the legislative process before becoming law.

World.title: Ebola: WHO expresses hope as cases surpass 10,000, deaths near 5,000 in DRC
World.content:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has expressed hope that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) can be contained, despite confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease surpassing 10,000.

The optimism comes as data released by the DRC’s Ministry of Public Health on Tuesday put confirmed cases at 10,060, with 4,887 deaths, according to a report by Al Jazeera.

The outbreak, declared on 15 May, is the largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic recorded in the DRC.

It is also the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak globally, behind the 2014–2016 West African epidemic, which recorded about 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths.

Reasons for hope

In a post on his official X account on Tuesday, Mohammed Janabi, the WHO Regional Director for Africa, said the rising figures reflected the toll the outbreak had taken on families and communities but noted that progress in recovery, research and response efforts offered reasons for hope.

Mr Janabi said more than 2,600 people had recovered, while new vaccine and treatment candidates were advancing through clinical trials.

He added that laboratory testing, treatment capacity, infection prevention and control, community engagement and surveillance were being strengthened to help contain the outbreak.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our teams are on the ground, working side by side with the government and partners to stop transmission and save lives,” he said, calling for sustained commitment, community trust and solidarity, as well as safe access to affected communities.

Spread beyond the DRC

The rising figures come amid growing concerns about the spread of the virus beyond the DRC, with Kenya and Nigeria reporting infections linked to the wider outbreak.

PREMIUM TIMES reported last week that Kenya had recorded nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, after the virus was introduced by a traveller who arrived from the DRC through Uganda.

Nigeria also confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October, after a woman who had travelled from Uganda tested positive in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

In a subsequent report, PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) was investigating a possible link between the Nigerian case and the infection recorded in Kenya.

Both patients travelled through Entebbe International Airport in Uganda on 3 October, prompting investigations into whether they had shared equipment or had other contact. However, health officials have stressed that a direct connection between the infections has not been established.

Nigeria’s health minister, Muhammad Pate, later said genomic sequencing showed that the viruses detected in Nigeria and Kenya differed by only one mutation. He cautioned, however, that the finding did not establish where the Nigerian patient contracted the virus.

Contact tracing challenges

According to the Al Jazeera report, about 80 per cent of new cases in the DRC are occurring outside the known chains of transmission being monitored by health authorities.

This means many infections are being detected among people whose exposure to previously confirmed cases has not been established, complicating efforts to identify contacts and interrupt further transmission.

The Africa CDC has said at least 95 per cent of cases must be linked to known contacts of infected people for an outbreak to be considered under control.

Vaccine research underway

The absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain remains another major challenge in the response.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on Friday that the World Health Organisation (WHO) had announced the commencement of the Tumaini clinical trial in Bunia, eastern DRC, to assess potential vaccines against the strain.

The trial began with the vaccination of its first participants on 23 October and is expected to evaluate several vaccine candidates, including Ervebo, which is licensed against a different Ebola virus species, as well as experimental candidates being developed by Moderna and the University of Oxford in collaboration with the Serum Institute of India.

The trial is intended to establish whether the candidates can safely generate an immune response and protect against the Bundibugyo virus. Their effectiveness against the strain has not yet been established.

The development follows an earlier WHO recommendation, reported by PREMIUM TIMES in August, that Ervebo be prioritised for a clinical trial after preliminary animal studies suggested it might offer some cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus disease.

World.title: Senate committee clears Eze Anaba, 15 other NHRC board nominees
World.content:
File: Eze Anaba

By Henry Umoru, ABUJA

THE Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters has cleared the President, Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE and Editor, Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba and 15 other nominees for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC.

The committee, chaired by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) screened the nominees as part of the legislative process for reconstituting the commission’s governing board following President Bola Tinubu’s request for Senate confirmation.

The Committee will thereafter forward its report to the Senate for consideration at plenary, where the upper chamber will take a final position on the nominations.

Speaking with journalists after the screening exercise, Anaba explained that his nomination would provide an opportunity to sustain his longstanding commitment to human rights protection, which he described as an integral part of his journalism career.

The NGE President who expressed confidence that his diverse professional backgrounds would strengthen the commission’s capacity to promote and protect the rights of Nigerians, however cautioned against making definitive commitments before the completion of the process by the Senate.

“We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one,” he said.

Anaba who expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision, added that the Senate’s final position would determine the next stage of the process.

Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, the Vanguaard Editor said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.

“I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said.

Anaba also disclosed that he had been associated with the activities of the NHRC before his nomination to its governing board, just as he expressed optimism that the incoming board, with its blend of professional expertise, would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in the country.

Earlier in his remarks after the screening, Adegbonmire explained that the screening exercise had been completed and that the committee’s recommendations would be presented to the Senate for consideration.

He said the Senate would communicate its decision to the President through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation after deliberating on the report.

Adegbonmire clarified that the NHRC’s governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs. He explained that the three ministries’ representatives were not subjected to individual screening because the law specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees.

World.title: Kidnappers abduct six in Kaduna
World.content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Suspected kidnappers have abducted six persons during an attack on Nuru Suraj Estate in the Millennium City area of Kaduna metropolis on Tuesday morning.

The attackers were said to have invaded the estate early in the morning, shooting sporadically and throwing residents into panic as they scrambled for safety.

Sources in the area disclosed that the suspected kidnappers gained access to the estate through its second gate before carrying out the abduction.

A resident, who identified herself as Maman Hamid, said her house was close to those of the victims, adding that the attackers arrived at the estate and began shooting, causing fear among residents.

According to her, the assailants exploited the second entrance to gain access to the estate before whisking away the victims to an unknown destination.

The circumstances surrounding the abduction, including the identities of the victims and whether any contact had been established with their families, were not immediately clear as of the time of filing this report.

The incident has renewed concerns over the security situation in Millennium City, an area of Kaduna metropolis that has witnessed previous attacks by suspected kidnappers.

A few weeks ago, suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded another part of Millennium City and abducted several persons, raising fresh concerns among residents over the recurrence of such attacks in the area.

Efforts to obtain a reaction from the Kaduna State Police Command were unsuccessful as the command had yet to react to the latest incident as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Nasarawa 2027: Ex-IGP Adamu raises alarm over PVC buying
World.content:
Former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has raised concerns over alleged vote-buying and the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women to prevent them from voting in the 2027 Nasarawa State governorship election.

Adamu spoke in Doma Local Government Area while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago nation.

He alleged that some political actors were buying voters’ cards to suppress participation in the election, urging residents not to surrender their PVCs for money.

“Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote,” he said.

He urged anyone whose PVC had been collected to retrieve it and encouraged eligible voters to turn out on election day with their cards.

“Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” the former police chief said.

The endorsement was announced at a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for Adamu, who is seeking to govern Nasarawa State in 2027.

He expressed appreciation to the group for its support, saying the endorsement had strengthened his confidence in his political ambition.

Adamu also thanked God for what he described as progress in his political journey, adding that the support from the Alago community was encouraging.

He said his ambition was driven by the need to improve the welfare of ordinary residents, particularly vulnerable people who, according to him, had been neglected under the present situation.

“Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he said.

Adamu pledged to prioritise education, healthcare and security if elected governor, promising to pursue improvements in public services and create safer communities.

“We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” he said.

He also expressed gratitude to the Alago Support Group and other supporters for their commitment to his aspiration, saying he hoped to secure victory in the 2027 election.

The former IGP’s allegation of PVC collection and vote-buying was not accompanied by specific details of those allegedly involved.

World.title: Nigeria records 43,000 snakebites, 2,500 deaths yearly
World.content:
Experts have urged residents to avoid handling snakes and seek prompt medical attention for snakebites, as Nigeria records an estimated 43,000 cases annually.

The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍‍⁠‌​‌‌​cases reportedly result in between 1,099 and 2,500 deaths yearly.

The experts gave the advice at a national training workshop on snakebite handling, treatment and management at the Lekki Conservation Centre, Lagos, on Tuesday.

A medical expert, Abubakar Ballah, described snakebite as a neglected tropical disease, identifying the carpet viper as responsible for about 66 per cent of snakebite deaths in Nigeria.

Ballah cited the World Health Organisation estimates of 5.4 million snakebites globally each year, resulting in 81,000 to 138,000 deaths and about 400,000 cases of permanent disability.

He identified Gombe, Plateau, Bauchi, Benue and Taraba as major snakebite-endemic states, particularly within the Niger-Benue trough and Sudan Savanna.

According to him, farmers, herders, children and hunters are among the most vulnerable, with cases often peaking during farming, rainy and harvest seasons.

Ballah identified the carpet viper, puff adder and black-necked spitting cobra as Nigeria’s three medically important snakes.

He said their venom could cause severe bleeding, tissue destruction, kidney injury, neurological complications and respiratory paralysis.

He warned that delayed hospital presentation and harmful first aid could worsen patients’ conditions.

He said such practices include applying tight tourniquets, cutting bite wounds, using animal dung and resorting to traditional remedies.

Citing clinical cases, Ballah said some patients died following delayed treatment and harmful first aid, while others recovered after early hospital presentation and appropriate care.

He identified the high cost of antivenom, poor healthcare access, bad roads and inadequate blood bank services as factors contributing to snakebite deaths.

According to him, antivenom costs between ₦170,000 and ₦250,000 per vial.

Ballah stressed that trained healthcare personnel should administer antivenom when clinically indicated and monitor patients for allergic reactions and other complications.

He called for quality antivenom supplies, proper storage, improved referral systems and community education to reduce snakebite-related deaths.

In a separate presentation titled “Dangerous Snakes of Lagos State, Nigeria,” wildlife conservation expert, Dr Mark Ofua, advised residents against attempting to catch, kill or handle snakes.

Ofua said snake encounters could occur in mangroves, swamps, farms, gardens, building sites, drains, compounds and stores.

He urged residents to exercise caution in such environments and leave snake handling to trained personnel equipped with appropriate tools.

He identified the puff adder, black-necked spitting cobra, forest cobra, green mamba and Gaboon viper among species requiring particular attention in Lagos.

Ofua also discussed the boomslang and carpet viper, noting that the presence of some species, particularly the carpet viper, required confirmation through local records.

He cautioned residents against identifying dangerous snakes solely by their head shape, pupils, colour or size.

He noted that some venomous species could be difficult to recognise and that protective equipment did not eliminate the risk of bites.

Ofua advised suspected snakebite victims to remain calm and still, immobilise the affected limb, remove tight items and seek immediate medical attention.

He warned against cutting or sucking bite wounds, applying tourniquets, using traditional remedies or attempting to chase and kill the snake.

For venom spat into the eyes, he recommended immediate and prolonged irrigation with water.

Both experts emphasised public awareness, prompt hospital treatment and safer interactions with wildlife as essential measures to reduce snakebite injuries and deaths.

Earlier, the Director-General of NCF, Dr Joseph Onoja, said snakes played important roles in biodiversity and ecosystem balance.

Onoja said snakes help control rodent populations, warning that unchecked rodent increases could heighten the risk of infections such as Lassa fever.

“It becomes important that we learn to live as one in harmony with nature and more specifically snakes,” he said.

The two-day national training workshop, scheduled for Oct. 27 and 28, focuses on improving snakebite handling, treatment and management.

World.title: Meet 5 Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to global positions in 2026
World.content:
Nigerians in the diaspora have continued to secure leadership positions in global companies, academic institutions and healthcare organisations, strengthening the country’s representation in global decision-making.

In 2026, several Nigerian professionals received appointments spanning corporate strategy, medicine, law, public health and academic leadership, placing them in positions to influence organisational growth, healthcare policy and international cooperation.

Their appointments highlight the contributions of Nigerian professionals working across different countries and industries.

Here are five Nigerians in the diaspora appointed to prominent positions in 2026.

1. Ugwechi Amadi — Chief Strategy Officer, McDonald’s

Nigerian-born executive Ugwechi Amadi was appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer of McDonald’s in July 2026, joining the American multinational fast-food company after holding senior positions in sports, retail and management consulting.

Her appointment was announced on July 15, 2026, following a statement by McDonald’s Chief Financial Officer, Ian Borden.

Before joining McDonald’s, Amadi served as Executive Vice President and Head of Corporate Strategy and Development at LIV Golf, where she oversaw strategic planning and business development.

She previously worked at Nike as Vice President of Global Operations Strategy, contributing to initiatives involving technology, supply chain management and organisational transformation.

Earlier in her career, she worked at Boston Consulting Group, advising multinational companies on corporate strategy and business performance.

Amadi holds a bachelor’s degree in Brain and Cognitive Sciences from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and a doctorate in Clinical Neuroscience from the University of Oxford.

Her appointment places her in a senior position overseeing strategic priorities and supporting the company’s long-term growth.

2. Professor Ibrahim Abubakar — CEO-designate, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations

Nigerian-born epidemiologist Professor Ibrahim Abubakar was appointed Chief Executive Officer-designate of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations in August 2026.

The appointment was announced on August 14, with Abubakar scheduled to join the organisation in March 2027 and formally assume leadership in April 2027.

He is expected to succeed Richard Hatchett, who has led CEPI since its establishment in 2017.

Abubakar is currently Vice-Provost for Health and Professor of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at University College London.

He previously directed UCL’s Institute for Global Health, contributing to research and policy development in infectious diseases, migration health and public health systems.

His academic work includes research on tuberculosis, epidemiology and global disease prevention.

CEPI is an international partnership that finances and coordinates vaccine development against emerging infectious diseases and potential pandemic threats.

In his new role, Abubakar is expected to oversee international vaccine research partnerships and initiatives aimed at strengthening pandemic preparedness.

3. Ibironke Odumosu-Ayanu — Dean, University of Saskatchewan College of Law

Nigerian-born legal scholar Ibironke Odumosu-Ayanu was appointed Dean of the University of Saskatchewan College of Law in Canada, effective October 1, 2026.

Her appointment was announced on September 1 for a five-year tenure, succeeding Professor Martin Phillipson.

Born and raised in Lagos, Odumosu-Ayanu obtained her law degree from the University of Lagos before moving to Canada for postgraduate studies.

She holds a Master of Laws degree from the University of Calgary and a doctorate from the University of British Columbia.

She joined the University of Saskatchewan in 2008 and previously served as a professor and Associate Dean of Research and Graduate Studies.

Her research focuses on international investment law, business and human rights, natural resource governance and community development.

She has also received recognition for her teaching and academic mentorship.

As dean, Odumosu-Ayanu is responsible for providing academic leadership, advancing research and supporting the strategic development of the Canadian law school.

4. Bolu Ogunyemi — President, Canadian Medical Association

Nigerian-born physician Dr Bolu Ogunyemi assumed office as President of the Canadian Medical Association on May 29, 2026, becoming the first Black person to lead the organisation.

His inauguration took place during the association’s annual general meeting, marking a milestone for representation in Canada’s medical profession.

Ogunyemi is a dermatologist based in St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, with experience in clinical medicine, medical education and healthcare advocacy.

The Canadian Medical Association is a national professional organisation that represents physicians and advocates improvements in healthcare delivery.

As president, Ogunyemi has focused on issues including access to primary healthcare, reducing administrative burdens on physicians and supporting innovations that improve patient outcomes.

He has also highlighted the importance of healthcare systems that reflect Canada’s diverse population.

His appointment places him at the forefront of national discussions on healthcare policy, physician welfare and the future of medical practice in Canada.

5. Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu — President, Union for International Cancer Control

Nigerian paediatrician and cancer advocate Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu assumed the presidency of the Union for International Cancer Control, a Geneva-based organisation working to reduce the global cancer burden and improve access to cancer care.

She is the founder of the Medicaid Cancer Foundation, a Nigerian nonprofit organisation focused on cancer awareness, screening, prevention and patient support.

Shinkafi-Bagudu previously served as First Lady of Kebbi State from 2015 to 2023, during which she championed healthcare interventions, particularly cancer prevention and treatment for women and children.

Her work has involved collaboration with international health organisations, policymakers and advocacy groups to improve cancer care in underserved communities.

As UICC president, she leads the organisation’s board in promoting international cooperation, equitable access to cancer treatment and stronger cancer-control policies.

Her appointment places a Nigerian healthcare professional at the helm of an international organisation working with partners across the global cancer-control community.
