World.title: Kano Assembly approves state police
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The Kano State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment to allow state governments to establish and operate their own police forces.

The approval was confirmed by the Majority Leader of the Assembly, Lawan Hussaini Dala, shortly after plenary on Tuesday.

Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police.

“We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said.

The approval followed deliberations on the proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which seek to give state governments the legal authority to establish and operate their own police forces.

During plenary, the lawmakers considered the constitutional alteration bill in the Committee of the Whole, deliberating on clauses one to 26 of the proposed amendment.

The lawmakers had earlier adopted a motion to consider the constitutional amendment bill in the Committee of the Whole before proceeding with deliberations on its provisions.

World.title: Ebola: NCDC defends patient’s evacuation, rejects claims of no confidence
World.content:
Volunteers of the Democratic Republic of Congo Red Cross wearing personal protective equipment carry the casket containing the body of an Ebola virus disease victim at the morgue of the Rwampara health centre, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, on June 8, 2026 before loading it into a vehicle for transfer to a cemetery as part of safe and dignified burial operations aimed at preventing the spread of the virus. The head of the World Health Organization visited Uganda on Monday and praised its efforts to limit the spread of an Ebola outbreak from neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. The WHO has declared an international health emergency over the outbreak which has caused 515 confirmed infections in the DRC, including 91 deaths, since it was announced on May 15 in northeastern DRC. Uganda has recorded 19 cases and two deaths. All but five have been Congolese nationals who crossed the border. (Photo by Jospin Mwisha / AFP)

Warns against politicising evacuation, false Ebola-free reports

By Sola Ogundipe

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has defended the evacuation of Nigeria’s Ebola index patient to Switzerland, rejecting claims that the transfer amounted to a vote of no confidence in the country’s medical system.

The Director-General of the agency, Dr Jide Idris, who spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at a capacity-building programme for journalists on effective Ebola reporting, also dismissed concerns that the evacuation was being politicised, including allegations that the Ebola incident could be used to impose a lockdown, restrict movement or interfere with the 2027 general elections.

Idris said the index patient, who returned to Abuja from Uganda, improved clinically while in isolation and left Nigeria in a stable and conscious condition, even as he said the evacuation did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, faulting reports that suggested otherwise.

“Within hours of WHO saying that Nigeria currently has no Ebola case, several platforms reported that Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free. It had not, WHO had to call the reports inaccurate and misleading, and a public that believes the danger is over stops washing its hands and stops calling 6232.

“The evacuation of the patient by her own government has been presented as a vote of no confidence in Nigerian medicine, when she was largely managed by Nigerian clinicians, and this case has been dragged into politics: that it is a pretext for a lockdown, for restricting movement, or for interfering with the 2027 elections.

“There are also persistent demands that we name the patient and her contacts. We will not. A contact who is named is a contact who hides, and a contact who hides is how an imported case becomes an outbreak.

Idris warned that premature claims that Nigeria was Ebola-free could weaken public vigilance and discourage people from observing preventive measures or contacting health authorities when symptoms developed.

“The welfare stipend of N100,000 a week that we approved for people in quarantine, so as to relief the burden of other family responsibilities those in quarantine ought to be performing but unable to for now , has been turned into a story about money sharing, as if people are being paid for Ebola.

“The next six weeks will test the country, and how the public comes through them depends as much on what is published by the agency and the media, ” he said.

He explained that although Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola case in the country following the patient’s evacuation, 53 primary contacts remained under daily follow-up, with most in quarantine in Abuja and a few at home. Three contacts who developed symptoms had tested negative for Ebola, he confirmed.

Idris said the 42-day surveillance countdown had begun, with December 7, 2026, marking the earliest possible date for declaring the event over if no new case emerged. The World Health Organisation (WHO) would validate any such declaration, he added.

Further, he cautioned against demands for the disclosure of patients’ and contacts’ identities, saying exposure could discourage people from cooperating with health authorities and undermine contact tracing.

“A contact who is named is a contact who hides, and a contact who hides is how an imported case becomes an outbreak,” he said.

Idris, however, stressed that scrutiny of the country’s Ebola response remained legitimate, including questions about preparedness, funding and the speed of contact tracing.

“Accountability is not misinformation. The difference is that a question seeks an answer, and a rumour supplies one,” he said, pledging that the agency would provide timely, on-the-record responses to journalists’ inquiries.

He urged journalists to verify information before publication, use designated NCDC communication channels and correct false reports on the same platforms with comparable prominence.

He also called for responsible reporting that protects patients and contacts from exposure, warning against publishing their names, photographs or addresses or using language that could stigmatise quarantined families.

Reiterating key public health messages, Idris said Ebola spreads through contact with the body fluids of a sick infected person, not through the air. He added that people without symptoms were not infectious and that healthy travellers should not automatically be treated as threats.

He advised anyone who develops a fever and has a relevant travel or contact history to call the NCDC’s 6232 hotline before visiting a health facility.

“The public does not need louder headlines; it needs accurate ones, repeated by voices it trusts. Those voices are yours,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu needs another term to consolidate reforms — Tompolo
World.content:
…Presents 30 vehicles for mobilisation

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Imo State, declaring that the President means well for Nigeria and deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s reforms.

Tompolo made the declaration on Tuesday at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State, where he donated 30 vehicles to facilitate grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election.

Represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo said the vehicles and other resources were provided to support Governor Hope Uzodimma and the movement’s campaign activities across the state.

He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who prioritised Nigeria’s interests by embarking on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration in May 2023.

“Our President, President Bola Tinubu, is a very courageous man. A man who puts Nigeria first. A man who loves Nigeria more than he loves himself.

“A man who loves Nigeria more than the office that he is vying for. When he came into office, he did not do the normal calculations that politicians usually do. He came in and said that he wants to reform Nigeria,” Tompolo said.

Relaying Tompolo’s message, Pondi said the donation was aimed at strengthening the movement’s capacity to mobilise voters for the President across the state.

“Your Excellency, we have come with vehicles. We have come with resources. These vehicles you have seen, there are 30 of them. We brought them to Imo State to support you in your cause to re-elect President Bola Tinubu,” he said.

Tompolo said the movement would work with Uzodimma and other political leaders to take the President’s campaign to households and communities across Imo State, adding that the newly inaugurated chapter would be available to support campaign activities whenever required.

“Your Excellency, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Imo State is at your beck and call. Anytime you need them, call them. Give them instructions. Tell them how you want them to campaign,” he said.

Speaking at the event, Governor Uzodimma commended Tompolo for providing resources to support the campaign, describing the movement as an important partner in efforts to secure another term for Tinubu.

Uzodimma said his assessment of the President’s performance had convinced him that Tinubu should be given another term to complete his programmes and initiatives.

“When we preach the Gospel about the All Progressives Congress government of President Bola Tinubu, we started, we were not many. But as the days go by, the efforts and activities of the government begin to trickle in. Nigerians begin to see the man called Bola Tinubu in his true colour,” he said.

The governor acknowledged that the administration had made progress but still had outstanding tasks to accomplish, adding that continuity would enable Tinubu to complete his work.

“We have assessed the achievements of President Bola Tinubu. And we have seen the good things he brought. We have also seen so many things he is also yet to do.

“And we decided to lead the crusade that will enable him to complete his good work. We have taken that decision,” Uzodimma said.

He described Tompolo as a committed supporter of the President’s re-election bid and praised the door-to-door campaign strategy for taking the message of the Renewed Hope Agenda directly to Nigerians.

“We are partners in progress. We work with you. We do the work. We elect the President,” he said.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Nigerians to remain patient with the administration, arguing that the economic difficulties associated with its reforms would give way to long-term benefits.

Asuku said Tinubu had laid a foundation for economic development in the past three and a half years and should be allowed another four years to build on it.

“The message we must tell today is simple and short. Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has sent us to make you understand that things might be rough, but Nigeria is on the right trajectory,” he said.

He maintained that economic reforms often came with temporary difficulties but argued that they were necessary to achieve lasting prosperity.

“Where there is reform, we are expected to go through some pains. But it is a pain that guarantees long-term prosperity. And we can get through for sure,” Asuku said.

He also challenged opposition politicians to account for their records in public office, urging Nigerians to examine their past performances before making electoral decisions.

Asuku called on voters to turn out en masse on January 16, 2027, to vote for Tinubu, adding that the movement would take its campaign from door to door, town to town and community to community.

In his remarks, Imo State APC Chairman, Chief Austine Onyedebelu, highlighted the Federal Government’s economic reforms and the state government’s infrastructure projects, urging party members to take the campaign directly to residents.

He cited the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the increase in the national minimum wage to N70,000 as measures introduced by the Tinubu administration.

Onyedebelu, however, acknowledged that rising food prices, transportation costs and other economic pressures remained concerns for many Nigerians, stressing that the ultimate measure of government policies should be their impact on citizens’ living conditions.

He also highlighted infrastructure projects undertaken by the Uzodimma administration, saying the door-to-door campaign would provide an opportunity to explain government policies and programmes directly to residents rather than relying solely on rallies.

World.title: Those Listed in Osun Presidential Campaign Council Are Not Our Representatives, Says IPAC
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Osun State chapter of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, IPAC, has disowned those listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council by the state coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke.

IPAC said the individuals paraded as its members in the Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, are on their own and were never authorised to represent it.

The council made this known in a press statement signed by leaders of some political parties in the state on Tuesday.

The political parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party.

Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party, All Progressives Grand Alliance and others.

It could be recalled that an advertorial signed by Adeleke, who is the coordinator of Tinubu Presidential Campaign Council in Osun, in one of the national dailies, named Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives.

However, the statement by Osun IPAC noted that the inclusion of the names in the PCC list is misleading and capable of creating confusion.

“We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity.

“IPAC is a structured body with duly recognised leadership and member political parties, and any representation must follow due process and official communication from our secretariat,” the statement noted.

The council said it dissociates itself completely from the list, stressing that IPAC should not be used to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance.

IPAC also urged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu not to recognise those listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that members with strong grassroots presence across all local governments are the legitimate stakeholders.

“We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added.

World.title: House Moves to Institutionalise Use of Strategic Research Findings in National Policy Formulation
World.content:
The House of Representatives has moved to institutionalise the consideration and utilisation of strategic research findings in national policy formulation, development planning and governance.

The move followed a motion sponsored by the Deputy Minority Leader, Rep. Abdussamad Dasuki, who represents Kebbe/Tambuwal Federal Constituency.

The motion seeks to establish a coordinated framework for the systematic review, referral and monitoring of strategic research recommendations produced by key national institutions, including the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru; the National Defence College (NDC), Abuja; and the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS).

The lawmakers noted that the Federal Government had over the years established and sustained these institutions to undertake research, develop strategic leadership capacity and provide informed policy recommendations to address Nigeria’s economic, security, governance and developmental challenges.

The House further noted that the institutions regularly produce comprehensive reports and policy recommendations through their executive courses, studies programmes and research activities, drawing on the expertise of senior public servants, military and security officers, academics, policymakers and other professionals.

The House also acknowledged the statutory mandate of NIPSS under Section 3 of the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies Act to conduct interdisciplinary research into Nigeria’s social, economic, political and security challenges and present practical policy options to support national policy formulation and implementation.

It cited Sections 13 and 18 of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for institutional consultation in the preparation of the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) and establish the framework as the basis for annual budget preparation.

According to the motion, these provisions offer an existing legal framework through which strategic research findings can contribute to national economic planning and expenditure priorities.

The lawmakers observed that although research reports and policy recommendations from the institutions are periodically presented to the Presidency and other relevant authorities, there is a need for a more systematic and coordinated mechanism to ensure their formal consideration, referral to responsible Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), and follow-up on decisions arising from their recommendations.

The House expressed concern that the absence of a clearly defined, government-wide framework requiring relevant MDAs to formally review and respond to strategic research recommendations could limit the effective utilisation of public investments in research.

The motion also warned that without an established process linking strategic research findings to national development plans, medium-term fiscal planning, sectoral policies and programme implementation, the government could overlook practical policy options for addressing recurring national challenges and improving public expenditure.

To address the concerns, the House expressed the conviction that institutionalising a formal Government Response to Strategic Research Recommendations mechanism would strengthen evidence-based governance, promote accountability and ensure greater value from publicly funded strategic research.

Under the proposed mechanism, relevant MDAs would be required to document whether recommendations referred to them were accepted, accepted with modification, deferred or rejected, alongside reasons for their decisions and proposed implementation measures where applicable.

The motion urged the Federal Government, through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning and other relevant authorities, to establish a coordinated framework for receiving, reviewing, referring and monitoring strategic research recommendations from NIPSS, NDC and NISS.

It also called on the government to integrate consideration of research recommendations into existing national development planning and budgetary processes, including the MTEF, Fiscal Strategy Paper (FSP), Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS) and annual budget preparation.

In addition, the motion urged the Office of the National Security Adviser, in collaboration with relevant defence, intelligence and security authorities, to establish procedures for the secure consideration and utilisation of strategic research findings from NDC and NISS, while safeguarding classified information and national security interests.

The lawmakers further called for a periodic reporting mechanism, through existing administrative and performance-monitoring structures, to track the consideration and implementation of strategic research recommendations, with appropriate summaries made available for accountability and policy evaluation, subject to applicable confidentiality requirements.

The motion also mandated the Committees on National Planning, National Security and Intelligence, Defence and Special Duties to engage the concerned institutions, monitor the establishment and implementation of the proposed framework, and report back to the House within four weeks.

The proposed measures are aimed at creating a more structured link between publicly funded strategic research and government decision-making, with the objective of improving policy coordination, institutional learning and the implementation of national development priorities.

World.title: US Asphyxiating, Illegal and Genocidal Blockade Policy Has Been the Main Factor Preventing Cuban Devt and That of Its People — Cuban Ambassador to Nigeria
World.content:
Miriam Morales is the Cuban Ambassador to Nigeria. She believes her country has been held back by several sanctions imposed by Washington and calls on Nigeria and other well-meaning countries to put an end to the sanctions that have brought sorrow, tears and blood to the people of Cuba. Michael Olugbode brings you an excerpt.

You have been in this country for some time now. What is your impression of Nigeria, its numerous cultures and its people?

It is a breathtaking and unforgettable positive impression. Multiculturalism enriches culture and, in general, the lives of people and countries. Nigerian culture is diverse and beautiful, and so are Nigerians. Getting along with Nigerians and learning every day about the country’s history, traditions and spiritual richness have been an enormous privilege.

Can you tell us about the highs and lows of your tour of duty so far in the country?

For every Cuban ambassador, the central objective is to develop friendly, mutually respectful and advantageous cooperation and relations, both with the peoples and the governments of the respective host countries. For a Cuban, being posted as an ambassador to an African country, in my case Nigeria, constitutes a great challenge, taking into consideration our great African heritage. Our histories and cultures are so deeply intertwined that only good things can come from relations between our peoples and governments. That alone makes any highs and lows totally irrelevant.

Anyway, life itself is full of highs and lows, and it is only our inner strength and resilience that enable us to move forward, find solutions and grow.

What is the bilateral relationship like between Nigeria and Cuba, and what are the trade figures?

Bilateral relations between Cuba and Nigeria were established in July 1974, and their 52nd anniversary was celebrated in July 2026. These relations are founded on deep historical, cultural and ancestral ties, as well as mutual respect.

We maintain a close partnership, traditionally focused on sectors such as health, education, human resource development, science and sports, including the exchange of scholarship recipients and the presence of Cuban medical personnel. There is a shared commitment to strengthening economic, political and cultural links for the benefit of both peoples.

Which areas do you think need improvement?

The current world situation, in which sanctions, blackmail, impositions and wars are being used instead of cooperation and diplomacy, is imposing heavy burdens on countries worldwide. That constitutes an undeniable fact, and I am not speaking specifically about Nigeria.

But let me tell you that your question could strongly stimulate the mind of any ambassador and lead to a situation in which there would not be enough space in your very important newspaper to publish the answers.

But, going straight back to your question, the global situation I was talking about is particularly demanding for a small country like Cuba. Cuba is the only country in the world subjected to the longest and most inhumane blockade in modern history, now coupled with new sanctions introduced weekly, a fuel blockade and the permanent threat of military aggression. All these measures are intended to turn my country back into a subjugated colonial state under US rule, as it was until January 1959.

However, Cuba has made resistance and creativity the core of its current endeavours. A new economic and social policy and programme is deeply transforming economic, trade, financial and investment relations, backed by powerful and enduring legislative activity. All these efforts are bringing Cuba into line with international standards for investment, cooperation and business in general, without abandoning the powerful social justice components that have always characterised our definition of socialism and will continue to do so.

I am confident that this entire process is already offering new possibilities for further developing a bilateral relationship such as that between Cuba and Nigeria, which has traditionally been guided by positive mutual interests.

An ambassador would rarely favour mentioning specific, isolated issues or areas where more could be done. Both countries will continue working together in areas where positive results have been achieved and will surely find new and diverse avenues to strengthen their bilateral relationship.

Nigerians used to go to Cuba for training in medicine, but that seems to have changed. What changed?

Bilateral relations between Cuba and Nigeria have always rested on mutual respect. The doors of the Latin American School of Medicine and those of every other higher education institution in Cuba will always be open to Nigerian students.

Cuba was a country that was on an upward trajectory, but this seems to have changed over time. What could have been responsible for this?

Almost immediately after the triumph of the Cuban Revolution, the US broke off relations and adopted a very hostile policy towards my country. From the very beginning, the main goal was to destroy the beacon of independence and sovereignty that the Revolution represented to all the subjugated countries in the Latin American region, which had suffered for decades under the oppression of successive dictatorships with direct political, financial and military support from Washington.

The current blockade policy is merely the codification and highest expression of all the aggressive actions set in motion by the US since the early years of the Revolution, including the military invasion internationally known as the Bay of Pigs invasion, which represented, for the US, its first military defeat in Latin America.

Cuba was then compelled to restructure all its economic, trade and financial relations and find new partners around the world. The former socialist countries of Eastern Europe, led by the Soviet Union at the time, became new partners for Cuba, based, in general terms, on shared political and ideological positions. Some other countries outside that bloc, in Africa, the Middle East and even Europe, also entered into this new relationship to varying degrees.

When the so-called socialist bloc in Eastern Europe collapsed and the former Soviet Union disintegrated, Cuba was once again left with almost no markets, trade, financial cooperation or investment. That dramatic situation led to the establishment of what became known as the Special Period in my country, severely affecting the upward trajectory you have referred to.

My country was once again compelled to rebuild all its external economic relations. Important socioeconomic changes were also introduced to adjust to the new and challenging situation. These included opening the country to mass international tourism and beginning to transform the Cuban legal system in relation to foreign investment.

Despite navigating a very difficult economic path, the country was eventually able to begin a new period of upward growth.

The situation in Latin America had started to change with the successive defeat of dictatorships and the establishment of progressive governments with different political characteristics. Strong South-South cooperation, in line with contemporary concepts, emerged but was attacked by Washington through various means. All this raised hopes across the region by opening the way for a new, qualitative form of cooperation.

In the case of Cuba and Venezuela, contrary to US propaganda, a highly mutually beneficial relationship developed, which also had a positive impact on the Latin American region. So, once again, to return to your question, this ushered in a new period of upward growth.

It is necessary to take into consideration that US hostility and its blockade policy against Cuba have persisted for more than six decades. Only changes in our region temporarily opened the way for Cuba, to use your words, to move upwards again. Throughout this period, we never lost sight of the fact that the US’s aggressive policy against my country was being permanently reinforced. It escalated immensely during Donald Trump’s first presidency and acquired a genocidal character with his return to the White House.

There have been weekly announcements of new sanctions, the introduction of a fuel blockade and constant threats of possible military aggression. I am sure you know the rest of that history, including the kidnapping of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and everything that followed. These developments have created a new and complicated environment, not only for Cuba but for the entire Latin American region.

Could the death of your great leader, Fidel Castro, have accounted for this, or perhaps the American blockade? Or is it that communism is no longer in vogue and your allies have dried up?

Without any country having truly experienced life under communism—which, in our view, cannot simply emerge from a proclamation—we consider it the highest level of socioeconomic development, social justice and well-being for all, without simplistic egalitarianism. It is an alternative for humanity to what several left-wing politicians, economists and philosophers have described as savage capitalism.

But that is only a rough definition. The overwhelming majority of Cubans still mourn, and will continue to mourn, the death of Commander-in-Chief Fidel Castro. His deeds and legacy remain, and will continue to remain, a political and human inspiration for the Cuban people as we continue building an alternative to brutal capitalism. We call it socialism.

The achievements and example of the Cuban Revolution are historically linked to Fidel Castro and the heroism of the Cuban people. Their influence extends far beyond our country, as you have surely seen in the celebrations of Fidel Castro’s centenary this year in Cuba and around the world.

The example and influence of the Cuban Revolution must, without any doubt, be immensely strong if we consider the genocidal and irrational hostility of the world’s foremost economic and military superpower in its attempts to destroy it.

The US’s asphyxiating, illegal and genocidal blockade policy has always been the main factor preventing the development of Cuba and its people, and it continues to be so today.

As the week drew to a close, Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel Bermúdez and Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla strongly rejected aggressive statements and threats made against Cuba by President Trump.

During a campaign rally in Fort Myers, Florida, Trump claimed that US warships would “pass by” Cuba upon returning from a war in Iran and stated that he would send Marco Rubio to “close the deal”—or, in other words, to negotiate the situation in the country. Subsequently, Marco Rubio, writing on his X account, publicly urged Cuban citizens to collaborate discreetly with the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) to push for political change on the island.

If not, what could explain US Secretary of State Marco Rubio leading a campaign of defamation, lies and hatred against the island and its people, while threatening, blackmailing and intimidating independent, sovereign states with the spectre of illegal sanctions in an effort to change their longstanding position of support for the UN resolution calling for the elimination of the economic, trade and financial embargo against Cuba on October 28?

What is the relationship between your country and America like? What about other countries, especially China and Russia, which have deep roots in socialism?

The Cuban government and people have no negative or hostile feelings towards the American people. In fact, there has been a growing sentiment among the American people in favour of a change in policy towards Cuba, with calls for the elimination of the blockade and descriptions of it as useless and obsolete. That sentiment is stronger today than ever before.

As for those in the White House, the Cuban government, even under the current circumstances, has reiterated its readiness to discuss any issue relating to bilateral relations on an equal footing. It also believes there are concrete areas for mutually beneficial cooperation.

In Cuba’s position, there is no room for impositions of any kind, dictating the type of political system Cuba should have or imposing changes in the Cuban leadership. Cuba will never surrender its independence and sovereignty.

Some communication channels remain open, although it has not been possible to establish an agenda for dialogue. Nevertheless, high-ranking representatives of the US government, including President Donald Trump, continue to claim from time to time that talks are taking place, as part of what we consider a disinformation campaign and an irresponsible appetite for fake news.

These claims have been accompanied by persistent hostile actions, such as last week’s decision by Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier to charge Army General Raúl Castro with conspiracy to commit first-degree murder. The charge was based largely on a federal indictment announced last May that included allegations concerning the downing of an aircraft belonging to the organisation “Brothers to the Rescue”, which Cuba considers a terrorist organisation.

There was also the US mission to the United Nations orchestrating an anti-Cuba event at UN headquarters, in what we consider a direct violation of the UN Charter, as part of the campaign surrounding the October 28 UN resolution on the blockade.

Our relations with Russia and China are based on deep-rooted historical ties, cooperation and exchanges in almost all areas of mutual bilateral interest, including international affairs. They also involve diverse organisations striving to place international collaboration in a different perspective, emphasising mutually beneficial projects and programmes within the framework of South-South cooperation.

Have you thought of meeting America halfway for the blockade to be lifted?

The Cuban government has reiterated several times that it is open to dialogue and negotiations on the basis I have already explained.

The blockade is really affecting Cuba. Do you think the international community has done enough to assist Cuba in getting it lifted?

On October 27 and 28, the UN General Assembly will consider, for the 34th time, the resolution entitled “Need to put an end to the economic, commercial and financial blockade imposed by the United States of America against Cuba”.

The overwhelming majority of UN member states have historically rejected the US blockade against Cuba, regardless of the potential risks. Threats, impositions, manoeuvres and blackmail have always existed, although never before as part of such an open international campaign, now prioritised by what remains of US foreign policy, which openly and shamelessly exhibits its brutal imperial characteristics.

For the first time, following the considerations made last July, the UN General Assembly will take a position through a resolution against the energy blockade, the fuel blockade and the collective punishment that such a policy represents for the entire Cuban people.

For decades, the international community has maintained a clear, longstanding and almost unanimous position in support of the immediate and unconditional elimination of the blockade against Cuba.

What is new, as I have already said, is the existence of such a brutal campaign, exemplified by an official US State Department document sent to its embassies, instructing them to exert pressure on host governments not to vote in favour of what it describes as “Cuban propaganda”. This is as though the blockade and its humanitarian consequences were not part of a reality that nobody can deny.

Even under these unbelievable circumstances, Cuba remains confident that the resolution will receive majority international support.

I would like to take this opportunity to express the profound gratitude of the Cuban government and people for Nigeria’s support in the international arena, most notably regarding its vote in the United Nations General Assembly against the economic, commercial and financial blockade imposed on Cuba. I reiterate that the vote will take place on October 28.

I am grateful to the newspaper THISDAY for providing the opportunity to present the situation in my country within the current context experienced by the Cuban people.

World.title: Tinubu Seeks Law to Bring Nigerians Convicted Abroad Home to Serve Jail Terms
World.content:
* President transmits amendment bill to Senate, seeks framework for prisoner transfers under bilateral agreements

* Senate orders probe of travel agencies over suspected human trafficking networks in Libya

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to amend the law governing the transfer of convicted offenders, seeking to empower Nigeria to enter into agreements with foreign governments to enable eligible Nigerians convicted abroad to serve their prison sentences at home.

The proposed legislation, known as the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Amendment Bill 2026, seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, Cap 216, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004.

Tinubu transmitted the bill to the Senate in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday.

The president explained that the proposed amendment would provide a legal framework for Nigeria to enter into agreements with other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders, while also enabling the country to honour similar requests from foreign governments under mutually agreed conditions.

In the letter, Tinubu said the bill sought to give effect to agreements between Nigeria and other countries on the transfer of convicted persons.

He stated: “The Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Amendment Bill 2026 seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, Act Cap 216, Laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 2004, to give effect to the provisions of any scheme or agreement for the transfer of convicted offenders between the Federal Government of Nigeria and the government of any other country.”

The president further explained that the proposed amendment would empower him to extend the application of the law to countries with which Nigeria had entered into relevant agreements through an order published in the Federal Gazette.

According to him, the provision would facilitate the implementation of prisoner-transfer arrangements, particularly with countries outside the Commonwealth.

After reading the president’s letter, Akpabio referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative consideration.

The proposed amendment comes amid several high-profile cases involving Nigerians convicted by foreign courts, including former public officials and political figures.

Among them is former Delta State Governor James Ibori, who was sentenced to 13 years’ imprisonment in the United Kingdom in 2012 after pleading guilty to money-laundering offences. He was released in 2016.

Former Deputy Senate President Ike Ekweremadu was sentenced to nine years and eight months’ imprisonment in the UK in 2023 over his role in an organ-trafficking conspiracy involving a young man.

Similarly, Abidemi Rufai, a former aide to Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment in the United States in 2022 for wire fraud and aggravated identity theft.

Nigeria and the United Kingdom already have a prisoner-transfer arrangement that allows eligible prisoners to serve their sentences in their home countries, subject to applicable legal requirements and the agreement of both governments.

The proposed amendment seeks to strengthen the domestic legal framework for implementing similar arrangements with countries outside the Commonwealth.

However, the proposed legislation would not automatically entitle every Nigerian convicted abroad to return home to serve a sentence. Any transfer would depend on the terms of the relevant agreement, the eligibility of the prisoner and the applicable legal conditions.

Meanwhile, the Senate has directed a comprehensive investigation into suspected human-trafficking networks and travel agencies allegedly connected to the trafficking, exploitation and abuse of Nigerians in Libya.

The resolution followed the adoption of a report on the urgent need to protect Nigerians from trafficking, slavery and other human rights abuses in the North African country.

Presenting the report on behalf of the joint committees on Diaspora, Judiciary, Foreign Affairs and Special Duties, Senator Anthony Yaro, representing Gombe South, said the committees had consulted relevant stakeholders, received memoranda and examined the circumstances surrounding the abuses before making their recommendations.

He said the recommendations were designed to strengthen Nigeria’s institutional response to human trafficking, improve the protection of victims and disrupt criminal networks responsible for exploiting vulnerable Nigerians.

The motion for the consideration and adoption of the report received the support of Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central.

In its resolutions, the Senate called for stronger enforcement of existing anti-trafficking laws, increased funding for the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) and other relevant agencies, and a comprehensive investigation into suspected trafficking networks and their associated travel agencies.

The lawmakers also called for the establishment of a national reintegration and protection programme for returning victims of trafficking.

They recommended that the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons coordinate the programme in collaboration with NAPTIP and other relevant institutions to ensure that returning victims received appropriate protection and support.

The Senate further urged the Federal Government to intensify diplomatic engagement with Libya through bilateral and multilateral channels to combat trafficking and promote safe and legal migration.

Contributing to the debate, Senator Neda Imasuen, representing Edo South, said the country’s major challenge was not the absence of laws against human trafficking but the failure to enforce existing legislation effectively and hold offenders accountable.

Imasuen’s position underscored concerns about the gap between Nigeria’s legal framework and the effective prosecution of individuals and networks involved in trafficking and exploitation.

In his remarks, Akpabio called for stronger deterrent measures against perpetrators of serious crimes, arguing that laws must carry sufficient consequences to discourage criminal conduct.

Recalling his tenure as governor of Akwa Ibom State, the Senate president said he had signed an anti-kidnapping law prescribing the death penalty and the forfeiture of property where a kidnapped victim was found.

He also advocated a strict Know-Your-Tenant policy, arguing that landlords should be able to provide information about their tenants when crimes were committed.

Akpabio warned that landlords who failed to provide relevant information could face questions over their possible complicity in criminal activities.

As part of its resolutions, the Senate directed NAPTIP to work with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Immigration Service, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to investigate identified travel agencies.

The agencies are expected to interrogate their directors, officers and agents to establish the extent of their involvement, if any, in recruitment networks, financial transactions and travel arrangements connected to the trafficking and exploitation of Nigerians abroad.

The investigation is expected to help identify the individuals and organisations facilitating the movement of victims, expose the financial channels sustaining trafficking operations and strengthen measures to prevent further exploitation.

The Senate’s resolutions also placed renewed emphasis on victim protection, the reintegration of returning Nigerians and diplomatic cooperation with Libya, alongside stronger law enforcement against suspected traffickers.

World.title: Six Killed in Fresh Attack on Plateau Community, Mutfwang Vows to Track Down Perpetrators
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Amid renewed security concerns in Plateau State, Governor Caleb Mutfwang has vowed to pursue the perpetrators of the deadly attack on Gero community in Jos South Local Government Area, where six residents were killed by armed assailants, according to police authorities.

The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday during the swearing-in ceremony of newly appointed Special Advisers at the New Government House, Little Rayfield, Jos, where he expressed deep sadness over the attack, describing it as disturbing and unfortunate.

The attack, which occurred on Monday night in Gero community, claimed several lives and has heightened concerns about security in parts of Plateau State.

Reacting to the incident, Mutfwang urged communities across the state to remain vigilant and work closely with security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could help prevent future attacks.

According to the governor, security operatives cannot be present in every location at all times and often rely on intelligence supplied by residents to respond effectively to emerging threats.

“The security forces cannot be everywhere; they can only cover some places. If they get information, they will react, but sometimes the reaction comes late because by the time the information gets to them, it is impossible to have saved the situation,” he said.

Mutfwang disclosed that investigators had already recovered crucial evidence from the scene of the attack and were actively pursuing leads that could result in the arrest of the perpetrators.

“This particular attack left some bits of evidence that we are trailing and, by the grace of God, we will continue to pursue these perpetrators of this dastardly act,” the governor said.

He further revealed that the suspected leader of a previous deadly attack on Kombun District in Mangu Local Government Area had been arrested, stressing that his administration would continue to support the prosecution of individuals linked to violent crimes across the state.

The governor maintained that security agencies had intensified operations against criminal elements in recent months and reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring that those responsible for violence face the full weight of the law.

Meanwhile, the Plateau State Police Command confirmed that six persons were killed during the Gero attack, revising an earlier casualty figure of seven provided by community representatives.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Alfred Alabo, the command said unidentified armed men invaded Gero community in the early hours of Tuesday and opened fire indiscriminately on residents.

The statement said the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Ayodeji Faniyan, immediately deployed riot policemen and tactical teams led by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations to the area.

According to the police, the operatives, working in collaboration with military personnel and Operation Rainbow, successfully dislodged the attackers, who fled into the surrounding hillside forest.

“The deceased bodies were evacuated to the morgue, while one victim who sustained injuries was rushed to the hospital for medical attention,” the statement said.

Police said investigations had been intensified to track down and arrest the fleeing suspects.

As part of efforts to reassure residents and assess the situation, CP Faniyan visited Gero community on Tuesday, where he met with traditional leaders, political representatives, youth and women leaders, as well as other stakeholders.

During the engagement, community leaders expressed concerns over the recurring security challenges and appealed for additional measures to prevent future attacks.

The police commissioner called for stronger collaboration between residents and security agencies, emphasising the importance of intelligence gathering and local vigilance in combating criminal activities.

He assured the community that the command would intensify efforts to apprehend those responsible for the attack while putting in place additional security measures to forestall a recurrence.

With six lives lost and fears of renewed violence hanging over the community, attention is now focused on the ongoing manhunt for the attackers.

Residents and community leaders say justice for the victims, coupled with a sustained security presence, will be critical to restoring confidence and preventing another tragedy in the troubled area.

World.title: Rising Sea Levels Could Threaten Lagos by 2050, Majekodunmi Warns
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Environmental activist and Chairman of the Lekki State Urban Forest and Animal Shelter Initiative (LUFASI), Dr. Desmond Majekodunmi, Tuesday warned that rising sea levels and the growing effects of climate change could threaten parts of Lagos by 2050, urging Nigerians to embrace sustainable environmental practices to avert an ecological crisis.

He stated that continued greenhouse gas emissions, deforestation, pollution and the destruction of biodiversity were worsening the climate crisis and putting communities at risk.

Majekodunmi made this known at the three-day international conference of Society for Environmental Toxicology and Pollution Mitigation (SETPOM), themed: ‘Driving Environmental Security, Innovation, and Resilience through AI, Research, Industry, and Regulation for Global Livelihoods,’ held at the University of Lagos.

He stressed the need for urgent collective action to protect the environment, warning that prioritising profit over people and the planet could have devastating consequences for future generations.

According to him, “The earth remains uniquely habitable because of its atmosphere, but human activities are increasingly threatening the natural systems that sustain life.”

He identified industrial activities, fossil fuel consumption, mining, deforestation, agricultural practices, waste disposal and transportation among the major contributors to environmental degradation and global warming.

Majekodunmi explained that rising global temperatures were intensifying the water cycle, contributing to heavier rainfall, flooding and other extreme weather events.

He cited the effects of coastal erosion and rising sea levels as particular concerns for Lagos, a coastal city vulnerable to the consequences of climate change.

He warned that continued emissions could worsen the situation, with potentially devastating implications for communities, infrastructure and institutions, including the University of Lagos.

The environmentalist called for greater public awareness and stronger commitment to sustainable development, saying: “Individuals, institutions, industries and governments must take responsibility for protecting the environment.”

He, however, expressed optimism that the climate crisis could be addressed through the adoption of renewable energy, improved waste management, recycling, scientific research, technological innovation and effective environmental regulation.

He identified solar, wind and water-based energy as potential sources of cleaner power, stressing that sustainable alternatives were available but required stronger commitment and investment.

Speaking with journalists, the President of the Society for Environmental Toxicology and Pollution Mitigation (SETPOM), Dr. Idowu Aneyo, stated that Nigerians must embrace behavioural change and leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) to protect the ecosystem and promote environmental sustainability.

Aneyo, a lecturer in the Department of Zoology at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), said although regulations were in place, particularly in Lagos State, effective environmental protection required greater public cooperation and a deliberate commitment to sustainable practices.

She commended the state government for its efforts in enforcing environmental regulations, noting that the major challenge was getting people to accept and adapt to the changes needed to protect the environment.

“There are regulations, especially in Lagos State. I want to say that the Lagos State Government is really trying to enforce them. It is just we humans that need to accept this change,” she said.

According to her, behavioural change remains difficult for many people, but individuals must be intentional about protecting the ecosystem.

She stressed the need for Nigerians to take personal responsibility for environmental preservation, adding that effective regulation must be complemented by public awareness and a willingness to adopt environmentally responsible practices.

Aneyo also emphasised the potential of AI and machine learning in addressing environmental challenges, noting that the technologies could help predict environmental risks, control damage and support sustainable ecosystem management.

“In the era of artificial intelligence, there is a lot that it can actually help to do. We need to use machine learning and AI to predict and also control some damage, and bring about sustainability of the ecosystem,” she stated.

The conference witnessed a debate competition among secondary school students, titled, ‘Harnessing Innovation and Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Sustainability Investments’.

It produced winners in the junior and senior categories who were rewarded with cash gifts and certificates.

World.title: Tinubu: South-east Must Move From Promises to Realities
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to industrialising the South-east, declaring that the region must move beyond promises to tangible economic development.

Tinubu spoke on Tuesday in Enugu at the launch of the South-east Gas Distribution Pipeline Infrastructure Project, an initiative of the South East Development Commission (SEDC), through the Southeast Investment Company (SEIC).

The project, launched in partnership with Gas Sync and NNPC Gas Marketing Limited (NNPC NGML), proposes a 400-kilometre pipeline network connecting the ANOH Gas Processing Plant in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the five South-east states.

The pipeline is expected to improve energy access, attract investments and stimulate regional economic growth.

Represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, the president said the project responded to the need for reliable energy infrastructure to support businesses and manufacturing in the region.

He called on investors, industrialists and manufacturers to explore the South-east’s economic opportunities, noting that energy security remained a key commitment of his administration under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

“Energy infrastructure will reduce costs, create jobs and expand opportunities. Nigeria has substantial gas resources, and the South-east has its fair share, but we must use them to create jobs and prosperity for our people,” he said.

Tinubu said manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than expanding their businesses, stressing the need for infrastructure that supports enterprise and industrial production.

“The prosperity of the region is inseparable from the prosperity of the entire country. We cannot achieve our full economic potential when any region operates below its economic potential,” he said.

In his address, Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, said inadequate energy supply and poor connectivity had remained major challenges to industrial development in the South-east.

According to him, unreliable energy increases production costs, limits business expansion and weakens the competitiveness of enterprises across the region.

Mbah said the proposed pipeline would provide opportunities for young people to build businesses and secure employment within the region rather than travel elsewhere in search of jobs.

“Enugu State alone has more than 20 tertiary institutions graduating young people annually,” he said. Reliable energy would help them turn their ideas into viable enterprises.”

“Enugu alone has four gas fields that remain unexploited. This shows the massive opportunities we have, and we also have reserves in other states. We cannot wait to see the project become a reality,” Mbah said.

The governor commended Tinubu for supporting the establishment of the SEDC, describing the commission as an important step towards addressing the region’s industrial development needs.

Earlier, the Managing Director of the SEDC, Mark Okoye, said the commission was committed to promoting inclusive prosperity and creating economic development opportunities across the region.

Okoye also proposed the establishment of a South-east Oil and Gas Week to bring stakeholders together to discuss investment opportunities and challenges in the sector.

The Deputy Governors of Ebonyi, Anambra and Imo States, Princess Patricia Onyemaechi, Dr Gilbert Ibezim and Chinyere Ihuoma, respectively, commended the SEDC for initiating the project.

They pledged their states’ cooperation to ensure its successful implementation.

World.title: Nasarawa Guber: Ex-IG Adamu Pledges to Prioritize Security As Ethnic Group Endorses Him
World.content:
Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia

A former Inspector General of Police (IGP) and gubernatorial candidate of the social Democratic party (SDP) in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has said his aspiration to govern Nasarawa State in 2027 is driven by the desire to uplift the common man.

Adamu stated this Tuesday in Doma, while responding to his endorsement as the preferred governorship candidate by the Alago ethnic nationality for the 2027 election.

The endorsement was announced during a rally organised by the Alago Support Group for IGP Adamu.

The former police boss first thanked God for the success recorded so far in his political journey, saying no success would have been possible without divine intervention.

He expressed appreciation to the Alago Support Group for the support and for agreeing to include them in his campaign, noting that the people have shown they will vote for him and, God willing, he will win the election.

“Because yesterday, the people gathered and the progressives as a whole came out and endorsed our candidate for governor. Also, the major tribe that is prominent here endorsed our candidate. We are grateful for the strong assurance they gave us that we will not face any hardship on election day,” he said.

Adamu said his decision to contest is for the common people who are suffering under the present situation, where mothers, children and youths are neglected while government focuses on things that do not concern their lives.

“Our coming out for this election is for the common people. We came out for the common man, to see that the common man does not suffer the way they are suffering now,” he stated.

He promised to prioritize the lives of the people if elected, with focus on quality education, quality healthcare and security.

“We will put people’s lives first, to see that education with quality is given to our people, health with quality our people have obtained, and the issue of security, we will see that everyone will find peace, so that people can return to their homes to sleep without any fear,” Adamu said.

He also raised the alarm over alleged vote-buying and collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from women to stop them from voting.

“Those who don’t have people following them are collecting cards in the hands of women; they are buying so as to stop them from coming out to vote. Therefore, anyone who collected a card, let them go and collect their card. Everyone should not agree to sell their card, and everyone should come out on election day with their card,” he urged.

Earlier in his address, the leader of the conveners, Danjuma Joseph, said the historic movement was conceived when they resolved that Alago could not remain on the sidelines while the future of Nasarawa State is being shaped.

Joseph said after thorough political and moral interrogation, they found in him a man of proven integrity, impeccable track record and uncommon patriotism who served Nigeria meritoriously to the pinnacle of his career.

He noted that Adamu is not a stranger to Alago land, as he shares deep historical and blood affinity with the people, having schooled with many prominent sons and daughters of Alago in Obi, and having maternal ties with Alago.

“We have resolved that we will no longer be onlookers or fence-sitters while the political destiny of our dear state is being decided. The time to participate, to take a stand and to take our destiny in our own hands is now,” Joseph declared.

He said there should be no acrimony over who Alago should support, citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution which guarantees freedom of association, and stressed that their constitutional and political choice remains IGP Adamu.

He added that the current political era is that of ‘Rainbow Coalition’, where one can remain in his party and still support any candidate of his choice, hence their action is not exceptional but a political alliance for the good of Alago and Nasarawa State.

“Your Excellency, this programme today is organised on the sacred sand of Alago ancestral land, in the name of Alago and in the interest of Alago. It is a political covenant, a bond of trust between you and Alago nation. By the grace of God, when you ascend as governor, do not forget Alago people,” he told Adamu.

Joseph said the group will traverse all Alago electoral wards in Nasarawa South and extend mobilisation to Nasarawa North and West Senatorial Districts to deliver Adamu.

World.title: SAPS jobs: More women than men apply as Gauteng leads the way
World.content:
SAPS has received more than 300 000 profile registrations as young South Africans apply for one of 5 500 available police trainee posts. Image: SAPS

The South African Police Service (SAPS) has received more than 300 000 profile registrations as thousands of young South Africans apply for one of 5 500 available police trainee posts.

The online recruitment portal opened on Wednesday, 21 October, recording 156 131 profile registrations nationwide in less than 24 hours.

The latest available data shows that more than 232 000 applicants had completed profile verification, while over 190 000 had started their applications.



A total of 172 721 applications had been completed and submitted for the available positions.

Gauteng leads SAPS applications

Gauteng has recorded the highest number of submitted applications, with 49 518, followed by KwaZulu-Natal with 33 661 and the Eastern Cape with 17 441.

The provincial breakdown is as follows:

Gauteng: 49 518

KwaZulu-Natal: 33 661

Eastern Cape: 17 441

When does SAPS recruitment close?

Only applicants who have not received an acknowledgement email should consider reapplying.

Applicants are also encouraged to use the portal outside peak hours where possible and to rely exclusively on official SAPS communication channels for recruitment information and updates.

The eRecruitment portal is available at https://erecruitment.saps.gov.za.



The recruitment drive closes on Friday, 13 November 2026. Prospective applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline.

World.title: WRAP | Australia stage fight back in Proteas decider at Newlands
World.content:
Marco Jansen was one of six South Africa wickets to fall to Mitchell Starc. Image: Marco Longari / AFP

Mitchell Starc said a “reset at lunch” led to an Australian fightback after South Africa made a flying start on the first day of the third Test at Newlands on Tuesday.

Starc finished with six for 72 as South Africa were bowled out for 329 shortly before the close in a match which will decide a series between the two leading Test nations.

‘Expected more out of the wicket’

It was a performance which looked unlikely as South Africa raced to 140 without loss at lunch after being sent in.



Starc was one of the bowlers punished, with the tall left-arm pacer conceding 39 runs in seven overs, including four successive boundaries by Marques Ackerman, who went on to score a rapid 95.

“We probably expected more out of the wicket,” said Starc.

“It was quite slow, with tennis ball bounce. They came at us hard.

“We didn’t have our best stuff in the first two hours but the last two sessions were right up there. It’s what we expect from this group. We had a reset at lunch and just tried to change the momentum in the field.”

Dazzling strokes

Ackerman, playing in his second Test, took the fight to the Australian bowlers with some dazzling strokes.

The slightly-built left-hander was on 82 not out at lunch, scored off just 75 balls.



He attacked veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon, dancing down the pitch and hitting him over the stand at midwicket for six. But he tried one shot too many after lunch and was stranded when Lyon pushed the ball wider, giving Alex Carey an easy stumping.

Ackerman, 30, said South Africa would probably have been happy if they had been offered a total of 329 before play.

But he admitted: “We probably left a few runs out there.”

Big scores

Ackerman, who won a place in the side through strong domestic performances and some big scores for South Africa A, including 256 against Bangladesh A in August, is not normally an opening batsman but said he was not troubled by the adjustment.

“I have quite often had to face a new ball in my career and playing against our own fast bowlers in the nets has been good preparation,” he said.

World.title: Gupta mansions in Saxonwold back on the market
World.content:
Two mansions linked to the Gupta family are back on the Johannesburg property market for R22 million combined. Image: File

Two luxury mansions linked to the Gupta family have returned to the property market in Johannesburg, with asking prices of R10 million and R12 million respectively.

The properties, situated in Saxonwold, are associated with Atul, Rajesh and Ajay Gupta, whose links to former president Jacob Zuma became central to South Africa’s state capture scandal.

READ | Two Gupta brothers still wanted by Interpol – Firoz Cachalia



According to Bloomberg, the one property, a seven-bedroom mansion, features an indoor swimming pool, a thatched outdoor entertainment area, a mini cricket pitch, water features and a garden containing endangered cycad plants.

The neighbouring 11-bedroom property includes a beauty parlour, a cinema lounge and a rooftop terrace.

According to the property s, sellers may consider offers below the asking prices.



Gupta properties struggle to attract buyers

The latest listings follow a private sale of the properties last year that fell through. At the time, the two mansions and a neighbouring three-bedroom house were sold for approximately 46% below their municipal value.

Kurt Knoop of Manci Knoop Financial Services, the business-rescue practitioner for Gupta-linked company Confident Concept, said the properties had been difficult to sell because of their association with the scandal and their condition.

“We’ve been battling to find buyers due to the stigma associated with the properties, and because of the poor state they’re in,” Knoop said.



However, he added that discussions with prospective buyers were under way and expressed hope that a sale could be concluded soon.

Confident Concept entered business rescue in 2018. Proceeds from the sale of the properties will help settle claims from creditors.

An open house is scheduled for this weekend, with prospective buyers required to provide identification and proof of funds before viewing the properties.



Mansions linked to state capture inquiry

The Saxonwold properties formed part of a compound associated with the state capture scandal, which involved allegations that private individuals used their relationships with political leaders and public officials to influence government decisions and secure state contracts.

A government-backed judicial inquiry into state capture heard that the Gupta brothers held private meetings at the properties. Evidence presented to the inquiry included allegations that influential guests were offered kickbacks and government positions in exchange for assistance in advancing the family’s interests.

The Guptas and Zuma have denied wrongdoing.

The scandal contributed to mounting political pressure on Zuma, who left office in 2018 as the African National Congress sought to stem declining electoral support.



Gupta brothers’ legal battles

The Gupta brothers left South Africa for Dubai shortly before Zuma resigned as president.

Atul and Rajesh Gupta, who have faced South African allegations including money laundering and fraud, were arrested in the United Arab Emirates in 2022 after Interpol placed them on its most-wanted list. They were also sanctioned by the United States and the United Kingdom.

In 2023, a UAE court rejected South Africa’s extradition request, and the arrest warrant was cancelled.



South Africa provisionally withdrew its arrest warrant for Ajay Gupta in 2019.

The return of the Saxonwold mansions to the market highlights the continuing challenge of selling high-value properties associated with one of the country’s most prominent political scandals.

World.title: Kaizer Motaung Jr replies to reports linking Mngqithi with Chiefs job
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs sporting director Kaizer Motaung Jr has rubbished reports claiming the club is in talks with Manqoba Mngqithi over the vacant coaching position.

Several reports have linked Mngqithi with a move to Amakhosi after the 55-year-old parted ways with Tanzanian giants Young Africans last week.

On X, user @InnocentKhabz claimed that talks between Mngqithi and Chiefs were ongoing. However, Motaung Jr responded directly to the post, dismissing the claims as “completely lies.”



The latest reports come days after Amakhosi were eliminated from the CAF Confederation Cup, raising further questions about the future of head coach Fernando Da Cruz.

There had been speculation about Da Cruz’s position following the disappointing continental campaign. Motaung Jr, however, issued a statement reaffirming the club’s support for the coach.

Mngqithi linked to Chiefs once again

Meanwhile, Mngqithi is currently a free agent following his departure from Young Africans.

The former Mamelodi Sundowns and Golden Arrows coach has previously revealed that Chiefs were interested in appointing him during his time at Chloorkop.

“Kaizer Chiefs did have interest in me. But someone blocked the move and I know who it is,” Mngqithi said.

“I have had very cordial talks with Chiefs, even with Kaizer Motaung Sn. It is not a lie. But it never reached any fruition because there are people who block these moves.”



The experienced coach added that he was not concerned about the individual who allegedly prevented the move from happening.

“I’m fortunate to know that the person who blocked it I am not even worried about. But it’s true there was interest recently,” he continued.

Despite Mngqithi’s availability and his previous admission of interest from the Soweto giants, Motaung Jr’s response has cast doubt on reports suggesting that the club is currently negotiating with the coach.

Mngqithi to Chiefs looks unlikely given Amakhosi management are backing Da Cruz.

Where should Mngqithi go?

World.title: Another top Springbok ruled out with injury
World.content:
As Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus prepares to reveal his end-of-year touring squad this week, a fair bit of time would have been spent making contingency plans for an ever-increasing injury list.

The likes of Handre Pollard, Eben Etzebeth and Andre Esterhuizen have all picked up recent injuries, while Cheslin Kolbe, RG Snyman and Kwagga Smith are also all unavailable.

It’s now been confirmed that veteran hooker Deon Fourie – who earned a memorable recall this year – has been added to that list after suffering a hamstring injury while in action with the Stormers.



“He’s not playing this weekend, that we can guarantee,” Stormers assistant coach Labeeb Levy confirmed on Tuesday. “The hamstring is a tricky one. It’s normally four to six weeks, sometimes longer.

“From what I remember of the medical report, an operation wasn’t necessary, which is good, but obviously it needs conservative management and treatment as well as going through all the various rehab protocols.

“But he’s definitely not playing this weekend … and then the re-evaluation process will just take its course.”



Springboks and Stormers counting the costs of a long injury list

The Springboks will need to now rely heavily on the services of Malcom Marx, and Johan Grobbelaar as back up, but the situation is even more dire at the Stormers after Fourie joined a couple of other injured hookers.

André-Hugo Venter (elbow injury) and Lukhanyo Vokozela (head knock) are both unavailable for the Cape club, and JJ Kotzé is still suspended.

SOS sent out

As a result of these injuries, Scarra Ntubeni has come out of retirement amid the crisis at hooker for the Stormers.



“Have we sent Scat an SOS call? Yes, we did. He’s just come into training,” Levy told the media. “We’ve got Vernon, who’s been training and playing as well, and then also the young (Altus) Rabe, who’s played in the Currie Cup.

“Scarra’s possibly the third one, in case there’s an injury in our training today, or on the captain’s run. He was in retirement. He trained a few weeks ago, but he’s just a stop-gap – a medical joker if you can call it that, in case something happens.

“But we’re looking around … we just need to get through this one ( Saturday’s round-five URC clash against Ulster).”
