This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Does One Phone Call Matter?

No government exists yet, so the call works as early recognition. It tells Belgrade’s political class that the EU sees the students, and not the outgoing ruling party, as the winner.

It also arrives before the official seat split is out. That split comes from the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), the state body that runs the count.

Vučić, who led Serbia as president until he resigned in September, conceded defeat after the vote. A public EU nudge toward a peaceful transition makes a late dispute harder.

How Big Was the Student Win?

Ipsos, a polling firm, and CeSID, a Serbian election monitor, projected from a full sample of polling stations that the Student List won 141 of the 250 seats and about 53% of the vote. Vučić’s United Serbia list is projected at 103 seats and about 38.8%.

A majority needs 126 seats, so the students would govern alone. A projection is an estimate, and RIK’s official seat split is what counts.

CeSID notes that its sample leaves out polling stations abroad. That could move a few seats in the final count.

Who Will Be Prime Minister?

That question is still open. Srdanović is one name traders price, though not the favourite.

The next steps are procedural but important. Parliament must meet and elect a government, and a presidential election is due to follow.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, an online prediction market, prices Dejan Šoškić, an economist and former central bank governor, at 37.0% to become prime minister. It gives Srdanović 15.5%, with US$3.48 million traded (read 2:11 p.m. ET, 27 October).

Kalshi, a prediction market regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal derivatives regulator, puts Srdanović at 19.0% in a thin market of 38,248 contracts. These prices are bets, not polls, and Kalshi lists a different name on top.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

Serbia is an official candidate to join the EU, so who governs Belgrade matters to Brussels and to investors in the region. A quick, peaceful handover would calm a country that has lived through nearly two years of street protests.

Watch two signals: the date parliament meets and the name put forward for prime minister. Until then, treat seat numbers as projections, not results.

What Is Not Known

Our sources do not give a final official seat split from RIK, so seat numbers here are projections. They also do not say when the new parliament will first meet.

Who the Student List will put forward for prime minister is also unclear. Costa’s post is a statement of support, not a commitment on EU membership talks.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is António Costa?

António Costa is the president of the European Council, the body that brings together the leaders of the 27 EU member states. He chairs their summits and speaks for them on major foreign questions.

Is Serbia in the European Union?

No. Serbia is an official candidate to join the EU, and Costa said on X that its place is in the Union.

Sources: António Costa on X; Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (RIK); Ipsos and CeSID projections; Polymarket; Kalshi. More in Serbia Election 2026.

World.title: Why Bolsonaro Allies Cry Persecution
World.content:
BRAZIL · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff, missed a Tuesday deadline to hand in his passports ordered by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes; the Bolsonaro family calls the court pressure political persecution.

— Why it matters The claim shapes how Brazil’s conservative camp answers its runoff defeat, and a White House notice of July 2026 uses similar persecution language about Brazil.

— The numbers Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and 3 months on 11 September 2025, Eduardo Bolsonaro to 4 years and 2 months on 16 June 2026, and President Lula won by about 4.4 million votes.

— Who is who Moraes sits on the Supreme Federal Court, Brazil’s highest court; Jair is the former president, Flávio his senator son, and Eduardo his son and former deputy living in the United States.

— What to watch Whether Flávio hands in or explains the missing passports, whether charges follow in the inquiry, and how Washington responds to the fight between the Bolsonaro family and the courts.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives about a 45% chance that Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate is charged or arrested by 31 October (27 October, 1:06 p.m. ET, thin market).

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you The orders hit named people, not visitors or firms, but the dispute adds political risk for holders of Brazilian assets and for US trade talks with Brazil.

Brazil’s defeated conservative candidate and his family say the courts are persecuting them. The dated court orders and the replies of judges and lawyers show a more contested picture.

Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff on Sunday, was ordered to hand in his passports and missed the deadline on Tuesday. He calls the order intimidation, and his family and allies call it political persecution by Brazil’s courts.

In a video on Monday, 26 October, he called the order “this aberration, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me.” He asked whether that is a reason to take his passport, adding: “Is this justice?”

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Happened This Week

Lula, the left-wing president, won Brazil’s runoff on Sunday, 25 October, with 51.79% of valid votes. Flávio, the conservative candidate, had 48.21%, a gap of about 4.4 million votes.

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes signed a passport order that night, and police served it on Monday, 26 October. It gave Flávio 24 hours to hand over his passports, barred him from leaving Brazil and banned contact with lawyer Willer Tomaz.

The order belongs to a sealed Supreme Court inquiry into suspected money laundering involving Flávio and Tomaz. Both deny wrongdoing, and no charge against Flávio has been made public.

On Friday, 23 October, his brother Eduardo told a US podcast he favoured Flávio leaving Brazil if he lost. Flávio says the order rests on that remark and that he never thought of leaving.

The deadline expired at 11:00 in Brasília on Tuesday, 27 October, and his defence had not delivered the passports. Sources in the Federal Police, Brazil’s national police, say the passports are now cancelled and he passed no regular border post.

An unconfirmed report says he crossed into Argentina, which his campaign coordinator, Senator Rogério Marinho, and Argentina’s government deny. The police are checking, and no official source has said where he is.

The Bolsonaro family’s Liberal Party, led by Valdemar Costa Neto, recognised Lula’s win in a note on Monday, 26 October. The note still asks for clarification of what it calls electioneering social spending.

The Persecution Claim in Their Own Words

On Monday, 26 October, Flávio said: “It wasn’t I who lost, it was the system that won.” He said he would seek to revoke Lula’s ticket, alleging the “largest vote buying” in Brazilian election history without presenting evidence.

On Saturday, 22 November 2025, Flávio called his father’s jailing by Moraes “one more proof of religious persecution.” He said the court was criminalising a prayer vigil he had called.

On Thursday, 8 October 2026, Flávio said online that Moraes was trying to “create a factoid” in the middle of the election. He urged the judge to “resign and answer in court for your acts.”

His father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, told reporters at Brasília airport on Monday, 25 November 2024: “I am persecuted all the time.” The Federal Police had indicted him for a coup plot days earlier, which he denied.

The Court Record Behind the Claim

The record shows orders from two courts in separate cases, each with a stated reason. The main ones follow in date order.

Friday, 30 June 2023: the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled 5 to 2 that Jair is ineligible until October 2030, over a July 2022 meeting where he attacked electronic voting.

the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled 5 to 2 that Jair is ineligible until October 2030, over a July 2022 meeting where he attacked electronic voting. Thursday, 11 September 2025: the Supreme Court’s First Panel convicted Jair 4 to 1 of attempting a coup, with 27 years and 3 months in prison. Justice Luiz Fux dissented.

the Supreme Court’s First Panel convicted Jair 4 to 1 of attempting a coup, with 27 years and 3 months in prison. Justice Luiz Fux dissented. Saturday, 22 November 2025: Moraes ordered preventive detention, citing a recorded ankle-monitor violation, a vigil called by Flávio and allies who fled abroad, such as former aide Alexandre Ramagem. The Federal Police asked, and the prosecutor-general agreed.

Moraes ordered preventive detention, citing a recorded ankle-monitor violation, a vigil called by Flávio and allies who fled abroad, such as former aide Alexandre Ramagem. The Federal Police asked, and the prosecutor-general agreed. Tuesday, 16 June 2026: the First Panel unanimously convicted Eduardo of coercion in legal proceedings, with 4 years and 2 months, for seeking US sanctions against the judges during his father’s trial.

the First Panel unanimously convicted Eduardo of coercion in legal proceedings, with 4 years and 2 months, for seeking US sanctions against the judges during his father’s trial. Wednesday, 7 October 2026: Moraes ordered Eduardo’s arrest to start his sentence and cancelled his passports, made public on 8 October. Eduardo, who lives in the United States, called it arbitrary; see Eduardo Bolsonaro’s prison order.

Moraes ordered Eduardo’s arrest to start his sentence and cancelled his passports, made public on 8 October. Eduardo, who lives in the United States, called it arbitrary; see Eduardo Bolsonaro’s prison order. Friday, 23 October 2026: Moraes froze up to BRL 6 billion (about US$1.2 billion at the central bank rate of 5.0377 per US dollar) of assets linked to Tomaz. That is a ceiling, not a sum found.

Moraes voted in the 2023 electoral ruling, was rapporteur of the coup trial and signed the Eduardo and Flávio orders. Flávio urged him to resign on 8 October, and the camp sees one judge behind every case.

What the Courts and the Government Say

In the Eduardo ruling on 16 June 2026, the court said coercion harms the administration of justice, not the judges. Moraes called his statements a “clear and ostensive attempt to coerce this Panel.”

On Sunday, 23 November 2025, in Johannesburg, Lula said Jair “will serve the sentence the court determined.” He said “the court made a decision” and that everyone knows what Jair did.

On 29 July 2026 the presidency’s communications office called the US persecution charge “unfounded and untrue.” It said Brazil’s judiciary follows the Federal Constitution and that the branches of government are independent.

What Independent Lawyers Say

Jurists split on Jair’s detention on 22 November 2025. Miguel Reale Júnior, justice minister under President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, said there was “no other possible measure” to secure criminal law.

Gustavo Badaró, a University of São Paulo professor who wrote an opinion for Jair’s defence, called the flight risk “speculative.” Lawyer André Marsiglia called jailing someone for the acts of third parties unconstitutional.

These views concern Jair’s detention, not Flávio’s passports. We found no independent analysis of the passport order.

What It Means for US Readers

The US Treasury sanctioned Moraes on 30 July 2025 and removed him from its list on 12 December 2025. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had called him “judge and jury in an unlawful witch hunt” against US and Brazilian citizens and companies.

On 28 July 2026 the White House extended a national emergency on Brazil for one year. Its notice says members of Brazil’s government are “politically persecuting a former President of Brazil, his family, and his followers.”

That language echoes the family’s claim, and Brazil’s government rejects it. See how Washington reacted to Lula’s win, whether he can overturn the result and Brazil and the United States explained.

We found no US government comment on the passport order yet. The Brazil hub and São Paulo page track the wider picture.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a platform where users bet on events, lists a market on whether Flávio Bolsonaro is charged or arrested by 31 October. The last trade implied 45% at 1:06 p.m. ET on Tuesday, 27 October.

About US$15,300 has been traded, with little liquidity, bids near 31% and offers near 45%. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

No official source has said where Flávio is, or why the passports were not delivered. The order text is not public, and the Supreme Court press office said it had no information.

Allies expect Moraes to consider preventive detention, but no arrest order has been reported. It is not known whether charges will follow, or whether the electoral court will act on his planned request.

No Brazilian court has accepted the persecution claim in a ruling we found. The Bolsonaro camp does not accept the court record.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Bolsonaro persecution claim?

The Bolsonaro family and allies say Brazil’s courts and a left-leaning establishment target them politically. The Lula government rejects that, and the courts say their orders follow specific cases.

Why was Flávio Bolsonaro told to hand in his passports?

Justice Moraes signed the order on the night of Sunday, 25 October, in a sealed money-laundering inquiry. The reasons are not public, and no charge has been made public.

Is Jair Bolsonaro in prison?

He was convicted on 11 September 2025 and sentenced to 27 years and 3 months. He serves it under humanitarian house arrest with an ankle monitor, extended in July.

What do the courts and the Lula government say?

The Supreme Court says coercion cases protect the administration of justice, and Lula says Jair must serve the sentence the court set. Brazil’s government says the judiciary follows the Constitution.

Does this affect US travellers or investors?

The orders name individuals, not visitors or companies. Investors face more political risk, and the real recovered to 5.33 per US dollar on 27 October after 5.50 on 26 October.

World.content:
The Central Bank of Brazil headquarters in Brasília. File photo. Photo: Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Brazil Economy · Household Debt · Central Bank

Published Tuesday, 27 October, 12:59 PM ET · Source: Banco Central do Brasil

Key Facts —The number. 20.3 million Brazilians are at-risk borrowers, up 75% since June 2021 and 17% of everyone with debt. —The strain. Families now spend more of their income on debt payments than at any point in 21 years. —The banks. The central bank says the financial system is sound, with comfortable capital and cash buffers. —Prediction markets. Brazil’s central bank saw no relevant threat to its banks on Tuesday, then spent much of its report worrying about their customers. About 20.3 million Brazilians now count as at-risk borrowers, people showing at least two signs of financial strain, a 75% jump in about five years.

The warning comes in the bank’s half-yearly Financial Stability Report, which covers the first six months of 2026. It lands as high interest rates weigh on households in Brazil’s economy, Latin America’s largest.

In Plain English Central bank: Brazil’s monetary authority, which also supervises banks.

Who Counts as an At-Risk Borrower

The central bank flags a borrower when at least two warning signs appear together. Those signs are a payment more than 90 days late, debt payments above half of income, use of several costly credit types at once, or leftover income below the poverty line.

By that test, 17% of all people with debt in Brazil’s financial system were at risk in June 2026. The 20.3 million total is 75% higher than in June 2021.

Why Families Are Stretched

The report says household problem assets reached their highest level since 2012 in most credit types, with missed payments the main driver. Problem assets are loans that are overdue or in trouble.

The share of family income going to debt payments is the highest in 21 years.The central bank expects the risk of missed payments to stay under pressure in the short term.

The Banks Are Fine, the Customers Less So

The central bank’s stress tests show lenders can absorb an adverse scenario. It describes capital and liquidity, the cash that banks keep on hand, as comfortable.

That split matters for investors. Bank shares can hold up while the people who borrow from them struggle, until bad loans start to eat into profits.

What the Central Bank Does Next

Officials say they are studying tougher rules for the riskiest credit lines to curb over-indebtedness. Last week it adopted three measures against inadequate or abusive credit offers and for clearer terms before a loan is signed.

The rate path matters too. On Polymarket, a prediction market where traders bet real money, the odds are 60.3% that Brazil holds rates at its November meeting and 33.0% that it cuts by 0.25 percentage points.

What It Means for US Readers

Brazil’s large banks and fintechs, such as Itaú (ITUB), Banco Bradesco (BBD) and Nubank (NU), trade in the US as ADRs, shares of foreign companies listed in New York. Rising bad loans are the main thing shareholders watch, alongside the wider Brazil stock market and the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ), a fund that tracks Brazilian shares.

The central bank’s concern is with unsecured credit, and newcomers who borrow in Brazil should read the terms closely. Our dollar-to-real guide explains how the real’s moves change what a debt costs in dollars.

What Is Not Known

The report does not say how many of the 20.3 million are already in default, or how soon the new rules will arrive. It also gives no date for when household strain might peak.

World.title: Brazil Orders Foreign Interference Probe
World.content:
BRAZIL · ELECTION

Key Facts — What is happening A Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered national police on Tuesday, 27 October, to investigate suspected foreign interference in the presidential election.

— Why it matters The inquiry asks whether foreign money or platform algorithms helped the losing conservative candidate, with a US network and two US companies mentioned in the decision.

— The numbers Five lines of inquiry in one Supreme Court case filed in 2024; no charge has been filed and no wrongdoing has been established.

— Who is who Justice Flávio Dino signed the order; candidate Flávio Bolsonaro lost the 25 October runoff to President Lula.

— What to watch Whether police find any foreign money, and whether Bolsonaro’s camp or the US groups mentioned respond to the order.

— What it means for you Meta and Polymarket are mentioned in the decision; travel and trade rules for US visitors and firms are unchanged.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

A Brazilian justice has told federal police to check whether foreign money or online platforms helped one presidential candidate. The order opens an inquiry, not a case.

Justice Flávio Dino of Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered a foreign interference probe by the Federal Police on Tuesday, 27 October. It asks whether foreign money, paid posts or algorithms helped conservative Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday’s runoff; these are suspicions.

Three groups mentioned in the decision are American: a conservative fundraising network, a prediction-market platform and the owner of Instagram. No US official is accused in the reports reviewed, and no US government response has been found.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Foreign Interference Probe Covers

Dino issued the decision inside Supreme Court case ADPF 1178, filed in 2024 by Ibram, Brazil’s mining industry institute. That case asks whether Brazilian towns may sue abroad over disasters such as Mariana, a fatal dam failure.

Dino refused to handle the election claims inside that case. He ordered separate proceedings under court supervision, citing possible involvement of members of Congress.

The Workers’ Party (PT), led by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, had asked him to act. Dino did not let the party join the case, but he found the claims serious enough to investigate.

Renan Santos, a defeated candidate of the small Missão party, made similar claims to the electoral court. That court, the Superior Electoral Court, runs and judges Brazil’s elections.

The order names Rockbridge Network and businessmen Tallis Gomes and Pedro Sang. Its five lines of inquiry are questions for police, not findings.

Whether talks between Rockbridge Network and businessmen Tallis Gomes and Pedro Sang involved money, services or other benefits for a campaign.

Who paid for election posts by foreign-based profiles, some citing Polymarket betting data, and where the money came from.

Whether talk of political funding is tied to foreign interest in Brazil’s rare earths and critical minerals.

The purpose and participants of contacts between Rockbridge representatives and Brazilian businesspeople.

Whether internet companies deliberately skewed algorithms to help or harm candidates.

Rockbridge is a US network of conservative businesspeople and investors. Brazilian reports say Vice President JD Vance helped found it in 2019.

Polymarket is a US betting platform that Brazil has blocked since 2024. Dino also sent his decision to federal bodies, including the intelligence agency Abin and the Central Bank.

Why It Matters

Dino wrote that Brazilian law bans foreign election financing, including indirect help such as services or advertising. Brazil’s Constitution also bars political parties from taking money from foreign entities or governments.

The order came two days after Lula won the runoff. It turns a campaign-season complaint about US-linked money and platforms into a formal police inquiry.

Rare earths are metals used in electric-vehicle motors and military hardware. The US Geological Survey puts Brazil’s reserves at 21 million tonnes, a large share of a world total above 90 million.

Dino stressed that rare earths and critical minerals belong to the Union, Brazil’s federal government. Opening an inquiry does not mean any irregularity has been found.

What It Means for You

Meta and Polymarket are US companies mentioned in the decision. Whether police will contact them has not been stated.

Nothing in the order changes travel, trade or tariff rules for US visitors or companies. The inquiry is a Brazilian police matter under Supreme Court supervision.

The probe lands while Brazil awaits a US tariff offer. The earlier interference complaint explains how it began.

See also Washington’s reaction to the vote and the court order barring Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving Brazil. The Brazil hub tracks the wider story.

What Is Not Known

No public evidence shows that Rockbridge money reached the Bolsonaro campaign. No deadline for the inquiry has been published.

No response from Flávio Bolsonaro, his Liberal Party (PL), Rockbridge, Gomes or Sang to the order had been found by Tuesday evening. In earlier statements, Gomes and Sang denied raising or moving election money.

The members of Congress who may be involved are not named. Nor is it known whether the US government has a position.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Justice Dino order?

He ordered the Federal Police to open an inquiry into foreign money, paid posts and platform algorithms in the election. The Supreme Court will supervise it.

Is Flávio Bolsonaro accused of a crime?

No. The order opens an investigation and does not find that anyone broke the law. No charge has been filed.

Why do rare earths appear in an election case?

Dino wants police to check whether electoral support was offered in return for access to Brazil’s rare-earth minerals. Rare earths are metals used in magnets for electric vehicles and defence equipment.

Does this affect US travellers or investors?

The order sets no new rules for US visitors or businesses. It does place US companies, including Meta and Polymarket, in the reasoning of a Brazilian police inquiry.

Sources: Supreme Federal Court, case ADPF 1178, decision of 27 October 2026; Supreme Federal Court, summary of the Ibram filing; US Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, rare earths; Constitution of Brazil, article 17 (accessed 27 October 2026).

World.title: Colombia Confirms Exit From Hague Group
World.content:
COLOMBIA · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — What is happening On Tuesday, 27 October 2026, Colombia’s government confirmed it is leaving the Hague Group, a bloc of states acting on Israel. The Foreign Ministry first announced the exit on Thursday, 15 October.

— Why it matters The exit reverses former president Gustavo Petro’s policy and moves Colombia, a long-time US security partner, closer to Israel. It also costs the group one of its two co-chairs.

— The numbers The group was founded on 31 January 2025, with eight founding states by Colombia’s count. Colombia and South Africa co-chaired it, and Bolivia and Honduras had already left.

— Who is who Presidency spokesperson Miller Soto explained the decision for conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella, in office since 7 August 2026. Foreign Minister Omar Bula made the first announcement.

— What to watch Watch for a reply from South Africa, the other co-chair, and the remaining members, and for the date the withdrawal takes effect.

— Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you For US readers it shows where a close security partner now stands on Israel, one of the most divisive issues in Latin American diplomacy.

Colombia’s government has confirmed it is leaving a group of countries that coordinates action on Israel. The exit was first announced on 15 October and reverses the previous government’s policy.

Colombia’s government confirmed on Tuesday, 27 October 2026 that it is leaving the Hague Group. The bloc coordinates legal and diplomatic steps by states over Israel’s war in Gaza.

The Foreign Ministry first announced the exit on Thursday, 15 October, so the 27 October statements explain a decision already taken. It matters to US readers because Colombia is a long-standing US security partner now realigning on Israel.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Colombia Said About Leaving

Presidency spokesperson Miller Soto presented the decision in a video on the Presidency’s social media account. He said Colombia is leaving both as a member state and as co-chair of the group.

Soto said, in Spanish, that the foreign relations of a serious country cannot be run like a “club of ideological activism”. He added that Colombia’s diplomacy should reflect its historical values and favour cooperation and open markets.

A Foreign Ministry statement the same day rejected using the group to attack or isolate other sovereign states. It said foreign policy should serve democratic and historical values and avoid ideological activism.

Foreign Minister Omar Bula had made the first announcement on 15 October, saying Colombia “officially requested its withdrawal”. In his words, the group was “created to isolate and attack Israel”, an approach Colombia rejects.

The ministry said Colombia stays committed to multilateralism, international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes. It added that Colombia will keep working for peace, justice and security through the United Nations.

Bula spoke during a visit to Israel, after Colombia opened its new embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday, 14 October. Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, attended, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the Jerusalem embassy opening.

Colombia restored diplomatic relations with Israel in August 2026, after Petro cut them in 2024. The government also says it withdrew in September from South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

What the Hague Group Is

The group was founded on 31 January 2025 in The Hague, in the Netherlands. Colombia’s government counts eight founding states: Bolivia, Colombia, Cuba, Honduras, Malaysia, Namibia, Senegal and South Africa.

The group calls itself a global bloc for coordinated legal and diplomatic measures defending international law and standing with Palestinians. Members spoke of steps such as limiting arms transfers to Israel and backing international court rulings.

Colombia and South Africa chaired the group together until now. Bolivia and Honduras had already left, according to the Colombian government.

Colombia’s government now describes the group’s purpose as hostile to Israel. The group itself says its work defends international law.

Why the Colombia Hague Group Exit Matters

The step completes a turn in foreign policy under conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella, in office since Friday, 7 August 2026. His left-wing predecessor, Gustavo Petro, had broken ties with Israel and helped lead the group.

The exit also separates Bogotá from South Africa, which brought the genocide case that Israel disputes. For Washington, it moves a major Latin American partner closer to Israel’s position.

What It Means for You

The statements named no change to visa rules, trade or travel advice, so travellers and exporters face no new rule from them. Companies with business tied to Israel should still watch for follow-up decisions.

Investors in Colombian assets should treat this as a political signal rather than a market event. The statements named no trade, arms or sanctions step.

For wider context, read how Colombia and the United States relate and the Colombia hub. Colombia’s earlier visa waiver for Israelis belongs to the same shift.

In Plain English

Hague Group: a bloc of countries, founded in 2025, that coordinates legal and diplomatic action over Israel’s war in Gaza.

a bloc of countries, founded in 2025, that coordinates legal and diplomatic action over Israel’s war in Gaza. Foreign Ministry: the Colombian government department, called the Cancillería, that runs foreign policy.

the Colombian government department, called the Cancillería, that runs foreign policy. Co-chair: one of two countries, Colombia and South Africa, that led the group together.

one of two countries, Colombia and South Africa, that led the group together. Presidency spokesperson: the official, Miller Soto, who explains the president’s decisions to the public.

the official, Miller Soto, who explains the president’s decisions to the public. International Court of Justice: the United Nations’ top court, which settles disputes between states.

What Is Not Known

No reaction to the exit from South Africa, the group itself or Israel’s government was found. The date the withdrawal takes effect and the formal procedure were not stated.

Colombia counts eight founding states, while the group’s own website also lists Belize. Whether Colombia will reverse measures adopted as a member, and any US government comment, are also unknown.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Hague Group?

It is a bloc of states set up on 31 January 2025 to coordinate legal and diplomatic steps on Israel and Gaza. It says it defends international law and stands with the Palestinian people.

When did Colombia announce it was leaving?

The Foreign Ministry announced it on Thursday, 15 October 2026. The government confirmed and explained the exit on Tuesday, 27 October.

Why did Colombia leave the Hague Group?

Foreign Minister Omar Bula said the group was created to isolate and attack Israel, and that Colombia rejects that approach. The exit follows Colombia’s restored ties with Israel in August 2026.

Which other countries have left?

Bolivia and Honduras left before Colombia, according to the Colombian government. Five states from Colombia’s founding list remain, including South Africa.

World.title: Brazil Plans Fiscal Target Bill After Rout
World.content:
BRAZIL · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Brazil’s Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, that the government is preparing a bill to steer the budget toward the centre of its fiscal target.

— Why it matters Brazilian stocks and the real fell hard on Monday after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election, and the bill is meant to reassure investors.

— The numbers The Ibovespa stock index fell 13.88% on Monday and the dollar closed near 5.40 reais. The 2026 target is a surplus of 0.25% of GDP, about US$6.4 billion.

— Who is who Durigan has run the Finance Ministry since March 2026. Lula, of the left-leaning Workers’ Party, won a fourth term over conservative Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

— What to watch Watch for the bill’s text and its date in Congress, the choice of Lula’s new economic team, and whether the Treasury keeps buying back bonds.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US investors in Brazilian shares, bonds and New York-listed companies get a first sign of how tightly Lula’s next government plans to control the budget.

Brazil’s finance minister says a new bill will push the budget toward its target. The plan follows Monday’s market rout after the election.

Brazil is preparing a bill to steer its budget toward its fiscal target, Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Tuesday, 27 October. The Brazil fiscal target plan follows a day when stocks fell 13.88%.

Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy, and many US funds hold its shares, bonds and New York-listed companies. Durigan gave no text or timetable for the bill.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

A fiscal target is the budget result a government promises for the year, counted before interest on its debt. Brazil calls it the primary result, and a surplus means revenue is higher than spending.

What Happened on Tuesday

Durigan spoke to reporters at the Finance Ministry on Tuesday morning. He said the government would take a bill to Congress so that it can pursue the centre of the target.

“We will seek the centre of the target,” he said in Portuguese. He said the bill would give the government legal tools so that there is no doubt about that aim.

Durigan described the measure as a complementary bill, a type of law that needs an absolute majority in both houses of Congress. He did not describe its content or say when it would be sent.

He added that other measures are being studied. He said President Lula would first choose his team, and that the team would then present the adjustment measures.

How the Fiscal Target Works

Brazil’s fiscal framework, in force since 2023, sets a yearly target with a tolerance band of 0.25 points of GDP either side. The goal counts as met if the result ends inside that band.

Congress approved the 2026 budget guidelines law on Thursday, 4 December 2025. It sets a surplus of 0.25% of GDP, about 34 billion reais (about US$6.4 billion).

That law also lets the government use the lower edge of the band when it decides how much spending to freeze. Aiming for the centre instead would demand a bigger budget effort.

The 2027 target is higher, at a surplus of 0.5% of GDP, or 73.2 billion reais (about US$13.7 billion). The band floor is 36.6 billion reais (about US$6.9 billion), under the 2027 guidelines bill sent to Congress in April.

Durigan did not say which year his bill covers. The 2027 bill lets it deduct 65.66 billion reais (about US$12.3 billion) of costs, such as court-ordered payments.

What the Markets Did

On Monday, 26 October, the first trading day after the runoff, the Ibovespa, Brazil’s main stock index, fell 13.88%. The dollar rose about 8% to close near 5.40 reais; Brazil’s central bank said its official daily rate rose 9.2% to 5.50.

Durigan called the moves a change of positions, not a loss of trust in public accounts. He said the market had been betting on the victory of a particular candidate.

Investors had expected Flávio Bolsonaro, a conservative senator and son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, to win and cut spending. Lula won the Sunday, 25 October runoff and begins his new term on 5 January 2027.

The National Treasury, which manages Brazil’s public debt, also bought back bonds on Monday. It offered up to 15 billion reais (about US$2.8 billion) of fixed-rate bonds due in 2031, 2033 and 2037.

It bought about 7.1 billion reais (about US$1.3 billion) of those bonds and a similar sum of inflation-linked bonds. Durigan said the buyback helped bring stability to the market.

What It Means for US Readers

American investors in Brazil funds and in New York-listed shares of Brazilian companies felt the rout. The bill’s wording will show how firmly Lula’s next government intends to hold spending in check.

A weaker real also makes Brazil cheaper for US visitors, but it raises costs for Brazilian firms that owe dollars. Read the Monday market report and the election results for the background.

For wider context see the guides to the Brazil stock market and to inflation, interest rates and the Selic. More is on the Brazil hub.

In Plain English

Fiscal target: the budget result Brazil promises each year, before interest on debt.

the budget result Brazil promises each year, before interest on debt. Primary result: revenue minus spending, not counting interest payments.

revenue minus spending, not counting interest payments. Tolerance band: the 0.25-point margin either side of the target that still counts as success.

the 0.25-point margin either side of the target that still counts as success. Complementary bill: a law that needs an absolute majority in both houses of Congress.

a law that needs an absolute majority in both houses of Congress. Ibovespa: the main index of shares traded on Brazil’s stock exchange.

What Is Not Known

The content of the bill and the date it goes to Congress are not public. It is also unclear whether it targets 2026, 2027 or later years.

The size of any extra spending freeze is not known, nor whether the Treasury will repeat the buyback. Lula has not named his new economic team, so it is not known who will serve as finance minister from January.

What Comes Next

Lula picks his team before the term starts on 5 January 2027, and Durigan said that team will present the measures. Congress must then pass the bill by an absolute majority.

The bill is a signal, not yet a spending cut. It does not by itself change the 2026 budget result.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Brazil fiscal target?

It is the yearly budget result the government promises, before interest on debt. For 2026 it is a surplus of 0.25% of GDP, with a band of 0.25 points either side.

What does aiming for the centre of the target mean?

Today the government may aim for the lower edge of the band. Aiming for the centre would demand a bigger budget effort.

Is the Brazil fiscal target the same as the budget deficit?

No. It is the primary result, which leaves out interest on debt, so it differs from the full deficit. Brazil’s 2026 goal is a primary surplus.

Why did Brazilian markets fall on Monday?

Durigan said investors had bet on a different winner and reversed their positions after Lula won. The Ibovespa fell 13.88% and the dollar closed near 5.40 reais.

World.title: Mexico Murder Count Passes 50,000 This Term
World.content:
MEXICO · SECURITY

Key Facts — What is happening TResearch, a private Mexican polling firm, puts murder victims since President Claudia Sheinbaum took office at 50,174 by Monday, 26 October 2026.

— Why it matters The toll is far below the rate of the previous term, yet violence still drives US pressure on Mexico over cartels, fentanyl and trade.

— The numbers TResearch counts 66 victims a day this term against 95 before; the government’s own figure was 42.2 a day in September 2026, a different measure.

— Who is who Sheinbaum, a leftist, has led Mexico since 1 October 2024; the SESNSP is the national public-security agency; INEGI is the statistics office.

— What to watch Watch for official October figures in November, and whether TResearch’s weekly average, 37 a day on 26 October after 43 on 17 October, rises again.

— Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US travellers, investors and policymakers get a data point that killings have fallen but remain high, as Washington presses Mexico on cartels and trade.

A private count says more than 50,000 people have been murdered in Mexico since Claudia Sheinbaum became president. Official figures show a steep fall.

The Mexico murder count has passed 50,000 since President Claudia Sheinbaum took office in October 2024, says TResearch, a private polling firm. Its tracker shows 50,174 victims in 756 days, to Monday, 26 October 2026, two years into a six-year term.

This matters to US readers because Washington presses Mexico on cartels, fentanyl and trade, and violence is central to that pressure. The figure is an estimate, and the government says killings have fallen by about half.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Mexico Murder Count Shows

TResearch counts victims of intentional homicide, meaning murder and other deliberate killings. Its total averages 66 victims a day over 756 days, or one victim about every 22 minutes.

Under Sheinbaum’s predecessor and political ally, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, TResearch counts 95 a day. Sheinbaum’s average is therefore about 30% lower, though the total still passes 50,000.

How TResearch Builds the Count

TResearch does not count bodies itself. It starts from the daily preliminary tally of the Federal Security Cabinet, which gathers reports from state prosecutors and federal agencies.

For finished months it uses official data: INEGI, the national statistics institute, to December 2025, then the SESNSP. The SESNSP is the Executive Secretariat of the National Public Security System.

The two measures are not like for like, because TResearch’s term total mixes INEGI figures for 2024 and 2025 with SESNSP months. TResearch’s own conversion puts INEGI counts about 19% above SESNSP counts, so its 66 a day should not be set against 42.2.

What the Official Figures Say

On Tuesday, 13 October, Sheinbaum and Marcela Figueroa, head of the SESNSP, said intentional homicides fell 52% in two years. Daily averages fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.2 in September 2026, the lowest September since 2015.

The SESNSP counts victims in murder investigations opened by the state prosecutors. INEGI instead counts death certificates, and its preliminary 2025 figure was 27,989 presumed homicides, down 16.6% from 33,550 in 2024.

Critics say some killings are filed under other crimes. Sheinbaum answered in July that “homicide is homicide” and that the figures are not dressed up.

Is the Trend Still Falling?

TResearch’s own data show a rebound since August and a partial retreat since mid-October. Its seven-day average rose from 32 a day on 7 August to 43 on 17 October, then fell to 37.

Official monthly averages stayed between 41 and 45 a day from June to September. TResearch counts 13,601 victims in 2026 to 17 October, 47 a day, down 30% on 2025.

TResearch projects about 20,300 victims for 2026, the lowest year since 2014, on an INEGI-equivalent basis. The 13,601 and 47 a day above use the lower SESNSP basis, so the two are not directly comparable.

What It Means for US Readers

Killings have fallen sharply but remain high, so security stays a live issue between Washington and Mexico City. Officials say seven states account for half of 2026 killings: Baja California, Guanajuato, Chihuahua, Sinaloa, State of Mexico, Guerrero and Morelos.

For context, read Mexico and the United States explained and Mexico geopolitics, US tariffs and China. An earlier report on the 53% drop claim and the Mexico hub give more background.

In Plain English

TResearch: a private Mexican polling and research firm led by Carlos Penna.

a private Mexican polling and research firm led by Carlos Penna. SESNSP: the government agency that publishes monthly crime counts from state prosecutors.

the government agency that publishes monthly crime counts from state prosecutors. INEGI: Mexico’s national statistics institute, which counts deaths from certificates.

Mexico’s national statistics institute, which counts deaths from certificates. Intentional homicide: murder and other deliberate killings, the category all three counts use.

What Is Not Known

TResearch’s own tracker, updated on 27 October, shows 50,174 victims in 756 days to 26 October. Its method note says the daily count is preliminary and is calibrated to SESNSP and INEGI figures.

No single official total for the term exists, so it is unknown whether official data alone pass 50,000. No government or opposition reply to the TResearch figure was found by Tuesday evening.

What Comes Next

The SESNSP is expected to publish October figures in November. INEGI released its 2025 count in early August 2026, so its 2026 count is not due until about mid-2027.

TResearch publishes a daily report, so its total will keep rising. A rising total alone does not show a worse trend, because the daily rate matters.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is TResearch?

A private Mexican polling and research firm led by Carlos Penna. It says it has run more than 3,000 studies since 2017 in 13 countries, and its homicide count builds on official data.

Is the 50,000 figure official?

No, it is a private estimate built from official sources. The government has not published a total for the term.

Are killings in Mexico rising or falling?

Official data show a fall of about half since September 2024. TResearch’s count shows a smaller rebound since August, then a dip in late October.

How does this term compare with the last one?

TResearch counts 66 victims a day now against 95 under López Obrador. INEGI recorded 33,550 homicides in 2024 and 27,989 in 2025.

Why do the counts differ?

The SESNSP counts investigations by prosecutors, INEGI counts death certificates, and TResearch blends both with a daily tally. Each method gives a different number.

World.title: Peru Red Rain Alert as River Hits 30 Homes
World.content:
PERU · WEATHER

Key Facts — What is happening Peru has issued a red rain alert for Tuesday, 27 October, to Thursday, 29 October, strongest in Tumbes and Piura, after a Monday river surge in Kimbiri.

— Why it matters Heavy rain and flooding are arriving as Peru braces for El Niño, a warming of the Pacific that the weather service expects to bring more intense rain from November.

— The numbers The alert covers 11 regions until 23:59 on Thursday; Tumbes stations recorded 30 to 50 millimetres of rain overnight; eight people were rescued in Kimbiri.

— Who is who Senamhi is the national weather service; Indeci is the civil defence institute; Werner Salcedo is governor of Cusco, where Kimbiri lies.

— What to watch Whether rain eases after Thursday, how many families in Kimbiri need shelter, and how heavy November rain becomes.

— Power Index Peru ranks 5th of 14 in Peru ranks 5th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 54.7 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US visitors should expect flooded streets and delays in northern Peru, ask operators about Cusco travel, and check the State Department advisory.

Peru’s weather service has raised its red alert for heavy rain on the north coast and in the highlands until Thursday. A river surge in the Kimbiri valley has already left dozens of families needing help.

Peru has issued a red alert for rain of strong to extreme intensity, running from Tuesday, 27 October, to Thursday, 29 October. Tumbes and Piura, on the north coast, face the strongest downpours.

On Monday, 26 October, a river surge in Kimbiri, in the Cusco region, damaged homes and trapped eight people, who were rescued. US travellers should check conditions before heading to the north coast or the Cusco highlands.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Happened in Tumbes and Piura

Senamhi, Peru’s national weather and hydrology service, has issued notice No. 440 at red level. The alert ends at 23:59 on Thursday, 29 October.

The notice covers 11 regions in all, including Cusco and Puno, with snow expected above 3,900 metres (12,800 feet) in the south. Tumbes and the inland coast of Piura face stronger rain than the others.

Rain began in Tumbes on Monday night, moderate at first, and grew heavy in the early hours of Tuesday, according to Senamhi. By Tuesday morning, streets and homes were flooded, mostly in Zarumilla province and in Tumbes city.

Tumbes stations recorded 30 to 50 millimetres (1.2 to 2 inches) of rain between Monday and 6 a.m. on Tuesday. The education office in Zarumilla moved classes online.

Nelson Quispe, a Senamhi specialist, said similar totals should continue for two more days. He linked the storms to warm sea-surface temperatures.
