World.title: Karmen Turk: Why Estonia's gambling license is not attracting foreign operators
World.content:
Estonia has strengthened its regulations through economic and money laundering crises, but along with the rules, the procedural environment has also changed, no longer conforming to good practice but instead deterring international companies, attorney-at-law Karmen Turk writes.

No one is disputing that a gambling operator is required to combat money laundering. The law requires it. The question lies elsewhere: do Estonia's rules prevent money laundering, or do they primarily act as a barrier to new companies coming to Estonia? Unfortunately, experience over the past year points more towards the latter.

The recently amended Remote Gambling Tax Act has brought into focus international opportunities for financing Estonia's state budget and, in particular, sport and culture. The environment here could be attractive given the purpose of an Estonian license is simple: to bring tax revenue earned elsewhere into digitally advanced Estonia. International remote gambling operators will not be targeting Estonian players. Their customers are in other countries, around the world. An Estonian license, however, means that taxes on their activities are paid into Estonia and go towards financing our sports and culture. Every license brought into Estonia is thus a victory for Estonian culture and sports, yet without increasing gambling in Estonia. To achieve this goal, however, companies need to actually come to Estonia. But what is deterring companies today? The simple answer is: fear-driven regulation that diminishes the legal opportunities created in Estonia, because every applicant is treated primarily as a potential risk.

To explain in more detail, a gambling operating license is issued by the Tax and Customs Board (MTA), but it must first be approved by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). The applicant must submit their internal anti-money laundering regulations, appoint a person who will communicate with the FIU (the so-called contact person), and submit documents concerning its owners and managers. Companies already operating must meet these requirements by January 1, 2027, at the latest. Gambling operators are now essentially treated in the same way as financial companies and cryptocurrency firms are. The purpose of stricter rules is understandable. The problem lies in how they get applied in practice.

The contact person must work in Estonia

Under current law, the contact person must be working on a permanent basis in Estonia. The FIU's training materials even state that "the entire department should be located in Estonia." In addition, the contact person must have suitable education, experience and an impeccable reputation, while the FIU must approve their appointment.

What does our regulation mean for an international company? Usually, the people responsible for its anti-money laundering controls work in the same location as its IT and payments teams would do, for example in Latvia, Italy or Malta. In order to obtain an Estonian license, however, it must find someone who works in Estonia, understands the risks of the gambling sector and passes the FIU's checks. The FIU has also indicated that one person may serve as a contact person for no more than two companies, and must have a replacement during vacation periods. In reality, consequently, one contact person is not sufficient; two experts meeting the same criteria are needed – but this is an over-regulation of the requirements. Estonia is small and there are few such specialists. This is as a result not merely a formality, but a real barrier to market entry.

Where the contact person sits says nothing about the quality of their work. The FIU's own updated guidelines do not mention location either. They require the contact person to report directly to the management board, to be competent and to have access to all the necessary information at all times. Even an entire department can serve as the contact person. None of these conditions depends on the country. On the contrary, actual knowledge and control are more effective when they are "close" to the operations themselves. According to the FIU's own data, the sector's real weakness is also the detection of suspicious transactions. In 2025, only about 14 percent of reports were related to genuine suspicions, while nearly 94 percent of all reports came from only about a tenth of all companies. This problem is solved by a good monitoring system and a skilled team, not by whether the contact person sits in Tallinn or in Rome. If a company's international team is stronger than an individual specialist who can be found in Estonia, the Estonian requirement may n fact weaken controls. This also raises a question of EU law. Companies with Estonian licenses often belong to groups managed in other EU countries and mainly serve foreign customers. The EU guarantees companies the right to operate and provide services in other member states. The European Court of Justice has allowed countries to restrict gambling, but only if the restriction has good grounds, genuinely helps achieve its objective, is applied consistently and does not go further than necessary. Estonia's location requirement is questionable in light of the last two conditions. First, it is not consistent: according to the FIU's guidelines, customers from other EU countries are considered lower risk, but a specialist working in another EU country is considered a risk. Second, less restrictive solutions exist. It would be sufficient for the contact person to be available at all times, communicate with the FIU in Estonian and ensure that the FIU has access to the data. In addition, a uniform EU anti-money laundering regulation will take effect on July 10, 2027. It is therefore appropriate to ask whether Estonia's additional requirements, which the EU does not demand, are even still necessary.

Documents must be in Estonian

The second obstacle is the language requirement. According to the experiences of companies, the FIU requires internal rules and other documents be in Estonian. It is natural that communication with the authority would take place in Estonian. However, an international company's internal rules are an everyday working tool. They are used by employees in various countries and so get written in a language that everyone understands. If a separate Estonian-language version has to be prepared for Estonia, two documents are created: one that is actually used at work and another that is shown to the authority. This contradicts the FIU's own objective, however. The FIU will check exactly whether the rules are actually being used or exist only on paper. The updated guidelines state that the rules must be understandable to employees and describe what the company actually does. In the case of customer documents, the guidelines themselves recommend avoiding translation if the original is in a comprehensible language, such as English. There is no requirement in the guidelines for internal rules to be in Estonian. The obligation to translate does nothing to help combat money laundering.

A procedure whose duration and outcome are unknown

In 2024, the Chancellor of Justice examined the FIU's licensing procedures and identified several problems. First, the FIU does not tell applicants when all their documents are in order. As a result, applicants do not know when the statutory 60-day deadline for making a decision starts. Second, in the course of an interview, an applicant may be advised to replace the contact person, an owner or a management board member, or to withdraw the application, but these interviews are not logged in the minutes. Based on the experiences of several companies from 2026, these interviews have gone on for hours, with three to four officials questioning one person all at the same time. For a company planning investments in Estonia, uncertainty of this kind is the worst possible signal. An official refusal can be challenged in court. However, if the outcome of the procedure depends on interviews that are not recorded in minutes, the company will simply choose another country where the procedure is clear and predictable.

Rules must be based on actual risks

The state fully knows what the sector's risks are. According to the national risk assessment, the money laundering risk posed by gambling operators is high because Estonian licenses are used mainly to serve foreign customers and business partners are often located abroad. The FIU focuses on the origin of funds, the use of front persons, the splitting of transactions and cryptocurrency. These are the right issues. But having the contact person live in Estonia or the rules written in Estonian does nothing to counter these risks. What is needed is good transaction monitoring, rapid information exchange and access to data for the FIU. The latter is already guaranteed by law, even when the server is located abroad.

The law itself requires proportionality: the extent of controls must correspond to the risk and be reasonable. The same should apply to the state when it decides what to require of a new market entrant. Penalties are already severe: a fine of up to €1 million can be imposed for violating the requirements for internal rules.

Estonia does not have to choose between strict anti-money laundering controls and an attractive license in order to regulate the market and generate tax revenue. But the success of controls must be measured by whether they stop suspicious money flows. Neither an office address in Tallinn nor the language of the documentation demonstrates this.

The author of this piece advises international gambling operators.

World.title: Almost 400 migrants detained in Estonia since July
World.content:
Since July, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) has detained 388 foreign nationals who arrived in Estonia without a legal basis after crossing the Belarusian border. Detentions in recent weeks have taken place exclusively in Tallinn.

As of Tuesday, 258 foreign nationals were being held at the detention center in Tallinn, while 148 people who entered the European Union via the Belarus-Latvia border have been handed over to Latvia.

"Each handover is essentially a logistical operation, the success of which requires verified information about the foreign nationals' routes, origins and intentions, as well as agreements between the authorities of both countries," said Indrek Aru, head of the border guard bureau at the PPA's Northern Prefecture.

Foreign nationals are transported back in groups.

Fifteen people are suspected of organizing illegal migration.

Medical attention

Detainees at the detention center have also sought medical attention due to health problems, including cold-like symptoms and skin rashes.

"Foreign nationals with high fevers were taken to West Tallinn Central Hospital, which provides healthcare services to the detention center. As of today, one foreign national remains hospitalized, and it is known that they will be able to return to the detention center in the coming days," Aru noted.

The hospital does not provide the detention center with detailed information about tests carried out or diagnoses.

"Due to personal data protection requirements, diagnoses are not disclosed to the detention center, but in the event of a health risk, the center's staff receive all the necessary information from medical professionals to immediately implement measures to limit the spread of disease, including isolation or quarantine," Aru said.

World.title: Tallinn mulling 1+1 and 2+1 lane options for Tulika tänav renovation
World.content:
Preliminary designs have been released for the renovation of Tulika tänav and the section of Paldiski maantee that intersects with it in Tallinn's Kristiine district, and the street will be rebuilt with either 1+1 or 2+1 traffic lanes.

Ahead of the renovation of Tulika tänav, which connects the Kristiine traffic junction and the Sõle intersection, Tallinn is considering two options: rebuilding the street with either 1+1 or 2+1 traffic lanes.

Both solutions will include new sidewalks, cycle paths and street greenery. A traffic study has been carried out to find a suitable solution, and the final choice will be made after assessing spatial possibilities and the needs of different modes of transport.

Tallinn Deputy Mayor Kristjan Järvan (Isamaa) said that he and Tallinn Deputy Mayor Joel Jesse (Center) prefer the 2+1 option.

"Our clear view is that this location cannot accommodate a 1+1 solution, and our firm preference is 1+2," he noted.

However, no decision has yet been made. "When making the final decision, we will naturally take residents' feedback into account," Järvan said.

The reconstruction will also include the renovation of water supply and sewerage facilities, the construction of a separate stormwater drainage system and improvements to street lighting.

Feedback on both options can be submitted until November 10.

World.title: Swedbank lays off 100 in Baltic states, warns AI could mean more cuts
World.content:
Swedbank is laying off around 100 staff in Estonia and the other Baltic states, while the bank says Artificial Intelligence (AI) could lead to further layoffs in future.

Swedbank CEO Olavi Lepp said the company is laying off employees across the entire group, meaning both in the Baltic states and in its home nation, Sweden, with redundancies to total around 500.

"Naturally, in the process, we are also offering existing employees the opportunity to retrain for other roles, but this does not suit everyone and, unfortunately, layoffs are also needed," he said.

Lepp added that Swedbank employs more than 6,000 people in the Baltic states, of whom around 100 have been laid off. The layoffs are linked to a general restructuring of work and investments in development, he went on.

Lepp explained that when the bank experienced a period of very high profitability a few years ago, it decided to invest more in IT development and data modeling, adding some of the aims have been accomplished. "Today, when profitability is at normal levels, we do not need as many people," he said, adding that when development work is not being carried out on a large scale, it makes no sense to retain employees at the same level.

Lepp said in any case there will certainly be jobs in the future that require fewer people. "Then it depends on the company's own sales and strategy what it does next: whether it reduces the number of employees or tries to increase business volumes with its existing workforce."

He added that it is currently unclear whether companies developing AI will meet investors' expectations on profitability. "The big question is that when they become profitable, meaning they start charging the proper price for their services, how much will the software licenses and tokens that we pay AI companies for then cost?"

There are currently more than 90 applications across the Swedbank group in which AI is being tested. Lepp said that so far as Estonia goes, the primary objective is to do more business with the same number of people — increasing business capacity and market share, and in some contexts reducing costs.

In implementing AI, a company needs to carry out a standard cost comparison, and if using tokens is cheaper than employing people, layoffs or retraining will probably follow. "I would say that when it comes to tasks governed by fairly formal logic, the capabilities of artificial intelligence are certainly much greater than those of humans in a great many cases," Lepp went on.

The bigger question, he added, is whether there will be customers from whom profits can be earned. "There have to be people somewhere who consume these services, and they, too, have to earn their income from somewhere," Lepp noted.

Swedbank's net profit in Estonia for the first nine months of this year came to €193 million, €2 million more than in the same period in 2025.

World.title: Estonian foreign minister briefed on Norway-Finland call with Putin
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said he had been briefed on Tuesday's call between the leaders of Norway and Finland and Russia's President Vladimir Putin.

A statement from the Finnish president's office described the call as "a follow-up of the meeting in Oslo on October 20 and held in consultation with Ukraine."

The call was initiated by Finland and Norway, which border Russia, and its aim "was to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations to help to end the war to President Putin." The statement said it was related to the upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi between Russia and Ukraine.

While Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen was critical of Tuesday's call, Tsahkna said that only increased pressure on Russia will make it take peace negotiations seriously.

He added that there is currently no indication whatsoever that Russia has changed its strategic objectives or is genuinely interested in negotiations.

Only increased pressure on Russia will make it take peace negotiations seriously. Every contact with Russia must convey Europe's unity and determination to support Ukraine and maintain pressure on Russia, while making clear that Europe will not negotiate away the fundamental principles underpinning its security. Ukraine wants peace, and Estonia supports all efforts to achieve it. But there is no indication that Russia has changed its strategic objectives or is genuinely interested in negotiations. Russia's goal is not merely to seize parts of Ukraine, but to subjugate the entire country and undermine Europe's security order, founded on NATO and the EU. A just and lasting peace requires increased pressure on Russia, tighter sanctions, action against sanctions evasion, Russia's international isolation and unwavering support for Ukraine. We must show Russia through concrete action that, as long as its war continues, pressure will remain strong and Ukraine's supporters will not abandon it. — Margus Tsahkna (@Tsahkna) October 27, 2026

Putin believes that Western support for Ukraine may weaken, which is why he remains motivated to continue the war, Tsahkna said.

"As long as Putin believes that time is on his side, he will continue the war," the minister said, referencing Russia's recent attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

He added that it was important to Estonia that every contact with Russia conveys Europe's unity and determination to support Ukraine and maintain pressure on Russia.

"It is also important to make clear that Europe will not negotiate over the fundamental principles underpinning its security arrangements. These include the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity, the understanding that borders cannot be changed by force, and every country's right to decide its own security arrangements," he added.

The eight Nordic and Baltic countries are some of the strongest supporters of Ukraine and often coordinate positions and release joint statements.

World.title: Estonia has run out of asphalt, says Tallinn deputy mayor
World.content:
Estonia is experiencing a shortage of asphalt as factories in Sweden and Lithuania are currently not supplying it to the country, Deputy Mayor Kristjan Järvan (Isamaa) has said

"I have to start with some sad news. Namely, Estonia has run out of asphalt," Järvan said at a Tallinn city government press conference on Tuesday.

The official said Estonia usually imports bitumen from two sources in Sweden and Lithuania.

"And for reasons still unknown, the Swedish company decided not to bring any more. It said that the ship that arrived three weeks ago would be the last this year. The next one will come in the spring. The Lithuanian company was delighted, immediately raised its prices, and then its factory broke down. This means that asphalt plants in Estonia can no longer obtain bitumen," the deputy mayor said.

Kristjan Järvan Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"What this means nationally is that those construction companies that have their own asphalt plants probably have their own contracts covered and, as usual, any surplus asphalt is put on the open market," he added.

Tallinn is affected by the issue as the second supplementary budget set aside money for roadworks this autumn.

"Now both of the City of Tallinn's partners have said that, unfortunately, the market situation is such that asphalt is simply unavailable. And this means that we are in a situation where we can happily announce that we have asphalt for resurfacing Liivalaia. We have to take a positive view of what we have," Järvan said.

Asphalting work on Liivalaia began on Monday, and Tallinn will grant an additional two weeks for this work, the deputy mayor added.

"But this also means that we will not take the risk of milling up Viljandi maantee and Vabaõhumuuseumi tee to lay new asphalt there. We will still avoid a situation where we have streets dug up for the winter and no asphalt to put down in their place," Järvan said.

World.title: Christopher Moseley, champion of Estonian literature in English, dies
World.content:
Christopher Moseley, the Australian-born translator and language teacher who devoted his career to bringing Estonian, Latvian and Nordic literature to English-language readers, has died. He was 76.

Moseley was born in Australia and came to Britain in 1974 to study Scandinavian languages, but his interests soon moved somewhat eastwards to Finland and the Baltic states, even while the latter countries were still shackled under the Soviet occuption.

He studied Finno-Ugric languages in Finland and the UK, and his fieldwork on Livonian between 1987 and 1993 was his first direct work with a minority language. It led to his Master's thesis at the School of Slavonic and East European Studies (SSEES), part of the University College London (UCL), and later to his book Livonian (2002).

He also authored the Estonian language installment of British publisher Routledge's "Colloquial" range, and co-authored its Latvian course too.

For many years he taught Estonian language and Baltic literature at SSEES and UCL, along with evening courses in Estonian and Latvian. He also worked as a translator and journalist specializing in Baltic affairs at BBC Monitoring for nearly two decades, before becoming a freelance translator and editor.

Moseley's own translations from Estonian into English included A.H. Tammsaare's classic "Põrgupõhja uus Vanapagan", Andrus Kivirähk's "The Man Who Spoke Snakish", Indrek Hargla's "Apothecary Melchior" series, and Ilmar Taska's "Pobeda 1946". His final translation, Rein Raud's "The Sun Script", was published by Norvik Press just this year.

From 2008 Moseley was General Editor of UNESCO's Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger, which became a key reference for the world's threatened languages. He was also a dedicated member of the Foundation for Endangered Languages.

In 2018, he was one of the speakers at the opening of the University of Latvia's Livonian Institute.

The Estonian Literature Center remembered Chris as a warm and friendly person with unceasing passion for languages and literature.

World.title: Estonian media association: Meta is planning the largest theft of content
World.content:
Estonian media companies have warned US tech giant Meta's new business terms would let it use news content without consent or payment.

The companies are urging the European Commission to intervene over the terms, due originally to take effect October 30.

The Commission says Meta has postponed them to 20 November, following discussions, but the Estonian Association of Media Companies (Eesti meediaettevõtete liit) says the delay changes little.

The Estonian Association of Media Companies has appealed to policymakers and regulators over Meta's new business terms, which would require business users — including news publishers — to grant Meta permission to access their web content by automated software. Meta could then index, store, search and update that content for its business purposes, without separate permission or payment.

Meta initially sought the right to use content for AI training. After publisher protests, it removed the word "training," but the association says the remaining terms are broad enough to permit AI-related use anyway.

In the association's view the terms threaten media business models, as Meta could build competing products from journalistic content without paying for it. Publishers now face a choice: allow the use of their content, or lose a key channel for reaching readers.

Media association board member Väino Koorberg called the development potentially the largest theft of content, while in the U.S., the News/Media Alliance, representing nearly 2,000 American publishers, has written Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg, demanding the terms be withdrawn. A further four European publishers' organizations have approached the Commission with similar concerns.

Väino Koorberg. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

"In European Union terms, Meta is a so-called major gatekeeper, on whose activities the visibility of others hinges, hence why stricter rules have been established for them," Koorberg said.

He added that Meta is also testing restrictions on link sharing on Facebook. "Only two links can be shared free of charge during a month," he said, which serves to limit the platform as a marketing channel.

The association says the situation threatens access to reliable information: more than half of people get daily news from social media, and reduced visibility for journalism could increase vulnerability to disinformation.

Koorberg said Estonia should send a clear message. "For example, state institutions can end cooperation with Meta and leave those platforms, because the change in terms also affects them," he said.

Elis Paemurd, deputy head of the European Commission Representation in Estonia, said Meta had postponed the terms to November 20 following discussions, adding that the Commission is ensuring Meta complies with EU law, including the prohibition on abuse of a dominant position.

Koorberg said the delay does not mean media have escaped. "Meta itself explains that it wants to specify and clarify how the terms should be interpreted," he said, adding that it may be a step toward neutralizing possible legal action. The association has told members to follow developments closely, and that the most extreme step would be to end all cooperation with Meta's products.

Estonian media companies have warned US tech giant Meta's new business terms would let it use news content without consent or payment.

World.title: Iraq’s general budget to exceed $300 billion in 2032
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi projected on Monday that the country’s federal budget will exceed $300 billion in 2032.

Al-Zaidi’s remark took place during his meeting with a large group of Iraqi businessmen operating in different sectors as part of his official trip to the Jordanian capital, Amman.

The prime minister noted that Iraq is on track to reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels of crude oil per day by 2032.

The Iraqi government will start the implementation of the Development Road project in 2027, according to al-Zaidi. He explained that work at the al-Faw Grand Port will continue around the clock to turn Iraq into a commercial hub connecting the East and the West.

Al-Zaidi pointed out that Iraqi entrepreneurs should take advantage of these opportunities to make investments in the industrial zones that would be developed as part of the Development Road project in the future.

The doors are open for Iraqi businesspeople to develop projects in accordance with the Iraqi investment laws, according to al-Zaidi.

The Iraqi prime minister added that the government is eager to attract investments by facilitating procedures, protecting domestic products, and providing tax exemptions.

World.title: Iraq reviews Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has held a coordination meeting with the prime minister’s advisor and representatives from the Italian design consultancy BTP Infrastrutture to review the engineering plans, feasibility studies, and routing for Iraq’s multi-billion-dollar Development Road project.

The western Tigris route has been confirmed as the optimal alignment for the 1,200-kilometer (approximately 745 miles) multimodal corridor, linking the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq through multiple provinces up to the Turkish border.

The project features a dual-track railway, designed for high-speed passenger trains up to 300 km/h and freight trains up to 120–140 km/h, running parallel to a modern several-lane highway network.

BTP Infrastrutture was contracted to deliver technical and economic feasibility studies, preliminary designs, and detailed engineering plans for the railway and highway portions.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Drone shot down in Baghdad’s Green Zone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Security Media cell (ISMC) said on Tuesday that a drone was shot down near Baghdad’s fortified ‌Green Zone.

The explosion from the interception created a loud noise that was audible in various areas of the Iraqi capital.

The US embassy’s air defense systems were triggered after spotting two drones nearing the Green Zone’s boundary and shooting them down, according to two Iraqi security sources who spoke to Reuters.

Debris from the two drones was found at two places, and security personnel were investigating the drones’ origin and destination further, according to the sources.

The Green Zone houses government buildings and foreign missions, including ⁠the US embassy. The US Embassy in Baghdad has faced multiple rocket and drone attacks since the outbreak of the regional Middle East war, which escalated following US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

Iran-aligned militias have repeatedly targeted the sprawling diplomatic compound in retaliation for the conflict. Significant incidents reported at the embassy complex since the war began.

In July, US air defenses intercepted and shot down an armed drone hovering directly over the embassy compound at night. The incident occurred hours after a separate rocket attack on a western Iraqi base housing US soldiers.

The constant threat of incoming rockets, missiles, and drones prompted the US State Department to issue a travel warning for Iraq.

US citizens have been repeatedly urged to leave the country immediately using overland borders, and routine consular services at the embassy remain strictly suspended due to the regional hostilities.

World.title: Iraqi PM to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is scheduled to arrive in Damascus on Wednesday for an official visit to Syria.

The trip marks the first official visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa took office following the fall of the Assad regime.

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Damascus is part of a broader regional tour. He recently met with Jordan’s King Abdullah II and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan in Amman on Monday and is expected to visit Lebanon as well.

Al-Zaidi and al-Sharaa are expected to discuss mutual security and economic concerns. High-priority items on the agenda include border security, counter-terrorism, energy, and economy.

The two leaders will discuss efforts to enhance coordination for securing the shared Iraq-Syria border, measures for intelligence sharing to combat regional terrorism, and initiatives to foster bilateral cooperation in the oil, energy, and trade sectors.

The meeting comes after al-Zaidi sent an official message through the Iraqi National Intelligence Service to al-Sharaa earlier this year. The message set the stage for normalized bilateral contacts and security assessments between the two countries.

World.title: Dangote, Nigeria’s oil tycoon rewriting Africa’s story
World.content:
Lagos – After going from hawking sweets to his primary schoolmates to becoming Africa’s richest man, Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote now stands on the cusp of what could be the continent’s biggest-ever IPO.

Dangote, whose business empire spans Africa, had initially planned to raise $1.6 billion to help turn his flagship mega-oil refinery into the world’s largest from the initial public offering, which closes on Tuesday.

The tycoon extended the application deadline for what he has called “the people’s IPO” by weeks to extend participation to more Africans, although it had already garnered enough interest to raise “more than three, four times” the target amount.

His initial plan was for 10 million investors to get involved in an offering designed to allow low-income earners in Africa to take part. Shares sold for $4 each.

Part of the proceeds will go towards doubling the capacity of his Lagos-based 700,000-barrel per day refinery — already bigger than any in Europe.

A great-grandson of colonial era Nigeria’s wealthiest businessman, Alhassan Dantata, Dangote exhibited signs of business acumen early in his childhood — buying sweets before peddling them to his schoolmates, when he was just eight years old.

Now at 69, his riches outstrip everyone on the continent, with a worth of $35.7 billion, according to the Bloomberg billionaires index, while Forbes estimates his fortune at $51.3 billion.

His vision for Africa and better grasp of the local markets over decades has helped him gain a competitive edge over foreign multinationals in fields like manufacturing and fossil fuels.

“By 2030, the majority of African countries will be self-sufficient,” he told AFP in Kenya last month when asked about when Africa would no longer need to import fuel.

– ‘Indefatigable, foresighted’ –

As he launched his 700,000 bpd refinery in Kenya worth $16 billion, Dangote declared: “This is Africa coming together to build Africa”.

“We’re breaking ground for a new chapter in Africa’s industrial journey to a brighter future,” Dangote said.

After graduating from Egypt’s Al-Azhar University, Dangote started trading in cement, rice and sugar.

He was later to start producing those commodities, building mega factories and expanding operations into at least 14 African countries.

By 2030, he aims to make the Dangote Group Africa’s first $100-billion company.

Time Magazine listed Dangote as one of the world’s 100 most influential people in 2026.

“He is indefatigable, resilient and foresighted. He is one of the greatest African entrepreneurs of our time,” Nigerian business leader and philanthropist Tony Elumelu was quoted as saying in Time Magazine.

– ‘Factories, not private jets’ –

Giving ordinary Nigerians and Africans a chance to own a stake in what would be the continent’s biggest industrial project, Dangote said the IPO was not just about raising funds: “It’s about getting our own Africans generally to be part and parcel of this refinery.”

Nigerian economist Bismark Rewane called what Dangote has done a “democratisation of the economy”, in a continent marked by stark inequality between the rich and poor.

Besides often keeping a low profile and maintaining an unremarkable wardrobe, Dangote sometimes drives himself, without the long security convoys associated with many Nigerian elites.

Locals have spotted him walking from his office to a mosque for Friday prayers in Lagos.

Despite buying his first private jet at 22, Dangote says he is comfortable travelling commercial flights.

He remarked that it took him 30 minutes to find parking for his plane in the capital Abuja recently, saying he wished the “place was full of factories, not private jets”.

Dangote has lived in the same house for nearly four decades, with no plans to move, and has sold off his holiday homes abroad.

Among his hobbies, he lists business, regularly clocking in 18-hour days.

– Philanthropy and football –

The tycoon, who said he has committed a third of his wealth to his Dangote Foundation, has also taken to giving back to society.

His foundation has spent millions of dollars on education, healthcare and disaster relief, helping victims of the last Ebola outbreak in west Africa and building a Covid isolation centre during the pandemic.

In 2012, he teamed up with the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to help eradicate polio in Nigeria.

He wants his legacy to be the one who “pioneered… the industrialisation of Africa”, he told Nicolai Tangen, the head of Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, in a podcast earlier this year.

Like many Nigerians, Dangote is an avowed football fan and had considered buying a stake in Arsenal, whichwould have made him the first African owner of an English Premier League club.

But given the competing demands on his time, he decided that “it’s better… to remain as a fan and continue to fund my own business.”

World.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash: reports
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday.

Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win.

Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone.

But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session.

The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim.

The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League.

World.title: Baghdad court sentences seven French ISIS operatives to life and 15 years
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad’s Karkh Criminal Court sentenced seven French nationals on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to life imprisonment and a 15-year prison term after convicting them of membership in the ISIS terrorist organization, in a hearing attended by their defense counsel and representatives from the French Embassy in Iraq.

According to a formal statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council’s media office, the court handed down life sentences to six convicts, while the seventh received a 15-year custodial sentence under federal anti-terrorism statutes.

Judicial authorities classified the individuals as highly dangerous elements, citing their role in threatening Iraqi national security, destabilizing border areas across Iraq and Syria, and inciting terrorist attacks in other countries.

The judicial authority confirmed that the seven convicts were part of a wider contingent of 47 French nationals transferred into Iraqi custody last year from detention camps across northeastern Syria.

Following their repatriation to Baghdad, the First Karkh Investigation Court led preliminary interrogations and evidence processing before referring the defendants to the competent criminal court for trial under Iraqi statutory procedures.

World.title: Iraq’s dollar reserves rebound to $80 billion as cash inflows continue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves rebounded to approximately $80 billion across September and October, recovering from a recent low of $73 billion.

The monetary authority offered assurances to the public regarding the ample availability of physical greenbacks, confirming that scheduled cash shipments from the United States are proceeding as planned.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Mahmoud Dagher, adviser to the CBI Governor and official spokesperson for the central bank, detailed that the aggregate dollar reserves—held across CBI accounts and federal government repositories at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York—gained significant ground, while sovereign gold reserves held firm at 170 metric tons.

Dagher attributed the reserve replenishment to recent monthly oil export revenues reaching near $6 billion, describing the inflow as acceptable given current regional market pressures. He noted that reserve health is measured by import coverage rather than absolute figures. When oil shipments faced disruptions earlier this year between April and June, Iraq’s reserve buffer contracted from 12 months of import cover to roughly nine months, before recovering back toward prior benchmarks. Dagher emphasized that the Ministry of Finance must accelerate structural diversification to reduce sovereign dependency on central bank foreign assets for operational budget financing.

Addressing physical liquidity, Dagher confirmed that Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is personally monitoring incoming cash flights, with each air consignment carrying roughly $500 million. Two cargo aircraft loaded with physical banknotes have already arrived in Baghdad, with additional shipments slated to land in the coming days. The surplus of cash liquidity enabled the central bank to raise individual traveler allowances from two quotas up to six quotas per year. However, Dagher noted that the pace of upcoming cash consignments remains tethered to regional security stability, as armed flare-ups or active conflict could complicate cargo transport logistics and transit insurance.

On the placement of Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves, Dagher affirmed that maintaining primary sovereign holdings with the U.S. Federal Reserve is governed by financial logic, technical prudence, and sovereign asset protection rather than political preferences. He explained that pending foreign legal claims against Iraqi state banks continue to restrict custodial options, making Federal Reserve custody vital for legal immunity. While Iraq maintains diversified secondary reserves across Switzerland (Basel), European centers, the United Arab Emirates, and China, the Federal Reserve remains the anchor repository safeguarding Iraqi sovereign wealth.

World.title: PM Modi urges Indian scientists to lead in future technologies and make country a global hub for solutions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India must embrace the future technologies, innovate boldly and lead the world in developing them, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said while addressing the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave here on Tuesday.

Asserting that a âViksit Bharatâ (developed India) will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation, he appealed to every researcher, industry leader, startup founder and student to set a concrete three-year target identifying which technology, prototype, pilot project or product they will help develop to make India a global hub for solutions.

Underlining how scientific judgement will evolve in the age of AI during the second quarter of the 21st century, the Prime Minister emphasised that while AI can rapidly execute routine tasks to boost productivity, it must enrich rather than restrict independent thinking, allowing researchers to use saved time for harder problems, new experiments, and idea validation.

âAI can give us answers quickly, but the responsibility of testing the veracity of the answer must lie with the scientist alone,â he asserted. The three-day Conclave brought together leading scientists, policymakers and global experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and innovation priorities.

Referring to emerging AI-era cybersecurity threats to financial networks and national security, Modi called for developing AI-based and quantum security solutions that protect national systems and serve humanity.





âOur goal is to develop such technologies which empower India and also contribute to solving the problems of humanity,â he said.

Invoking the collective spirit and conviction of âwe will do itâ, the Prime Minister said the country has to prepare such a generation which is not merely a participant in emerging science and technology, but leads it. âOur goal is also to expand our power in critical technologies,â he asserted.

World.title: Act to improve last-mile broadband connectivity, COAI to govt
World.content:
NEW DELHI: To improve last-mile connectivity in Indiaâs broadband sector, the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) has urged govt to expeditiously notify the rule amendments enabling standard power operations in the delicensed lower 6 GHz band.

An expert committee constituted by dept of telecom, that was led by IIT Madrasâs Professor Radha Krishna Ganti had recommended enabling higher-power outdoor use at 36 dBm in the 5925â6425 MHz band. The industry has asked the telecom ministry to implement the same âwithout further delayâ.

COAI DG Lt Gen (retired) S P Kochhar said: âIndia's broadband sector has progressed significantly, yet last-mile connectivity gaps persist particularly in rural, semi-urban, and difficult-to-reach areas due to Right-of-Way (RoW) challenges, limited fibre availability and high deployment costs.

The expert committee's recommendation to permit Standard Power (36 dBm) outdoor use of the lower 6 GHz delicensed band (5925â6425 MHz) remains a practical and cost-effective solution to this challenge â one that is yet to be operationalised through the necessary regulatory notification.

â

âFixed wireless access (FWA) and point-to-multi-point (P2MP) deployments at standard power are suited for last-mile broadband delivery where fibre penetration is absent, economically unviable or physically impractical.





Enabling outdoor Standard Power operations ensures this 500 MHz of valuable delicensed spectrum is fully harnessed in service of national objectives and can be utilised by all service providers,â Kochhar said.

COAI says once implemented, this move will not only expand broadband coverage but also substantially improve broadband utilisation, bringing high-quality, high-speed connectivity to homes, enterprises and institutions âthat have long remained on the wrong side of the digital divide.â

âEnabling these operations will ensure that India's delicensed spectrum serves not just indoor enterprise and consumer Wi-Fi but becomes a genuine engine of rural broadband penetration and digital inclusion. Several months since the Expert Committee submitted its report, COAI earnestly requests the DoT to expedite the notification of the necessary rule amendments enabling Standard Power (36 dBm) outdoor operations in the lower 6 GHz band (5925-6425 MHz) for P2MP/P2P, so as to enable licensed and authorised entities to deploy these capabilities and bring the transformative benefits of high-quality, affordable broadband to every segment of our society,â he added.

World.title: Days after Rubio's visit, Centre says 'under no pressure' to stop buying Russian oil
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union petroleum minister

on Tuesday said that India was not under any pressure to stop buying Russian oil.

During an interaction at the 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet, Puri said Indian refiners would purchase crude from suppliers offering the most competitive prices as the country prioritises energy security amid global market uncertainties.

"I have never felt any pressure," Puri said during the interaction at the 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet, which began here on Tuesday.

"India was not particularly buying Russian oil at present, but the decisions in this regard were guided by commercial considerations rather than pressure from any country," he added.

"At the point of negotiation, whoever is supplying a particular grade, we will buy from them.

Prices come down sometimes," he further said.

Puri also said India had diversified its energy investments and sourcing, adding that New Delhi's approach was guided by the need to ensure reliable supplies while managing costs for consumers and the broader economy.

"India had diversified its energy investments and sourcing," the minister said.

"India, as a major energy-consuming nation, could not compromise on its energy security amid geopolitical developments and volatility in international markets," he added.





Puri's remarks come days after US secretary of state Marco Rubio visited India against the backdrop of USâ Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act meant to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil and Trumpâs subsequent suspension temporarily of related tariffs.

Rubio said New Delhi had repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, describing it as a sensible strategy.

âIn the end, itâs not just about Russian oil; itâs about their desire to diversify,â he said, adding US was keen to be a source of energy supplies for India.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Imran Khan gets temporary relief as 'leave India' notice put on hold; Karnataka loses nearly 1cr voters after SIR & more
World.content:
Imran Khan gets relief as the Bombay HC extended the deadline to leave India until November 2, when it will hear his challenge to an FRRO notice directing his deportation over an alleged protest-related offence.

Karnataka's final electoral roll recorded 4.54 crore voters after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), marking a reduction of nearly one crore from the original electorate, with 65.45 lakh voters classified as permanently shifted.

Kiren Rijiju demanded an apology from the Congress after the Indian Army debunked an AI-generated video falsely attributing remarks about Chinese control of Arunachal Pradesh territories to an Army officer.

Israel voted in a crucial parliamentary election amid reports of missing and defaced ballot slips, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a major leadership test.

Abhishek Sharma and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a world record for the highest scoring rate in a 100-plus opening partnership in men's T20 internationals, powering India to a six-wicket win over New Zealand.

Here are your top stories of the day

Imran Khan gets relief as Bombay HC to hear 'leave India' plea on November 2

Karnataka loses nearly one crore voters after SIR

Kiren Rijiju targets Congress after Army debunks AI video on China

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Israel election: Ballot tampering claims, record turnout and Netanyahu's leadership test

Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set world record as India beat New Zealand

The Bombay High Court extended actor Imran Khan's deadline to leave India until November 2 and scheduled a hearing on his challenge to an FRRO notice directing him to leave the country. Khan, who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, has argued that the notice violates his constitutional rights and was issued without giving him an opportunity to respond. The notice followed an FIR linked to an alleged protest in Mumbai on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Karnataka's final electoral roll recorded 4,54,55,689 voters after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), down from the original electorate of around 5.5 crore. Of the voters removed during the exercise, 65.45 lakh were classified as permanently shifted. The final list includes 6.83 lakh new voters, while 61,867 people were excluded following the notices phase. The state has around four lakh more female voters than male voters.Union minister Kiren Rijiju demanded an apology from the Congress after the Indian Army debunked an AI-generated video falsely attributing remarks about Chinese control of areas in Arunachal Pradesh to Lieutenant General Girish Kalia.The Army said the video had been digitally altered and that the original footage was from a 2023 press briefing in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, concerning infiltration attempts along the Line of Control. It clarified that the officer had made no remarks about Chinese control of Arunachal Pradesh or the denial of supplies to Indian troops.Israelis voted in a crucial parliamentary election as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced a challenge from rival political blocs seeking to unseat him. Reports of missing, damaged and defaced ballot slips prompted the Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, to file a complaint with the Central Elections Committee. Turnout reached 31.5% by noon, the highest recorded at that hour since 1973, according to The Times of Israel. Arab-led parties could play a decisive role in government formation if neither major political bloc secures a majority.Abhishek Sharma and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a world record for the highest scoring rate in a 100-plus opening partnership in men's T20 internationals, scoring at 18.13 runs per over against New Zealand in Wellington. Abhishek smashed 113 off 38 balls, while Sooryavanshi contributed 45 off 18 deliveries as the pair added 133 runs in seven overs. Their explosive start helped India chase down 199 in 13.2 overs, securing a six-wicket victory and completing a 3-0 series sweep.

World.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro headed to U.S. after losing election, sources say
World.content:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing ​Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over ‌his passports, two sources said.

The U.S. Embassy in Brazil did not immediately ​respond to a request for comment. Flavio Bolsonaro’s lawyer also did not ⁠respond. It was not immediately clear where Flavio Bolsonaro was heading, what time he would arrive or whether he would seek asylum.

U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration has previously alleged that Flavio Bolsonaro’s father, former President ‌Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.

Mr. Flavio’s departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most ‌populous nations in the Americas. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has ‌accused ⁠Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, ⁠and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) election on a U.S. State Department campaign to restore them to office.

Mr. Flavio was favoured to win Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result to ​leftist Lula. On Monday (October 26, 2026), he was given ‌24 hours to hand in his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing, but that deadline has now lapsed, two other sources said, leading to his documents being canceled.

A final surge: On Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph in Brazil

It was unclear if he ‌could seek entry to the United States with his passports canceled.

Jair Bolsonaro also ​went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former U.S. President Joe Biden was in office. ⁠He eventually returned to Brazil but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

His son has yet to officially ‌concede defeat — saying on Sunday (October 25, 2026) he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities — but his Liberal Party said on Monday (October 26, 2026) it acknowledged Mr. Lula’s victory.

It remains unclear how Mr. Flavios was able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour Supreme Court deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Brazilian Federal Police official said Jair had not exited the country via any regular migration point.

Right-wing ‌influencer Paulo Figueiredo, who serves as a sort of unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined to answer ​questions about Mr. Flavio’s whereabouts.

“After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to ⁠the press,” he said in a message. “If I have any comments to make on any ⁠matter, I will get in touch.”

Eduardo Bolsonaro, Mr. Flavio’s younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election ‌loss would require a move.

“If my brother does not win, I’m in favour that he would leave the country,” he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

World.title: A Delhi event unveils fault lines in the Dalit-OBC formulation of SP politics
World.content:
In the high-stakes arena of Uttar Pradesh elections, the line between social representation and competitive polarisation is razor-thin. Samajwadi Party (SP) spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati discovered it last week when he faced trolls from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and a reprimand from the party’s top leadership after participating in a Buddhist Dhamma Diksha ceremony in Delhi.

During the annual ceremony, Mr. Bhati, a prominent OBC leader of SP in western U.P., participated in the mass recitation of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s 22 vows. The viral video recorded him explicitly repeating the controversial opening segments of the pledge, which include the statements: “I will not consider Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh as gods, nor will I worship them. I will not consider Rama and Krishna as gods, nor will I worship them.” He was also filmed repeating the vow to refuse any religious rituals performed by Brahmin priests.

The 22 vows, which Ambedkar took with his followers on October 14, 1956, stem from his formulation of Navayana Buddhism. He did not want his followers to transition from one ritualistic or superstitious framework to another. He observed that historically, whenever reform movements emerged within India, they were eventually absorbed back into the dominant Hindu fold as mere sub-sects. He drafted the vows as an explicit checklist to guarantee a complete, irreversible psychological break from the Hindu social order.

A Gurjar by birth, Mr. Bhati organised a massive rally for party president Akhilesh Yadav in March this year. His Dalit push seemed in line with the party’s Lohiate policy of numerical aggregation, uniting everyone outside the so-called upper-caste hegemony to capture state power. Ram Manohar Lohia’s “Socialisto ne bandhi ganth, pichhde paavein sau mein saat”, referring to roughly 40% OBC and 20% SC vote in the State, still echoes in the air. He also put forward the idea of roti-beti for intermingling of castes. SP founder Mulayam Singh Yadav put the slogan into action by joining hands with Bahujan Samaj Party founder Kanshi Ram in 1993, captured by the popular slogan, ‘Mile Mulayam-Kanshi Ram, hawa mein ud gaye Jai Shri Ram’ – but the caste barriers remained. Now Mr. Akhilesh seeks to revive Lohia’s logic through his comprehensive PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formula.

Ambedkar’s 22 vows

However, his uncles, Ram Gopal Yadav and Shivpal Yadav, reacted to Mr. Bhati’s overtures, reviving Ambedkar’s fears about numerical aggregation. While Mr. Ram Gopal threatened to strip Mr. Bhati of his post in the party, Mr. Shivpal said, “Hum Ishwarwadi hain.” Political observers feel the Yadav leadership can’t separate its cultural ties to Lord Krishna. A Shiva temple has come up in the Yadav stronghold of Saifai, whose trust is headed by Mr. Akhilesh.

Right-wing elements reminded the SP of their party president’s recent statement that P in PDA also stood for Pandit. Facing an FIR, Mr. Bhati clarified that he repeated the words out of respect for the organisers and Ambedkar, without intending to change his religion. But he also underlined that Ambedkarites would understand the spirit of his stance and respond to his right-wing trolls.

Dalit intellectuals emphasise Ambedkar consistently argued that the Hindu caste structure is not a simple binary of oppressors and oppressed, but a system of graded inequality. Shudras/OBCs, while socially backward compared to upper castes, historically sit higher in the rural socio-economic hierarchy than Dalits.

The Bhati episode mirrors previous political flashpoints, demonstrating that while mainstream parties actively engage in competitive adulation of Ambedkar, their leadership quickly distances itself the moment a politician explicitly recites the radical, anti-scriptural elements of his 22 vows.

In 2022, Rajendra Pal Gautam, a prominent Dalit leader and senior Minister in Arvind Kejriwal’s Delhi Cabinet, took the same vows at the same event and faced similar pressure from the BJP and its parivar ahead of Gujarat polls. Mr. Kejriwal, who was indulging in competitive communalism at the time, succumbed to pressure. Mr. Gautam resigned and subsequently joined the Congress in 2024. Today, he is the All India Congress Committee in-charge for U.P. and is seen as the central leadership’s eyes and ears.

Whether Mr. Bhati is on a similar trajectory and sees a space in an idea-rich, cadre-thin Congress if SP gives in, only time will tell. Rumblings in the INDIA bloc suggest the SP leadership wants Congress to bring in a share of the mature Dalit vote. When Ajay Rai was replaced and the State Congress presidency was split between Mona Misra and Imran Masood, a senior SP insider told this journalist that if the Congress really wants to turn the clock back, instead of focusing on Brahmins and Muslims, it should try to win back 40-plus Dalit voters from Mayawati’s hold. “The rest we will manage,” he said. This is the voter Mr. Bhati was addressing.

Meanwhile, the BJP is finding itself in a bind over allegedly providing cover to its ‘nationalist’ Dalit leader Dushyant Gautam in the Ankita Bhandari case by making him a Governor. Framing it as beti vs Dalit vote narrative, a section of social media influencers who post in favour of the ruling dispensation accuse the BJP of appeasing a Dalit leader without a considerable mass base, which would hurt the party in U.P.

For now, Mr. Akhilesh, who has often cited an incident where a temple was cleaned with ‘Ganga jal’ after his visit, hasn’t taken a stance on Mr. Bhati’s vows. Political observers feel the BJP seeks to appropriate Ambedkar the same way Brahminical scholars appropriated Gautam Buddha as part of the Hindu pantheon, but the Hindutva ecosystem doesn’t want to extend reservation benefits to those who openly negate the presence of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh, and herein the Opposition sees a vote bank.

World.title: Jain seer gives Karnataka govt. 10-day deadline to meet demands; threatens sallekhana in December if demands remain unmet
World.content:
Acharya Gunadharanandi Maharaj of Varur Navagraha Teertha Kshetra has given the State government 10 days to provide written assurances on five demands of the Jain community, including the establishment of a Jain Development Corporation.

He warned that he would intensify an agitation in stages and undertake sallekhana (a Jain religious vow involving voluntary fasting unto death) in December if the demands were not met.

Addressing a press conference in Hubballi on Tuesday, he said the government had failed to take decisive action despite repeated representations over the past three years. He said he could no longer remain a silent spectator to what he described as injustice to the Jain community.

The jain monk said the agitation would begin if the government failed to provide a clear written assurance within 10 days. A march and satyagraha would be organised in November, and he would consider undertaking sallekhana in December if the government continued to remain unresponsive.

The five demands include setting up an independent Jain Development Corporation or board; introducing a special security mechanism for the safe movement of Jain monks and nuns; framing regulations to protect Jain pilgrimage centres, temples and historic religious institutions; providing annual free pilgrimage to Shri Sammed Shikharji for economically weaker Jain devotees; and establishing government rest houses or temporary night shelters along the routes used by monks and nuns.

He urged the government to convene a high-level meeting and constitute a joint committee comprising community representatives and officials from the departments concerned. The government should also provide a written response within 10 days, specifying the status of each demand, the department responsible and a timeline for implementation, he said.

If the government failed to respond positively, the first phase of the agitation would involve foot marches to the residences of MLAs in Jamkhandi, Teradal, Kagwad, Athani, Chikkodi, Nipani, Hukkeri and Belagavi to submit memoranda. This would be followed by a large-scale foot march from Chikkodi to Belagavi and a satyagraha, he said.

The agitation would remain entirely non-violent and would not target any political party, he said, appealing to legislators across party lines to support the community’s demands.

The acharya said the demands concerned the development of the Jain community, the safety of monks and nuns, and the protection of its religious heritage. The government should move beyond assurances and provide a written commitment with a clear implementation schedule, he added.

World.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: Flights, trains cancelled as rain batters A.P.; 30,000 boats brought ashore; southern Odisha on edge
World.content:
Heavy rain pounded the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), leaving one dead and a trail of destruction, while southern Odisha remained on edge as the ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ Arnab moved closer to the coast.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm is likely to make landfall early — around 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28) – near the Yanam-Kakinada region in Andhra Pradesh. Initially, the IMD had said that the landfall would take place around forenoon on Wednesday.

Keep track | Cyclone ‘Arnab’ LIVE updates | Storm 140 km from Kakinada; highest danger signal hoisted at Kakinada port

According to real-time information from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), Jathara premises in Visakhapatnam rural mandal recorded Tuesday’s (October 27) highest rainfall of 141.75 mm between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. Visakhapatnam district, where many places experienced rainfall above 100 mm and strong winds, bore the brunt of the cyclone. At least 200 trees were uprooted within the city limits.

A 65-year-old man died at Mangalapalem after he came into contact with live electrical wires that had snapped and fallen into water. The districts of Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, and Srikakulam also recorded widespread rainfall of above 80 mm until 7 p.m. on Tuesday.

As per the latest information from the IMD, the storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal is moving at a speed higher than expected. As of 5.30 p.m., it was located around 90 km southeast of Kakinada, 170 km south of Visakhapatnam, 170 km east of Machilipatnam, 240 km east-northeast of Bapatla, and 380 km south-southwest of Gopalpur in Odisha.

IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Nagaratnam, who is monitoring the cyclone situation along with her team from Vijayawada, said the rainfall activity, which is centred around northern districts in the morning, would shift to the districts of Kakinada, West and East Godavari, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema by Tuesday night, when the system moves northwestwards towards Yanam.

21 flights cancelled

Due to the increasing severity of the storm on Tuesday (October 27), airlines cancelled at least 21 flights in Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam. At the Vijayawada airport, five flights bound for Hyderabad, Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam, and Kadapa were cancelled on Tuesday (October 27). The Vijayawada airport authorities have cancelled all flights on Wednesday as well.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said 290 cyclone shelters had been set up and 84,396 people evacuated to safer locations. More than 30,000 fishing boats had been brought back from the sea, while 93 Andhra Pradesh boats and their crew were reported safe at Gopalpur in Odisha.

The State has mobilised 8,400 personnel to respond to electricity disruptions and is prepared for the possible collapse of up to 15,000 power poles. Teams from the National and State Disaster Response Force, the Navy and the Coast Guard had also been alerted.

Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) Managing Director Prakhar Jain have advised the public to be alert, as extremely heavy rain is expected on Tuesday night in the districts of Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, and Anakapalli. In cases of emergency, one can dial toll-free helplines 1070, 112, or 18004250101.

Odisha on high alert

With cyclone Arnab moving closer to the A.P. coast, thousands of people living in adjoining hilly southern districts of Odisha are bracing for heavy rain and strong gales.

The Odisha government has begun evacuation of over 48,000 people from vulnerable southern districts, sources in the government said. Owing to the prospect of landslips, the government has shut several ghat roads.

The East Coast Railway said 22 express and passenger train services connecting Visakhapatnam, Secunderabad, Kirandul, Jagdalpur, Rourkela, Sambalpur, Rayagada, Howrah, Bhubaneswar and Koraput would remain cancelled or regulated on different dates between October 27 and November 5, 2026. Similarly, private bus operators have also placed restrictions on movement of their buses to southern Odisha.

Manorama Mohanty, Director of IMD, Bhubaneswar, said southern districts such as Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Gajapati, Koraput, and Rayagada could experience wind speeds between 50 and 60 km per hour gusting to 70 kmph.

Thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty surface wind is likely to occur at one or two places over the districts of Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, Ganjam on Wednesday, said the IMD.

“We plan to shift 48,000 people from vulnerable places to safer place in the first phase in eight districts. In Nabarangpur and Gajapati district, 11,000 each will be evacuated. In Malkangiri, 9,850 people have been identified for shifting. About 6,500 in Ganjam and 5,000 in Koraput will take shelter in identified locations,” said Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil.

As many as 48 units of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, eight National Disaster Response Force teams, and 225 fire services teams have been deployed.

World.title: Radhatri Nethralaya conducts workshop on first aid for firecracker-related eye injuries
World.content:
Radhatri Nethralaya conducted its 14th annual workshop on first aid for firecracker-related eye injuries at its T. Nagar branch on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). The workshop was attended by 65 students and 30 teachers from 20 schools in Chennai.

A press release said Medical Director Vasumathy Vedantham led the hands-on session, during which students enacted various scenarios involving firecracker-related eye injuries and learned first-aid measures.

The participants received certificates, first-aid kits, and pamphlets to distribute in their respective schools, the release added. Philanthropist and entrepreneur Subash Chand Ranka was the chief guest. Praveen Krishna, medical director, Radhatri Nethralaya, said thousands of students had benefited from the workshop over the past 14 years.

World.title: Cyclone Arnab causes high waves in north Chennai, Tiruvallur
World.content:
Traffic on Ennore Expressway and other coastal roads in north Chennai and Tiruvallur district witnessed high waves lashing onto the land as a result of cyclone Arnab on Tuesday evening (October 27, 2026). Residents of Kasikoilkuppam, Ennore, Tiruvottiyur, Bharathi Nagar and Ramakrishna Nagar came out of their homes in panic, seeing the storm surge. Tiruvottiyur MLA N. Senthil Kumar, who visited the spot, said that there was no need for the public to panic.

Mahalingam of Kasikoilkuppam said that water had entered their village. It is a scary situation, he added. The National Highways Authority of India closed the expressway to traffic after vehicles were drenched in the waves. Smaller vehicles were pushed due to the force of the waves. Some fishermen thought the waves could be a due to a tsunami and wanted to find if there was any earthquake.

Ennore: Massive wave crashes onto road, hits passengers and shops

Ennore traffic police have diverted vehicles along two routes. Vehicles from Ramakrishna Nagar to Annai Sivagami Nagar are being diverted via Ernavur Bridge, Murugar Kovil Road and Kathivakkam Beach. Vehicles from Thazhakuppam and Ennore are being diverted via Kathivakkam Bridge and Murugar Kovil road, police said.

In Tiruvallur district, the Collector S. Kavitha has pressed the police, fire services and the revenue department to ensure the safety of the public living along the coast. The Regional Meteorological Centre here had warned of rough seas due to the cyclone. The sea is expected to calm down by noon on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

World.title: Cyclone Arnab leaves parts of Visakhapatnam in darkness
World.content:
Prolonged power interruptions following ‘Cyclone Arnab’ have caused considerable hardship to residents in several parts of Visakhapatnam, with people in Kancharapalem and Akkayyapalem reporting outages lasting several hours.

According to complaints by residents of Kancharapalem, they said: “Electricity supply was disrupted since 5 a.m. on October 27, leaving several neighbourhoods, including Kapparada, Babuji Nagar, Indira Nagar, Sanjeevayya Colony and adjoining hill-slope settlements, without power for nearly 18 hours.”

The prolonged outage added to the anxiety of people living in vulnerable hillside areas amid the cyclone threat. The absence of electricity affected routine activities, with elderly persons, children and other residents facing difficulties.

Residents alleged that repeated attempts to contact the electricity department had failed to elicit a response. They also complained that the toll-free helpline and local electricity office telephone numbers were not functioning effectively, leaving them uncertain about when the power supply would be restored.

Similar complaints emerged from Akkayyapalem, Madhurawada and a few other localities, where residents reported power outages for several hours on Tuesday. They alleged that complaints had not resulted in prompt action and appealed to officials to expedite restoration work.

The outages have also raised questions among residents about the resilience of the city’s power distribution network during extreme weather events. Residents sought clarity on the proposed underground cabling works, reportedly estimated at ₹800 crore, and the extent to which such infrastructure had been implemented in the affected localities.

Officials pointed out that cyclone-related damage to electrical lines, poles and distribution equipment can complicate restoration works, particularly when strong winds and heavy rainfall hamper field operations. However, the precise causes of the reported outages and the status of restoration in the affected neighbourhoods could not be independently confirmed.

Residents urged the electricity authorities to deploy adequate field staff, improve grievance-response mechanisms and restore supply at the earliest. They also called for transparent communication on repair timelines to help households cope with the continuing disruption.

When contacted, an EPDCL official said, “Most of our focus including that of the higher officials and the CMD is on Konaseema and Kakinada districts, where the cyclone has a stronger impact. Power supply will be restored soon.”

World.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ LIVE updates | Storm 140 km from Kakinada; highest danger signal hoisted at Kakinada port
World.content:
Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ was about 140 km from Kakinada and 170 km from Visakhapatnam at 2.30 p.m. on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. It is expected to cross the coast just south of Yanam by Wednesday forenoon, with winds of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph. A storm surge of 1 to 2 metres could flood low-lying areas near Kakinada and Yanam.

Also read | Cyclone ‘Arnab’ Highlights on October 26, 2026

Nearly 89,000 people on the Kakinada coast are being moved to 101 relief camps, and Odisha plans to move 48,000 people. Sea water has flooded parts of Uppada near Kakinada, and all beaches in Visakhapatnam are closed. At least 72 trains have been cancelled, and several flights at the Visakhapatnam airport have been cancelled or diverted.

Also read | Very severe cyclone ‘Arnab’ to make landfall near Yanam-Kakinada; red alert issued for seven districts

Visakhapatnam city has had over 100 mm of rain at several places since morning. Heavy rain is also forecast for parts of Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, and Nepal is on high alert from October 29 to 31. Follow our Live updates.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs3.19 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.25
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.19 per litre and increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.25.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs376.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs398.07 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 28 (Wednesday).

Earlier today, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy.

The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17.

For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then.

On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions.
